verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, as his fathers had done. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 15:10
verses.text: And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him. And he struck him before the people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:11
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Zachariah, behold, they <hi>are</hi> written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 15:12
verses.text: This <hi>was</hi> the word of the LORD which He spoke to Jehu, saying, Your sons shall sit on the throne of Israel until the fourth <hi>generation</hi>. And it was so.

verses.name: II Kings 15:13
verses.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah. And he reigned in Samaria a full month.

verses.name: II Kings 15:14
verses.text: For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria and struck Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria. And he killed him and reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:15
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy which he made, behold, they <hi>are</hi> written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 15:16
verses.text: Then Menahem struck Tiphsah, and all in it, and its borders, from Tirzah. Because they did not open, he struck it. He ripped up all its pregnant women.

verses.name: II Kings 15:17
verses.text: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi began to reign over Israel, ten years in Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 15:18
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, all his days.

verses.name: II Kings 15:19
verses.text: Pul, the king of Assyria came against the land. And Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

verses.name: II Kings 15:20
verses.text: And Menahem took the silver from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth (fifty shekels of silver from each man) to give to the king of Assyria. And the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.

verses.name: II Kings 15:21
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 15:22
verses.text: And Menahem slept with his fathers. And Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:23
verses.text: In the fiftieth year of Uzziah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, two years.

verses.name: II Kings 15:24
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 15:25
verses.text: But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a commander of his, conspired against him and struck him in Samaria, in the palace of the king's house, with Argob and Arieh, and fifty men of the Gileadites with him. And he killed him and reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 15:26
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they <hi>are</hi> written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 15:27
verses.text: In the fifty-second year of Uzziah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, twenty years.

verses.name: II Kings 15:28
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

verses.name: II Kings 15:29
verses.text: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he deported them Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 15:30
verses.text: And Hoshea the son of Elah made a plot against Pekah the son of Remaliah. And he struck him and killed him and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.

verses.name: II Kings 15:31
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they <hi>are</hi> written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Israel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 15:32
verses.text: In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 15:33
verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.

verses.name: II Kings 15:34
verses.text: And he did right in the sight of the LORD. He did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.

verses.name: II Kings 15:35
verses.text: Only, the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 15:36
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 15:37
verses.text: In those days the LORD began to send Rezin the king of Syria against Judah, and also Pekah the son of Remaliah.

verses.name: II Kings 15:38
verses.text: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. And his son Ahaz reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:1
verses.text: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 16:2
verses.text: Ahaz <hi>was</hi> twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do right in the sight of the LORD his God, like David his father.

verses.name: II Kings 16:3
verses.text: But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel. Yes, and he made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD cast out from before the sons of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 16:4
verses.text: And he sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:5
verses.text: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem for war. And they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome <hi>him</hi>.

verses.name: II Kings 16:6
verses.text: At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drove the Jews from Elath. And the Syrians came to Elath and lived there until this day.

verses.name: II Kings 16:7
verses.text: And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, I <hi>am</hi> your servant and your son. Come up and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who rise up against me.

verses.name: II Kings 16:8
verses.text: And Ahaz took the silver and gold which was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasures of the king's house, and sent a present to the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 16:9
verses.text: And the king of Assyria listened to him, for the king of Assyria went up against Damascus and took it. And he carried it away captive to Kir, and killed Rezin.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:10
verses.text: And king Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria <hi>at</hi> Damascus. And <hi>he</hi> saw an altar at Damascus. And king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the pattern of the altar, and the form of it, according to all its work.

verses.name: II Kings 16:11
verses.text: And Urijah the priest built an altar according to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus. So Urijah the priest did until king Ahaz came in from Damascus.

verses.name: II Kings 16:12
verses.text: And the king came in from Damascus, and the king saw the altar. And the king approached to the altar and offered on it.

verses.name: II Kings 16:13
verses.text: And he offered his burnt offering and his food offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings, on the altar.

verses.name: II Kings 16:14
verses.text: And he also brought the bronze altar which <hi>was</hi> before the LORD, from the forefront of the house, from between the altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of the altar.

verses.name: II Kings 16:15
verses.text: And king Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, On the great altar burn the morning offering and the evening food offering, and the king's burnt sacrifice and his food offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their food offerings, and their drink offerings. And sprinkle all the blood of the burnt offerings on it, and all the blood of the sacrifice. And the bronze altar shall be for me to inquire by.

verses.name: II Kings 16:16
verses.text: And Urijah the priest did according to all that king Ahaz commanded.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 16:17
verses.text: And king Ahaz cut off the borders of the bases, and removed the laver from them. And he took down the sea from off the bronze oxen under it, and put it on a pavement of stones.

verses.name: II Kings 16:18
verses.text: And the covered way for the sabbath which they had built in the house, and the king's entry outside, he turned from the house of the LORD for the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 16:19
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 16:20
verses.text: And Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:1
verses.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, nine years.

verses.name: II Kings 17:2
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him.

verses.name: II Kings 17:3
verses.text: Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him. And Hoshea became his servant and gave him taxes.

verses.name: II Kings 17:4
verses.text: And the king of Assyria found treachery in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and had brought no taxes to the king of Assyria, as before, year by year. And the king of Assyria shut him up and bound him in prison.

verses.name: II Kings 17:5
verses.text: And the king of Assyria went up into all the land. And he went up to Samaria and besieged it three years.

verses.name: II Kings 17:6
verses.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria. And he placed them in Halah, and in Habor <hi>by</hi> the river Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:7
verses.text: And it happened because the sons of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,

verses.name: II Kings 17:8
verses.text: and walked in the statutes of the nations whom the LORD cast out from before the sons of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which the nations had made.

verses.name: II Kings 17:9
verses.text: And the sons of Israel secretly did things that <hi>were</hi> not right against the LORD their God. And they built high places in all their cities for themselves, from the Watch Tower to the fortified city.

verses.name: II Kings 17:10
verses.text: And they set up images and Asherahs for themselves in every high hill, and under every green tree.

verses.name: II Kings 17:11
verses.text: And they burned incense in all the high places, like the nations whom the LORD had removed from before them; and did evil things to provoke the LORD to anger.

verses.name: II Kings 17:12
verses.text: For they served the idols, of which the LORD had said to them, You shall not do this thing.

verses.name: II Kings 17:13
verses.text: And the LORD testified against Israel, and against Judah, by all the prophets, <hi>by</hi> all the seers, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by My servants the prophets.

verses.name: II Kings 17:14
verses.text: But they would not hear, but hardened their necks, like the neck of their fathers who did not believe in the LORD their God.

verses.name: II Kings 17:15
verses.text: And <hi>they</hi> rejected His statutes and His covenant which He made with their fathers, and His testimonies which He testified against them. And they went after the vain thing, and became vain, and after the nations around them, concerning whom the LORD had charged them not to do like them.

verses.name: II Kings 17:16
verses.text: And they left all the commandments of the LORD their God, and made molten images, two calves, for themselves. And they made an Asherah and worshiped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.

verses.name: II Kings 17:17
verses.text: And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire. And they used divination and incantations, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.

verses.name: II Kings 17:18
verses.text: So the LORD was very angry with Israel, and turned them away from His face; not one was left, only the tribe of Judah by itself.

verses.name: II Kings 17:19
verses.text: Also Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the statutes which Israel made.

verses.name: II Kings 17:20
verses.text: And the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until He had cast them out of His sight.

verses.name: II Kings 17:21
verses.text: For He tore Israel from the house of David. And they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king. And Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD, and made them sin a great sin.

verses.name: II Kings 17:22
verses.text: For the sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did. They did not depart from them

verses.name: II Kings 17:23
verses.text: until the LORD turned away Israel from His face, as He had said by all His servants the prophets. So Israel was carried away out of their own land to Assyria until this day.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 17:24
verses.text: And the king of Assyria brought <hi>men</hi> from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed <hi>them</hi> in the cities of Samaria instead of the sons of Israel. And they possessed Samaria and lived in its cities.

verses.name: II Kings 17:25
verses.text: And it happened at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear the LORD. And the LORD sent lions among them, who killed them.

verses.name: II Kings 17:26
verses.text: And they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations which you have removed and placed in the cities of Samaria do not know the manner of the God of the land. And He has sent lions among them, and, behold, they kill them because they do not know the way of the God of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 17:27
verses.text: And the king of Assyria commanded, saying, Cause one of the priests whom you removed from there to go there. And they shall go and live there, and he shall teach them the way of the God of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 17:28
verses.text: And one of the priests whom they had removed from Samaria came and lived in Bethel. And he taught them how they should fear the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 17:29
verses.text: And every nation made gods of their own, and put <hi>them</hi> in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities in which they lived.

verses.name: II Kings 17:30
verses.text: And the men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,

verses.name: II Kings 17:31
verses.text: and the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their sons with fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech the gods of Sepharvaim.

verses.name: II Kings 17:32
verses.text: So they feared the LORD, and made to themselves, of the lowest of them, priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.

verses.name: II Kings 17:33
verses.text: They feared the LORD and served their own gods, according to the custom of the nations whom they removed from there.

verses.name: II Kings 17:34
verses.text: Until this day they do according to their former ways. They do not fear the LORD, neither do they do according to their statutes, or according to their ordinances, or according to the law and commandment which the LORD commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He named Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 17:35
verses.text: And the LORD had made a covenant and charged them, saying, You shall not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them,

verses.name: II Kings 17:36
verses.text: but the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and a stretched-out arm, you shall fear Him, and you shall worship Him, and you shall do sacrifice to Him.

verses.name: II Kings 17:37
verses.text: And the statutes, and the ordinances, and the law, and the commandment, which He wrote for you, you shall be careful to do forever. And you shall not fear other gods.

verses.name: II Kings 17:38
verses.text: And the covenant that I have made with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods.

verses.name: II Kings 17:39
verses.text: And you shall fear the LORD your God. And He shall deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.

verses.name: II Kings 17:40
verses.text: But they did not listen, but they followed after their former way.

verses.name: II Kings 17:41
verses.text: And it happened, these nations feared the LORD, and they served their graven images, both their sons and their sons' sons, as their fathers did, they do until this day.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:1
verses.text: And it happened in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.

verses.name: II Kings 18:2
verses.text: He <hi>was</hi> twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name <hi>was</hi> Abi, the daughter of Zachariah.

verses.name: II Kings 18:3
verses.text: And he did the right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father did.

verses.name: II Kings 18:4
verses.text: He removed the high places, and broke the pillars, and cut down the Asherah. And he broke in pieces the bronze serpent which Moses had made; for until those days the sons of Israel burned incense to it. And he called it Nehushtan.

verses.name: II Kings 18:5
verses.text: He trusted in the LORD God of Israel, and after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor who were before him.

verses.name: II Kings 18:6
verses.text: For he clung to the LORD. He did not depart from following Him, but kept His commandments, which the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.name: II Kings 18:7
verses.text: And the LORD was with him. He was blessed wherever he went. And he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and did not serve him.

verses.name: II Kings 18:8
verses.text: He struck the Philistines to Gaza and its borders, from the Watch Tower to the fortified city.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:9
verses.text: And it happened in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.

verses.name: II Kings 18:10
verses.text: And at the end of three years they took it, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, it <hi>was</hi> the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.

verses.name: II Kings 18:11
verses.text: And the king of Assyria carried away Israel to Assyria, and put them in Halah and in Habor <hi>by</hi> the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,

verses.name: II Kings 18:12
verses.text: because they did not obey the voice of the LORD their God, but transgressed His covenant, <hi>and</hi> all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded, and would not listen to them, nor do them.

verses.name: II Kings 18:13
verses.text: And in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.

verses.name: II Kings 18:14
verses.text: And Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, I have offended; turn back from me. Whatever you put on me I will bear. And the king of Assyria appointed to Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver, and thirty talents of gold.

verses.name: II Kings 18:15
verses.text: And Hezekiah gave him all the silver which was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasures of the king's house.

verses.name: II Kings 18:16
verses.text: At that time Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid. And he gave them to the king of Assyria.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 18:17
verses.text: And the king of Assyria sent Tartan, and the chief of the eunuchs, and the chief of the cupbearers from Lachish, to king Hezekiah with a great army against Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem. And when they had come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the Fuller's Field.

verses.name: II Kings 18:18
verses.text: And they called to the king. And Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who <hi>was</hi> over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, went out to them.

verses.name: II Kings 18:19
verses.text: And the chief of the cupbearers said to them, Speak now to Hezekiah, So says the great king, the king of Assyria, What hope <hi>is</hi> this in which you trust?

verses.name: II Kings 18:20
verses.text: Do you say that a mere word of the lips <hi>is</hi> wisdom and strength for the war? Now on whom do you trust that you rebel against me?

verses.name: II Kings 18:21
verses.text: Now, behold, you trust on the staff of this bruised reed, on Egypt, on which if a man leans, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So <hi>is</hi> Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust on him.

verses.name: II Kings 18:22
verses.text: But if you say to me, We trust in Jehovah our God, is He not the one whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has said to Judah and Jerusalem, You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem?

verses.name: II Kings 18:23
verses.text: And now, please give pledges to my lord the king of Assyria, and I will deliver two thousand horses to you if you are able to set riders on them.

verses.name: II Kings 18:24
verses.text: And how will you turn away the face of one commander of the least of my master's servants, and put your trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

verses.name: II Kings 18:25
verses.text: Have I now come up against this place to destroy it without Jehovah? Jehovah said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.

verses.name: II Kings 18:26
verses.text: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joah said to the chief of the cupbearers, Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand. And do not talk with us in Jewish, in the ears of the people who are on the wall.

verses.name: II Kings 18:27
verses.text: And the chief of the cupbearers said to them, Has my master sent me to your master and to you, to speak these words, <hi>and</hi> not to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?

verses.name: II Kings 18:28
verses.text: And the chief of the cupbearers stood and cried with a loud voice in Jewish, and spoke, saying, Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria:

verses.name: II Kings 18:29
verses.text: so says the king, Do not let Hezekiah fool you. For he shall not be able to deliver you out of his hand.

verses.name: II Kings 18:30
verses.text: And do not let Hezekiah make you trust in Jehovah, saying, Jehovah will surely deliver us, and this city shall not be delivered into the hands of the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 18:31
verses.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah. For so says the king of Assyria, Make with me a blessing, and come out to me, and you each shall eat of his vine, and each of his fig tree, and you each shall drink of the waters of his own cistern,

verses.name: II Kings 18:32
verses.text: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and of honey, and live, and not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah when he deceives you, saying, Jehovah will deliver us.

verses.name: II Kings 18:33
verses.text: Has any of the gods of the nations at all delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

verses.name: II Kings 18:34
verses.text: Where <hi>are</hi> the gods of Hamath and of Arpad? Where <hi>are</hi> the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

verses.name: II Kings 18:35
verses.text: Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their land out of my hand, that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?

verses.name: II Kings 18:36
verses.text: But the people kept silent and did not answer him a word. For the king's command was, saying, Do not answer him.

verses.name: II Kings 18:37
verses.text: And Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who <hi>was</hi> over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn. And they told him the words of the chief of the cupbearers.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:1
verses.text: And it happened when king Hezekiah heard, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth. And he went into the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 19:2
verses.text: And he sent Eliakim who <hi>was</hi> over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.

verses.name: II Kings 19:3
verses.text: And they said to him, So says Hezekiah, <hi>This is</hi> a day of trouble and of rebuke and contempt. For the sons have come to the birth, and <hi>there is</hi> no strength to bring forth.

verses.name: II Kings 19:4
verses.text: It may be the LORD your God will hear all the words of the chief cupbearer with which his master the king of Assyria has sent to reproach the living God, and will rebuke the words which the LORD your God has heard. And you shall lift up prayer for the rest who are left.

verses.name: II Kings 19:5
verses.text: And the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

verses.name: II Kings 19:6
verses.text: And Isaiah said to them, You shall say to your master, So says the LORD, Do not be afraid of the words which you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.

verses.name: II Kings 19:7
verses.text: Behold, I will send a blast on him, and he shall hear a rumor and shall return to his own land. And I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:8
verses.text: And the chief cupbearer returned and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.

verses.name: II Kings 19:9
verses.text: And when he heard it said of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, Behold, he has come out to fight against you, he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 19:10
verses.text: So you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 19:11
verses.text: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands by completely destroying them. And shall you be delivered?

verses.name: II Kings 19:12
verses.text: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, nations which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden in Telassar?

verses.name: II Kings 19:13
verses.text: Where <hi>is</hi> the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivah?

verses.name: II Kings 19:14
verses.text: And Hezekiah received the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read it. And Hezekiah went up into the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 19:15
verses.text: And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, O LORD God of Israel, who dwells <hi>between</hi> the cherubs, You <hi>are</hi> God Himself, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made the heavens and the earth.

verses.name: II Kings 19:16
verses.text: LORD, bow down Your ear and hear. O LORD, open Your eyes and see, and hear the words of Sennacherib, who has sent him to taunt the living God.

verses.name: II Kings 19:17
verses.text: Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands,

verses.name: II Kings 19:18
verses.text: and have thrown their gods into the fire; for they <hi>were</hi> no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, and they have destroyed them.

verses.name: II Kings 19:19
verses.text: And now, O, LORD our God, I beseech You, save us out of his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You <hi>are</hi> the LORD God, and You only.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:20
verses.text: And Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, So says the LORD God of Israel, I have heard what you have prayed to Me against Sennacherib king of Assyria.

verses.name: II Kings 19:21
verses.text: This <hi>is</hi> the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin, the daughter of Zion, has despised you <hi>and</hi> laughed you to scorn. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.

verses.name: II Kings 19:22
verses.text: Whom have you mocked and blasphemed? And against whom have you exalted <hi>your</hi> voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Even against the Holy One of Israel!

verses.name: II Kings 19:23
verses.text: You have mocked the Lord by your messengers, and have said, With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Lebanon, and will cut down its tall cedar trees, its choice fir trees. And I will enter into the lodgings of its borders, its densest forest;

verses.name: II Kings 19:24
verses.text: I have dug and drunk foreign waters, and with the sole of my feet I have dried up all the rivers of Egypt.

verses.name: II Kings 19:25
verses.text: Have you not heard it from afar, I made it? From days of old I fashioned it! Now I have caused it to come; that you should make fortified cities desolate heaps of ruins.

verses.name: II Kings 19:26
verses.text: And their people were of small power, they were fearful and put to shame. They were <hi>like</hi> the grass of the field, and the green herb, like the grass on the house-tops, and like grain blasted before it was grown up.

verses.name: II Kings 19:27
verses.text: But I know your sitting down, and your going out, and your coming in, and your rage against Me.

verses.name: II Kings 19:28
verses.text: Because of your rage against Me, and because your arrogance has come up into My ears, even I will put My hook in your nose, and My bridle in your lips. And I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

verses.name: II Kings 19:29
verses.text: And this shall be a sign to you: you shall eat this year such things as grow of themselves, and in the second year that which springs up of the same. And in the third year, sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat the fruits of them.

verses.name: II Kings 19:30
verses.text: And the remnant that has escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

verses.name: II Kings 19:31
verses.text: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and they who escape out of Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts shall do this.

verses.name: II Kings 19:32
verses.text: So the LORD says this concerning the king of Assyria. He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor throw up a bank against it.

verses.name: II Kings 19:33
verses.text: By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and shall not come into this city, says the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 19:34
verses.text: For I will defend this city, to save it for My own sake and for My servant David's sake.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 19:35
verses.text: And it happened that night, the Angel of the LORD went out and struck a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. And they arose early in the morning, and behold, they were all dead bodies.

verses.name: II Kings 19:36
verses.text: And Sennacherib king of Assyria departed. And he went and returned and lived at Nineveh.

verses.name: II Kings 19:37
verses.text: And it happened as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him with the sword. And they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:1
verses.text: In those days Hezekiah was sick to death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him and said to him, So says the LORD, Set your house in order, for you shall die and not live.

verses.name: II Kings 20:2
verses.text: And he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying, O LORD,

verses.name: II Kings 20:3
verses.text: I pray, O LORD, remember now how I have walked before You in truth and with a sincere heart, and have done good in Your sight. And Hezekiah wept with a great weeping.

verses.name: II Kings 20:4
verses.text: And it happened <hi>before</hi> Isaiah had gone out into the middle of the court, the word of the LORD came to him saying,

verses.name: II Kings 20:5
verses.text: Return again and tell Hezekiah the leader of My people, So says the LORD, the God of David your father, I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 20:6
verses.text: And I will add fifteen years to your days. And I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria. And I will defend this city for My own sake, and for My servant David's sake.

verses.name: II Kings 20:7
verses.text: And Isaiah said, Take a lump of figs. And they took and laid <hi>it</hi> on the boil, and he recovered.

verses.name: II Kings 20:8
verses.text: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, What <hi>shall be</hi> the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I shall go up into the house of the LORD the third day?

verses.name: II Kings 20:9
verses.text: And Isaiah said, This <hi>will be</hi> the sign from the LORD, that the LORD will do the thing which He has spoken. Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?

verses.name: II Kings 20:10
verses.text: And Hezekiah answered, It is a light thing for the shadow to go down ten steps. No, but let the shadow go backward ten steps.

verses.name: II Kings 20:11
verses.text: And Isaiah the prophet cried to the LORD. And He brought the shadow ten steps backward, by which it had gone down on the sundial of Ahaz.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 20:12
verses.text: At that time Berodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah. For he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

verses.name: II Kings 20:13
verses.text: And Hezekiah listened to them, and showed them all the house of his precious things, the silver and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house nor in all his dominion which Hezekiah did not show them.

verses.name: II Kings 20:14
verses.text: And Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah and said to him, What did these men say? And from where did they come to you? And Hezekiah said, They have come from a far country, from Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 20:15
verses.text: And he said, What have they seen in your house? And Hezekiah answered, They have seen all that <hi>is</hi> in my house. There is nothing among my treasures which I have not shown to them.

verses.name: II Kings 20:16
verses.text: And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 20:17
verses.text: Behold, the days come when all that <hi>is</hi> in your house, and which your fathers have laid up in store until today, shall be carried into Babylon. Nothing shall be left, says the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 20:18
verses.text: And of your sons which shall issue from you, which you shall father, they shall take away. And they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 20:19
verses.text: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, Good <hi>is</hi> the word of the LORD which you have spoken. And he said, <hi>Is it</hi> not <hi>good</hi> if peace and truth are in my days?

verses.name: II Kings 20:20
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made a pool and a conduit, and brought water into the city, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 20:21
verses.text: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers. And Manasseh his son reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:1
verses.text: Manasseh <hi>was</hi> twelve years old when he began to reign. And he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Hephzibah.

verses.name: II Kings 21:2
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, after the abominations of the heathen whom the LORD cast out before the sons of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 21:3
verses.text: For he built up again the high places which his father Hezekiah had destroyed. And he reared up altars for Baal, and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel did. And he worshiped all the host of heaven, and served them.

verses.name: II Kings 21:4
verses.text: And he built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD said, In Jerusalem I will put My name.

verses.name: II Kings 21:5
verses.text: And he built altars for all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 21:6
verses.text: And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times and used fortune-tellers. And he dealt with familiar spirits and wizards. He worked much wickedness in the sight of the LORD, to provoke <hi>Him</hi> to anger.

verses.name: II Kings 21:7
verses.text: And he set a graven image of the Asherah which he had made in the house, of which the LORD had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.

verses.name: II Kings 21:8
verses.text: And I will not again make the feet of Israel wander any more out of the land which I gave their fathers; only if they will be careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that My servant Moses commanded them.

verses.name: II Kings 21:9
verses.text: But they did not listen. And Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than the nations ever did, whom the LORD destroyed before the sons of Israel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:10
verses.text: And the LORD spoke by His servants the prophets, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 21:11
verses.text: Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations, doing more wickedly than all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has made Judah also to sin with his idols,

verses.name: II Kings 21:12
verses.text: therefore, so says the LORD God of Israel, Behold, I <hi>am</hi> bringing evil on Jerusalem and Judah, so that whoever hears of it, both his ears shall tingle.

verses.name: II Kings 21:13
verses.text: And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the measuring line of the house of Ahab. And I will wipe Jerusalem like a dish is wiped, wiping and turning <hi>it</hi> upside down.

verses.name: II Kings 21:14
verses.text: And I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies. And they shall become a prey and a spoil to all their enemies,

verses.name: II Kings 21:15
verses.text: because they have done the evil in My sight, and have provoked Me to anger, since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt even until this day.

verses.name: II Kings 21:16
verses.text: And also Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another, besides his sin with which he made Judah to sin, in doing the evil in the sight of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 21:17
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin which he sinned, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 21:18
verses.text: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza. And his son Amon reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 21:19
verses.text: Amon <hi>was</hi> twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

verses.name: II Kings 21:20
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did.

verses.name: II Kings 21:21
verses.text: And he walked in all the way that his father walked, and served the idols which his father served, and worshiped them.

verses.name: II Kings 21:22
verses.text: And <hi>he</hi> left the LORD God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 21:23
verses.text: And the servants of Amon plotted against him and killed the king in his own house.

verses.name: II Kings 21:24
verses.text: And the people of the land killed all those who had plotted against king Amon. And the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 21:25
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Amon which he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Books of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 21:26
verses.text: And <hi>he was</hi> buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. And his son Josiah reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:1
verses.text: Josiah <hi>was</hi> eight years old when he began to reign. And he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath.

verses.name: II Kings 22:2
verses.text: And he did the right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in all the way of David his father, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

verses.name: II Kings 22:3
verses.text: And it happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam the scribe, to the house of the LORD, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 22:4
verses.text: Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, so that he may count the silver which is brought into the house of the LORD, which the doorkeepers have gathered from the people.

verses.name: II Kings 22:5
verses.text: And let them deliver it into the hand of the workers who have the oversight of the house of the Lord. And let them give it to the workers who <hi>are</hi> in the house of the LORD, in order to repair the breaks of the house,

verses.name: II Kings 22:6
verses.text: to carpenters, and builders, and masons, and to buy timber and cut stone to repair the house.

verses.name: II Kings 22:7
verses.text: Only, the silver that is given into their hand shall not be reckoned with them, for they are dealing in faithfulness.

verses.name: II Kings 22:8
verses.text: And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

verses.name: II Kings 22:9
verses.text: And Shaphan the scribe came to the king and brought the king word again, and said, Your servants have gathered the silver that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hand of the workers, who have the oversight of the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 22:10
verses.text: And Shaphan the scribe showed the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest has delivered me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 22:11
verses.text: And it happened when the king had heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.

verses.name: II Kings 22:12
verses.text: And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Michaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asahiah a servant of the king, saying,

verses.name: II Kings 22:13
verses.text: Go inquire of the LORD for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book which is found. For great <hi>is</hi> the wrath of the LORD which is kindled against us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of this book, to do according to all which is written concerning us.

verses.name: II Kings 22:14
verses.text: And Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asahiah, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. And she lived in Jerusalem in the second <hi> part</hi>. And they talked with her.

verses.name: II Kings 22:15
verses.text: And she said to them, So says the LORD God of Israel, Tell the man who sent you tome,

verses.name: II Kings 22:16
verses.text: So says the LORD, Behold, I will bring evil on this place and on the people of it, all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read;

verses.name: II Kings 22:17
verses.text: because they have forsaken Me, and have burned incense to other gods, so that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands, therefore My wrath shall be kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched.

verses.name: II Kings 22:18
verses.text: But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, so you shall say to him, So says the LORD God of Israel, The words which you have heard,

verses.name: II Kings 22:19
verses.text: because your heart <hi>was</hi> tender and you have humbled yourself before the LORD, when you heard what I spoke against this place, and against its people (that they should become a waste and a curse, and have torn your clothes and wept before Me), I have heard you, says the LORD.

verses.name: II Kings 22:20
verses.text: Behold, even so I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace. And your eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring on this place. And they brought the king <hi>this</hi> word again.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:1
verses.text: And the king sent. And they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 23:2
verses.text: And the king went up into the house of the LORD. And all the men of Judah and all the people of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets, and all the people, from the small even to the great. And he read all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the LORD in their ears.

verses.name: II Kings 23:3
verses.text: And the king stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all <hi>his</hi> heart and all <hi>his</hi> soul, to perform the words of this covenant which was written in this Book. And all the people stood to the covenant.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:4
verses.text: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the doorkeepers, to bring forth out of the temple of the LORD all the vessels which were made for Baal, and for the Asherah, and for all the host of heaven. And he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them to Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 23:5
verses.text: And he put down the idol-worshiping priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn <hi>incense</hi> in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places around Jerusalem. He also put down those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of the heavens.

verses.name: II Kings 23:6
verses.text: And he brought out the Asherah from the house of the LORD outside Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped <hi>it</hi> to powder, and threw the powder of it on the graves of the sons of the people.

verses.name: II Kings 23:7
verses.text: And he broke down the houses of the sodomites, which <hi>were</hi> by the house of the LORD, where the women wove coverings for the Asherah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:8
verses.text: And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned <hi>incense</hi>, from Geba to Beer-sheba. And he broke down the high places of the gates which <hi>were</hi> in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man's left hand at the gate of the city.

verses.name: II Kings 23:9
verses.text: But the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they ate of the unleavened <hi>bread</hi> among their brothers.

verses.name: II Kings 23:10
verses.text: And he defiled Topheth, in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, so that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

verses.name: II Kings 23:11
verses.text: And he took away the horses which the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the LORD, by the room of Nathan-melech the eunuch, which <hi>was</hi> in the suburbs. And he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

verses.name: II Kings 23:12
verses.text: And the altars which <hi>were</hi> on the top of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made, and the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king beat them down, and broke them down from there. And he threw the dust of them into the brook Kidron.

verses.name: II Kings 23:13
verses.text: And the high places which <hi>were</hi> before Jerusalem on the right hand of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.

verses.name: II Kings 23:14
verses.text: And he broke the images in pieces, and cut down the Asherahs, and filled their places with the bones of men.

verses.name: II Kings 23:15
verses.text: And also the altar which <hi>was</hi> at Bethel, <hi>and</hi> the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, both that altar and the high place he broke down, and burned the high place; he stamped it to powder, and burned the Asherah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:16
verses.text: And as Josiah turned, he spied the tombs which <hi>were</hi> there in the mountain. And he sent and took the bones out of the tombs, and burned <hi>them</hi> on the altar and defiled it, according to the word of the LORD which the man of God had proclaimed, who spoke these words.

verses.name: II Kings 23:17
verses.text: And he said, What monument <hi>is</hi> that which I see? And the men of the city told him, <hi>It is</hi> the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things which you have done against the altar of Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 23:18
verses.text: And he said, Let him alone; let no one move his bones. And they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came out of Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 23:19
verses.text: And also all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke <hi>the LORD</hi> to anger, Josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts which he had done in Bethel.

verses.name: II Kings 23:20
verses.text: And he killed all the priests of the high places <hi>which were</hi> there on the altars, and burned men's bones on them, and returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 23:21
verses.text: And the king commanded all the people saying, Prepare the Passover to the LORD your God, as <hi>it is</hi> written in the Book of the Covenant.

verses.name: II Kings 23:22
verses.text: Surely there was not held such a Passover from the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah,

verses.name: II Kings 23:23
verses.text: but in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, this Passover was held to the LORD in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 23:24
verses.text: And also Josiah put away the mediums, and the soothsayers, and the family gods, and the idols, and all the abominations which were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, so that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book which Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:25
verses.text: And there was no king like him before him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses. And after him none rose up like him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:26
verses.text: But the Lord did not turn from the heat of His great wrath, with which His anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations which Manasseh had provoked Him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:27
verses.text: And the LORD said, I will also remove Judah out of My sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.

verses.name: II Kings 23:28
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 23:29
verses.text: In his days Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates. And king Josiah went against him. And he killed him at Megiddo, when he saw him.

verses.name: II Kings 23:30
verses.text: And his servants made him ride dead in a chariot from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father's place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 23:31
verses.text: Jehoahaz <hi>was</hi> twenty-three years old when he began to reign. And he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:32
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

verses.name: II Kings 23:33
verses.text: And Pharaoh-necho put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he might not reign in Jerusalem. And he put the land to a tax of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

verses.name: II Kings 23:34
verses.text: And Pharaoh-necho made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father. And he changed his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away. And he came to Egypt and died there.

verses.name: II Kings 23:35
verses.text: And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh. But he taxed the land to give the silver according to Pharaoh's command. He exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, from each one according to his worth, to give it to Pharaoh-necho.

verses.name: II Kings 23:36
verses.text: Jehoiakim <hi>was</hi> twenty-five years old when he began to reign. And he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.

verses.name: II Kings 23:37
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:1
verses.text: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

verses.name: II Kings 24:2
verses.text: And the LORD sent against him troops of the Chaldees, and bands of the Syrians, and troops of the Moabites, and troops of the Ammonites. And He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke by His servants the prophets.

verses.name: II Kings 24:3
verses.text: Surely at the commandment of the Lord <hi>this</hi> came on Judah, to remove <hi>them</hi> out of His sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;

verses.name: II Kings 24:4
verses.text: and also for the innocent blood which he shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, which the LORD would not pardon.

verses.name: II Kings 24:5
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the Kings of Judah?

verses.name: II Kings 24:6
verses.text: And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers. And Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Kings 24:7
verses.text: And the king of Egypt did not come again out of his land any more. For the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt to the river Euphrates all that <hi>belonged to</hi> the king of Egypt.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 24:8
verses.text: Jehoiachin <hi>was</hi> eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 24:9
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.

verses.name: II Kings 24:10
verses.text: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.

verses.name: II Kings 24:11
verses.text: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants besieged it.

verses.name: II Kings 24:12
verses.text: And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother, and his servants, and his leaders, and his eunuchs. And the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

verses.name: II Kings 24:13
verses.text: And <hi>he</hi> carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had said.

verses.name: II Kings 24:14
verses.text: And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the leaders, and all the mighty men of war, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths. None remained except the poorest sort of the people of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 24:15
verses.text: And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his eunuchs. And the mighty of the land he carried into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 24:16
verses.text: And the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon all the men of might, seven thousand of them, and a thousand craftsmen and smiths, all who were strong and able for war.

verses.name: II Kings 24:17
verses.text: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his father's brother, king in his place. And he changed his name to Zedekiah.

verses.name: II Kings 24:18
verses.text: Zedekiah <hi>was</hi> twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.name: II Kings 24:19
verses.text: And he did the evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.name: II Kings 24:20
verses.text: For it was through the anger of the LORD that Zedekiah happened to rebel against the king of Babylon in Jerusalem and in Judah, until <hi>God</hi> had put them out of His presence.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:1
verses.text: And it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came. He and all his army came against Jerusalem and pitched against it, and built a siege-mound all around it.

verses.name: II Kings 25:2
verses.text: And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Zedekiah,

verses.name: II Kings 25:3
verses.text: on the ninth of the <hi>fourth</hi> month, when famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

verses.name: II Kings 25:4
verses.text: And the city was broken up, and by night all the men of war <hi>went</hi> by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king's garden. And the Chaldeans were against the city all round. And the king went the way toward the plain.

verses.name: II Kings 25:5
verses.text: And the army of the Chaldees pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. And all his army were scattered from him.

verses.name: II Kings 25:6
verses.text: And they took the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon, to Riblah. And they gave judgment on him.

verses.name: II Kings 25:7
verses.text: And they killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with bronze chains and carried him to Babylon.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:8
verses.text: And in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month; it was the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; Nebu-zaradan the chief of the executioners, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Kings 25:9
verses.text: And he burned the house of the LORD, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. And every great one's house he burned with fire.

verses.name: II Kings 25:10
verses.text: And all the army of the Chaldeans who <hi>were</hi> with the chief of the executioners broke down the walls of Jerusalem all around.

verses.name: II Kings 25:11
verses.text: And the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the fugitives who fell away to the king of Babylon, with the rest of the multitude, the chief of the executioners carried away.

verses.name: II Kings 25:12
verses.text: But the chief of the executioners left a few of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

verses.name: II Kings 25:13
verses.text: And the bronze pillars in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the bronze sea in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke into pieces and carried the bronze from them to Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 25:14
verses.text: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of bronze with which they ministered, they also took away.

verses.name: II Kings 25:15
verses.text: And the chief of the executioners took away the fire-pans, and the bowls, that <hi>were</hi> all of gold, and all of silver;

verses.name: II Kings 25:16
verses.text: also the two pillars, the one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD. The bronze of all these vessels was without weight.

verses.name: II Kings 25:17
verses.text: The height of the one pillar <hi>was</hi> eighteen cubits, and the capital on it <hi>was</hi> bronze. And the height of the capital <hi>was</hi> three cubits. And the grating and the pomegranates on the capital all around <hi>were</hi> all of bronze. And the second pillar had grating like these.

verses.name: II Kings 25:18
verses.text: And the chief of the executioners took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

verses.name: II Kings 25:19
verses.text: And he took out of the city a certain eunuch who was appointed over the men of war, and five men of those who were in the king's presence, who were found in the city, and the chief scribe of the army (who called up the people of the land together), and sixty men of the people of the land found in the city.

verses.name: II Kings 25:20
verses.text: And Nebu-zaradan the chief of the executioners took these and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.

verses.name: II Kings 25:21
verses.text: And the king of Babylon struck them and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. And he exiled Judah from its land.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Kings 25:22
verses.text: And he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left.

verses.name: II Kings 25:23
verses.text: And all the commanders of the army, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor. And they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.

verses.name: II Kings 25:24
verses.text: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, Do not fear to be the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.

verses.name: II Kings 25:25
verses.text: And it happened in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama of the seed of the kingdom, and ten men with him, came and struck Gedaliah, and he died, and also the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

verses.name: II Kings 25:26
verses.text: And all the people, both small and great, and the commanders of the armies, arose and came to Egypt. For they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

verses.name: II Kings 25:27
verses.text: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison.

verses.name: II Kings 25:28
verses.text: And he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the throne of the kings who <hi>were</hi> with him in Babylon.

verses.name: II Kings 25:29
verses.text: And he changed his prison clothes. And he always ate bread before him all the days of his life.

verses.name: II Kings 25:30
verses.text: And his allowance <hi>was</hi> a regular allowance given him from the king, a daily ration for every day, all the days of his life.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:1
verses.text: Adam, Seth, Enos,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:2
verses.text: Cainan, Mahalaleel, Jered,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:3
verses.text: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:4
verses.text: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:5
verses.text: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:6
verses.text: And the sons of Gomer were Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:7
verses.text: And the sons of Javan were Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:8
verses.text: The sons of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:9
verses.text: And the sons of Cush were Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:10
verses.text: And Cush fathered Nimrod. He began to be mighty on the earth.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:11
verses.text: And Mizraim fathered Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:12
verses.text: and Pathrusim, and Casluhim (from whom came the Philistines), and Caphthorim.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:13
verses.text: And Canaan fathered Zidon his firstborn, and Heth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:14
verses.text: the Jebusite also, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:15
verses.text: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:16
verses.text: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:17
verses.text: The sons of Shem were Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:18
verses.text: And Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:19
verses.text: And to Eber were born two sons. The name of the one <hi>was</hi> Peleg (because in his days the earth was divided), and the name of his brother <hi>was</hi> Joktan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:20
verses.text: And Joktan fathered Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazar-maveth, and Jerah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:21
verses.text: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:22
verses.text: and Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:23
verses.text: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:24
verses.text: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:25
verses.text: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:26
verses.text: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:27
verses.text: Abram (the same <hi>is</hi> Abraham).  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:28
verses.text: The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:29
verses.text: These <hi>are</hi> their generations. The first-born of Ishmael was Nebaioth, and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:30
verses.text: Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:31
verses.text: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These <hi>are</hi> the sons of Ishmael.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:32
verses.text: And the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: She bore Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:33
verses.text: And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these <hi>are</hi> the sons of Keturah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:34
verses.text: And Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac <hi>were</hi> Esau and Israel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:35
verses.text: The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:36
verses.text: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:37
verses.text: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:38
verses.text: And the sons of Seir: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:39
verses.text: And the sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. And Timna <hi>was</hi> Lotan's sister.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:40
verses.text: The sons of Shobal: Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:41
verses.text: The son of Anah <hi>was</hi> Dishon. And the sons of Dishon: Amram, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:42
verses.text: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zavan, and Jakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:43
verses.text: And these <hi>are</hi> the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over the sons of Israel: Bela the son of Beor, and the name of his city <hi>was</hi> Dinhabah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:44
verses.text: And Bela died; and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:45
verses.text: And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:46
verses.text: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city <hi>was</hi> Avith.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:47
verses.text: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:48
verses.text: And Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:49
verses.text: And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:50
verses.text: And Baal-hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place. And the name of his city <hi>was</hi> Pai. And his wife's name <hi>was</hi> Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:51
verses.text: And Hadad died. And the chiefs of Edom: chief Timnah, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:52
verses.text: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:53
verses.text: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

verses.name: I Chronicles 1:54
verses.text: chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These <hi>are</hi> the chiefs of Edom.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:1
verses.text: These <hi>are</hi> the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:2
verses.text: Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:3
verses.text: The sons of Judah: Er and Onan, and Shelah, three born to him from the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess. And Er, the first-born of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD, and He killed him.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:4
verses.text: And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Pharez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah <hi>were</hi> five.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:5
verses.text: The sons of Pharez: Hezron and Hamul.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:6
verses.text: And the sons of Zerah <hi>were</hi> Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara, all of them five.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:7
verses.text: And the sons of Carmi: Achan, the troubler of Israel, who sinned in the cursed thing.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:8
verses.text: And the son of Ethan <hi>was</hi> Azariah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:9
verses.text: And the sons also of Hezron, who were born to him: Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:10
verses.text: And Ram fathered Amminadab. And Amminadab fathered Nahshon, prince of the sons of Judah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:11
verses.text: And Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:12
verses.text: and Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:13
verses.text: And Jesse fathered his first-born Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:14
verses.text: Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:15
verses.text: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:16
verses.text: Their sisters <hi>were</hi> Zeruiah and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah <hi>were</hi> Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:17
verses.text: And Abigail bore Amasa. And the father of Amasa <hi>was</hi> Jether, the Ishmaelite.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:18
verses.text: And Caleb the son of Hezron fathered <hi>sons</hi> of Azubah <hi>his</hi> wife, and of Jerioth. Her sons <hi>are</hi> these: Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:19
verses.text: And when Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrath to himself, who bore him Hur.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:20
verses.text: And Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezaleel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:21
verses.text: And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he <hi>was</hi> sixty years old. And she bore him Segub.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:22
verses.text: And Segub fathered Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:23
verses.text: And he took Geshur, and Aram, with the towns of Jair, from them, with Kenath, and its towns, sixty cities. All these <hi>belonged</hi> to the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:24
verses.text: And after Hezron died in Caleb-ephratah, then Abiah, Hezron's wife bore him Ashur the father of Tekoa.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:25
verses.text: And the sons of Jerahmeel the first-born of Hezron: Ram the first-born, and Bunah, and Oren, and Ozem, <hi>and</hi> Ahijah.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:26
verses.text: Jerahmeel also had another wife, whose name <hi>was</hi> Atarah. She <hi>was</hi> the mother of Onam.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:27
verses.text: And the sons of Ram the first-born of Jerahmeel: were Maaz, and Jamin, and Eker.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:28
verses.text: And the sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. And the sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:29
verses.text: And the name of Abishur's wife <hi>was</hi> Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:30
verses.text: And the sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. But Seled died without sons.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:31
verses.text: And the son of Appaim <hi>was</hi> Ishi. And the son of Ishi <hi>was</hi> Sheshan. And the son of Sheshan <hi>was</hi> Ahlai.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:32
verses.text: And the sons of Jada, the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether died without sons.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:33
verses.text: And the sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:34
verses.text: And Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, and his name <hi>was</hi> Jarha.

verses.name: I Chronicles 2:35
