verses.name: II Chronicles 4:7
verses.text: And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their form, and set <hi>them</hi> in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:8
verses.text: And He made ten tables, and placed <hi>them</hi> in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left. And he made a hundred basins of gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:9
verses.text: And he made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:10
verses.text: And he set the sea on the right side of the east end, over against the south.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:11
verses.text: And Hiram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basins. And Hiram finished the work that he was to make for king Solomon for the house of God:

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:12
verses.text: the two pillars, and the bowls, and the capitals on the tops of the two pillars, and the two wreaths to cover the two bowls of the capitals which <hi>were</hi> on the top of the pillars,

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:13
verses.text: and four hundred pomegranates on the two wreaths, two rows of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:14
verses.text: He also made bases, and he made lavers on the bases;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:15
verses.text: and one sea, and twelve oxen under it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:16
verses.text: And Hiram made the pots, and the shovels, and the flesh-hooks, and all their vessels of burnished bronze for king Solomon for the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:17
verses.text: In the plain of Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:18
verses.text: And Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance. For the weight of the bronze could not be found out.

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:19
verses.text: And Solomon made all the vessels <hi>for</hi> the house of God, and the golden altar, and the tables on which the showbread <hi>was set</hi>;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:20
verses.text: and the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, so that they should burn according to the law before the holy place;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:21
verses.text: and the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs <hi>of</hi> gold, perfect gold;

verses.name: II Chronicles 4:22
verses.text: and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the censers, <hi>of</hi> pure gold; and the entrance of the house, the inner doors of it for the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the house of the temple, <hi>of</hi> gold.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:1
verses.text: And all the work that Solomon made for the house of the LORD was finished. And Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated. And he put the silver and the gold, and all the vessels among the treasures of the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:2
verses.text: And Solomon gathered the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which <hi>is</hi> Zion.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:3
verses.text: And all the men of Israel gathered themselves to the king in the feast in the seventh month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:4
verses.text: And all the elders of Israel came. And the Levites took up the ark.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:5
verses.text: And they brought up the ark, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that <hi>were</hi> in the tabernacle. The priests <hi>and</hi> the Levites brought these up.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:6
verses.text: And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel that were gathered to him before the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen which could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:7
verses.text: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the Holy of Holies in the house, into the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubs.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:8
verses.text: For the cherubs spread out <hi>their</hi> wings over the ark, and the cherubs covered the ark and its staves above.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:9
verses.text: And they drew out the staves so that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the oracle. But they were not seen outside. And there it is until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:10
verses.text: Nothing <hi>was</hi> in the ark except the two tables which Moses put <hi>in it</hi> at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:11
verses.text: And it happened as the priests came out of the holy <hi>place</hi>, for all the priests present were sanctified, and did not wait by division.

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:12
verses.text: And the Levitical singers, all of them of Asaph, of Heman, of Jeduthun, with their sons and their brothers, <hi>being</hi> clothed in white linen, having cymbals and with harps and lyres, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets,

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:13
verses.text: and <hi>they</hi> were as one to the trumpeters and to the singers, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD; and as they lifted up <hi>their</hi> voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, <hi>saying</hi>, For He is good, for His mercy <hi>endures</hi> forever, the house was filled with a cloud, the house of the LORD,

verses.name: II Chronicles 5:14
verses.text: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of God!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:1
verses.text: And Solomon said, The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick darkness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:2
verses.text: And I have built a house for You to live in, and a place for Your dwelling forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:3
verses.text: And the king turned his face and blessed the whole congregation of Israel. And all the congregation of Israel stood.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:4
verses.text: And he said, Blessed <hi>be</hi> the LORD God of Israel, who has with His hands fulfilled that which He spoke with His mouth to my father David, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:5
verses.text: From the day that I brought My people out of the land of Egypt I have not chosen any city among all the tribes of Israel to build a house in, so that My name might be there. Nor have I chosen any man to be a ruler over My people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:6
verses.text: But now I have chosen Jerusalem, so that My name might be there, and now I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:7
verses.text: And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:8
verses.text: But the LORD said to David my father, Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well in that it was in your heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:9
verses.text: But you shall not build the house; but your son, who shall come forth out of your loins, shall build the house for My name.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:10
verses.text: And the LORD has lifted up His word that He has spoken. For I have risen up in place of David my father, and am set on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:11
verses.text: And I have put the ark in it, in which <hi>is</hi> the covenant of the LORD which He made with the sons of Israel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:12
verses.text: And he stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:13
verses.text: For Solomon had made a bronze scaffold, five cubits long and five cubits broad and three cubits high. And he had set it in the midst of the court. And he stood on it, and kneeled down on his knees before all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward Heaven.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:14
verses.text: And he said, O LORD God of Israel, <hi>there is</hi> no God like You in Heaven or in earth. You keep Your covenant and show mercy to Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:15
verses.text: You have kept with Your servant David my father that which You have promised him. And You spoke with Your mouth, and have fulfilled <hi>it</hi> with Your hand, as <hi>it is</hi> this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:16
verses.text: And now, O LORD God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father that which You have promised him, saying, There shall not fail you a man in My sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your sons take heed to their way to walk in My law, as you have walked before Me.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:17
verses.text: And now, O LORD God of Israel, let Your word be proven true, which You have spoken to Your servant David.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:18
verses.text: But truly will God in deed dwell with men on the earth? Behold, Heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You! How much less this house which I have built?

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:19
verses.text: And You have turned toward the prayer of Your servant, and to his cry, O LORD my God, to listen to the cry and the prayer which Your servant prays before You.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:20
verses.text: I pray that Your eyes may be open on this house day and night, on the place of which You have said that You would put Your name there, to listen to the prayer which Your servant prays toward this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:21
verses.text: And You will listen to the cries of Your servant, and of Your people Israel, which they shall pray toward this place, and You will from Your dwelling-place, from Heaven, and shall hear and forgive.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:22
verses.text: If a man sins against his neighbor, and if an oath is laid on him to make him swear, and if the oath comes before Your altar in this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:23
verses.text: then hear from Heaven, and do, and judge Your servants by repaying the wicked, by bringing his way back on his own head, and by justifying <hi>the</hi> righteous, by giving to him according to his righteousness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:24
verses.text: And if Your people Israel be put to the worse before the enemy because they have sinned against You, and if they shall return and confess Your name, and shall pray and cry before You in this house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:25
verses.text: then hear from Heaven, and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them again into the land which You give to them and to their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:26
verses.text: When the heavens shall be shut up, and there is no rain because they have sinned against You; if they pray toward this place, and confess Your name, and turn from their sin when You afflict them,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:27
verses.text: then hear from Heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants and of Your people Israel, when You have taught them the good way in which they should walk. And send rain on Your land which You have given to Your people for an inheritance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:28
verses.text: If there is famine in the land, if there is a plague, if blasting or mildew, locusts or ravagers, if their enemies have distressed them in the gates of their land, with any plague and any sickness;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:29
verses.text: whatever prayer, whatever cry shall be made by any man, or by all Your people Israel, when everyone shall know his own plague and his own grief, and shall spread forth his hands in this house;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:30
verses.text: then hear from Heaven, Your dwelling-place, and forgive, and give to every man according to all his ways, whose heart You know. For You only know the hearts of the sons of men.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:31
verses.text: Do this so that they may fear You, to walk in Your ways, as long as they live in the land which You gave to our fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:32
verses.text: And also to the stranger who is not of Your people Israel, but has come from a far country for Your great name's sake, and Your mighty hand, and Your stretched out arm, if they come and pray in this house;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:33
verses.text: then hear from Heaven, from Your dwelling-place, and do according to all that the stranger calls to You for, so that all people of the earth may know Your name, and fear You, as Your people Israel, and may know that this house which I have built is called by Your name.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:34
verses.text: If Your people go out to war against their enemies by the way that You shall send them, and if they pray to You toward this city which You have chosen, and the house which I have built for Your name,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:35
verses.text: then hear from Heaven their prayer and their cry and maintain their cause.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:36
verses.text: If they sin against You (for there is no man who does not sin), and if You are angry with them and deliver them up before their enemies, and they carry them away captives to a land far off or near,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:37
verses.text: yet if they think within themselves in the land where they are carried captive, and turn and pray to You in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done wrong and have dealt wickedly

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:38
verses.text: if they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity where they have carried them captives, and if they pray toward their land which You gave to their fathers and toward the city which You have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for Your name;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:39
verses.text: then hear from Heaven, from Your dwelling-place, their prayer and their cries, and maintain their cause, and forgive Your people who have sinned against You.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:40
verses.text: Now, my God, I beseech You, let Your eyes be open and Your ears hear the prayer made in this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:41
verses.text: And now arise, O LORD God, into Your resting-place, You, and the ark of Your strength. Let Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let Your saints rejoice in goodness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:42
verses.text: O LORD God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed. Remember the good deeds of David Your servant.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:1
verses.text: And when Solomon had made an end of praying, the fire came down from Heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices. And the glory of the LORD filled the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:2
verses.text: And the priests could not enter into the house of the LORD because the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD's house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:3
verses.text: And when all the sons of Israel saw how the fire came down, and the glory of the LORD on the house, they bowed <hi>their</hi> faces to the ground on the pavement, and worshiped and praised the LORD, saying, For <hi>He is</hi> good, for His mercy <hi>endures</hi> forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:4
verses.text: And the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:5
verses.text: And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand oxen, and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. And the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:6
verses.text: And the priests waited on their offices, and the Levites with instruments of music of the LORD, which David the king had made to praise the LORD, because His mercy <hi>endures</hi> forever, when David praised by their ministry. And the priests sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:7
verses.text: And Solomon made the middle of the court before the house of the LORD holy. For there he offered burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt offerings, and the food offerings, and the fat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:8
verses.text: And at the same time Solomon kept the feast seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath to the river of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:9
verses.text: And in the eighth day they made a solemn assembly. For they kept the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:10
verses.text: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away into their tents, glad and merry in heart for the goodness that the LORD had shown to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel His people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:11
verses.text: So Solomon finished the house of the LORD, and the king's house. And all that came into Solomon's heart to make in the house of the LORD, and in his own house, he did with success.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:12
verses.text: And the LORD appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him, I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place to Myself for a house of sacrifice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:13
verses.text: If I shut up the heavens, and there is no rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send a plague among My people;

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:14
verses.text: if My people, who are called by My name, shall humble themselves and pray, and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from Heaven and will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:15
verses.text: Now My eyes shall be open, and My ears shall be open to the prayer of this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:16
verses.text: For now I have chosen and sanctified this house, so that My name may be there forever. And My eyes and My heart shall be there forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:17
verses.text: And you, if you will walk before me, as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and shall observe My statutes and My judgments,

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:18
verses.text: then I will make the throne of your kingdom sure, as I have covenanted with David your father, saying, There shall not fail you a man <hi>to be</hi> ruler in Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:19
verses.text: But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments which I have set before you, and if you shall go and serve other gods and worship them,

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:20
verses.text: then I will pluck them up by the roots out of My land which I have given them. And this house which I have sanctified for My name, I will cast out of My sight, and I will make it to be a proverb and a byword among all nations.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:21
verses.text: And this house, which is high, shall be a wonder to everyone who passes by it, so that <hi>they</hi> shall shudder and say, Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:22
verses.text: And it shall be answered, Because they forsook the LORD God of their fathers who brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods and worshiped them and served them. Therefore He has brought all this evil on them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:1
verses.text: And it happened at the end of twenty years, Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:2
verses.text: As to the cities that Hiram had given to Solomon, Solomon had built them, and he caused the sons of Israel to live there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:3
verses.text: And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah, and prevailed against it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:4
verses.text: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities which he built in Hamath.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:5
verses.text: And he built Beth-horon the upper and Beth-horon the lower, fenced cities with walls, gates, and bars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:6
verses.text: And he built Baalath, and all the store cities which Solomon had, and all the chariot cities, and the cities of the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:7
verses.text: All the people <hi>who were</hi> left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who <hi>were</hi> not of Israel,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:8
verses.text: of their sons who <hi>were</hi> left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel did not destroy, Solomon made them subject to forced labor until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:9
verses.text: And of the sons of Israel, Solomon did not make any servants for his work. But they <hi>were</hi> men of war, and commanders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots, and his horsemen.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:10
verses.text: And these <hi>were</hi> the chief of king Solomon's officers, two hundred and fifty who bore rule over the people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:11
verses.text: And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David to the house which he had built for her. For he said, My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because <hi>the places</hi> into which the ark of the LORD has come are holy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:12
verses.text: And Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD which he had built before the porch,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:13
verses.text: even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the Feast of Unleavened <hi>Bread</hi>, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of Tabernacles.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:14
verses.text: And according to the order of David his father, he appointed the divisions of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their charges, to praise and minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required; and the gatekeepers by their divisions at every gate; for so David the man of God had commanded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:15
verses.text: And they did not depart <hi>from</hi> the command of the king to the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:16
verses.text: And all the work of Solomon was prepared until the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD, and until it was finished. And the house of the LORD was complete.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:17
verses.text: And Solomon went to Ezion-geber, and to Eloth, at the seaside in the land of Edom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:18
verses.text: And Hiram sent ships to him by the hand of his servants, and servants who knew <hi>the</hi> sea. And they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took four hundred and fifty talents of gold from there, and brought <hi>them</hi> to king Solomon.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:1
verses.text: And the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, and came to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that carried spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones. And she came in to Solomon and spoke with him of all that was in her heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:2
verses.text: And Solomon told her all her questions. And there was nothing hidden from Solomon which he did not tell her.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:3
verses.text: And the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:4
verses.text: and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers and their apparel, and his burnt offerings that he offered up in the house of the LORD, there was no more spirit in her.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:5
verses.text: And she said to the king, The word that I heard in my own land of your acts and of your wisdom is true.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:6
verses.text: But I did not believe their words until I came, and my eyes had seen. And behold, the one half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told me. You are greater than the fame which I heard.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:7
verses.text: Happy <hi>are</hi> your men, and happy are these your servants who stand always before you and hear your wisdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:8
verses.text: Blessed <hi>be</hi> the LORD your God, who delighted in you to set you on His throne to <hi>be</hi> king for the LORD your God. Because your God loved Israel to establish them forever, therefore He made you king over them to do judgment and justice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:9
verses.text: And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and an abundance of spices, and precious stones. And there has not been any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave king Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:10
verses.text: And also the servants of Hiram, and the servants of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum trees and precious stones.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:11
verses.text: And the king made terraces to the house of the LORD with the algum trees, and terraces to the king's palace, and lyres and harps for singers. And there were none such seen before in the land of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:12
verses.text: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides what she had brought to the king. And she returned and went away to her own land, she and her servants.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:13
verses.text: And the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:14
verses.text: besides <hi>that</hi> from the traders, and that the merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:15
verses.text: And king Solomon made two hundred targets <hi>of</hi> beaten gold. Six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:16
verses.text: And he <hi>made</hi> three hundred shields <hi>of</hi> beaten gold. Three hundred <hi>shekels</hi> of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:17
verses.text: And the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:18
verses.text: And there <hi>were</hi> six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold. fastened to the throne. And there <hi>were</hi> stays on each <hi>side</hi> of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:19
verses.text: And twelve lions stood there on the one <hi>side</hi>, and on the other, on the six steps. There was not the like made in any kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:20
verses.text: And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon <hi>were</hi> of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon <hi>were</hi> of pure gold. None <hi>were</hi> of silver. It was not prized in the days of Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:21
verses.text: For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:22
verses.text: And king Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:23
verses.text: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom that God had put in his heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:24
verses.text: And they each brought his present, vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and clothing, weapons, and spices, horses, and mules, a ration year by year.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:25
verses.text: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he put in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:26
verses.text: And he reigned over all the kings from the River even to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:27
verses.text: And the king made silver in Jerusalem like stones, and he made cedar trees as the sycamore trees in the low plains.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:28
verses.text: And they brought to Solomon horses out of Egypt and out of all lands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:29
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah of Shiloh, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:30
verses.text: And Solomon reigned forty years in Jerusalem over all Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:31
verses.text: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:1
verses.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem. For all Israel had come <hi>to</hi> Shechem to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:2
verses.text: And it happened when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who <hi>was</hi> in Egypt where he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard <hi>it</hi>, Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:3
verses.text: And they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:4
verses.text: Your father made our yoke heavy. And now lighten the heavy service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, and we will serve you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:5
verses.text: And he said to them, Come again to me after three days. And the people departed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:6
verses.text: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What advice do you give <hi>me</hi> to return answer to this people?

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:7
verses.text: And they spoke to him saying, If you are kind to this people and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:8
verses.text: But he departed from the advice which the old men gave him and listened to the young men who were brought up with him, who stood before him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:9
verses.text: And he said to them, What advice do you give that we may return answer to this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Lighten the yoke which your father put on us?

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:10
verses.text: And the young men who were brought up with him spoke to him saying, In this way shall you answer the people who spoke to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten our yoke, this you shall say to them, My little <hi> finger</hi> shall be thicker than my father's loins.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:11
verses.text: And now my father put a heavy yoke on you, and I will surely add to your yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I <hi>will chastise you</hi> with scorpions.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:12
verses.text: And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day as the king commanded, saying, Come again to me on the third day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:13
verses.text: And the king answered them roughly. And king Rehoboam departed from the advice of the old men,

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:14
verses.text: and answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father chastised you with whips, but I <hi>will chastise you</hi> with scorpions.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:15
verses.text: And the king did not listen to the people, for <hi>the</hi> revolution was from God so that the LORD might perform His word which He spoke by the hand of Ahijah of Shiloh to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:16
verses.text: And all Israel <hi>saw</hi> that the king would not listen to them, and the people answered the king saying, What part do we have in David? And we have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to your tents, O Israel! Now, David, see to your own house. And all Israel went to their tents.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:17
verses.text: <hi> As for</hi> the sons of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:18
verses.text: And king Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who <hi>was</hi> over the forced labor. And the sons of Israel stoned him with stones so that he died. But king Rehoboam <hi>was</hi> warned to get up into <hi>his</hi> chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:19
verses.text: And Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:1
verses.text: And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and gathered a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors from the house of Judah, to fight against Israel, so that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:2
verses.text: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:3
verses.text: Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:4
verses.text: So says the LORD, You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers. Let every man return to his house. For this thing is done by Me. And they obeyed the words of the LORD, and returned from going against Jeroboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:5
verses.text: And Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built cities for defense in Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:6
verses.text: And he built Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:7
verses.text: and Beth-zur, and Shoco, and Adullam,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:8
verses.text: and Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:9
verses.text: and Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:10
verses.text: and Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which <hi>are</hi> in Judah and in Benjamin, fortified cities.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:11
verses.text: And he fortified the strongholds and put commanders in them, and stores of food, and of oil and wine.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:12
verses.text: And <hi>he put</hi> in each separate city shields and spears, and made them very strong, and Judah and Benjamin were his.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:13
verses.text: And the priests and the Levites in all Israel presented themselves to him out of all their borders.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:14
verses.text: For the Levites left their open lands and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem. For Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priests' office to the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:15
verses.text: And he ordained priests for himself for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:16
verses.text: And after them, those who gave their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel, out of all the tribes of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:17
verses.text: And they made the kingdom of Judah stronger, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong for three years. For three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:18
verses.text: And Rehoboam took Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David as a wife for himself, <hi>and</hi> Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:19
verses.text: who bore him sons, Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:20
verses.text: And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom, who bore Abijah to him, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:21
verses.text: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines (for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and had twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters).

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:22
verses.text: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, <hi>to be</hi> ruler among his brothers, in order to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:23
verses.text: And he dealt wisely and dispersed all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities. And he gave them food in abundance. And he demanded many wives.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:1
verses.text: And it happened when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had made himself strong, he departed from the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:2
verses.text: And it happened in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the LORD

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:3
verses.text: with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. And the people who came with him out of Egypt <hi>were</hi> without number: Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:4
verses.text: And he took the fortified cities in Judah, and came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:5
verses.text: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam, and <hi>to</hi> the rulers of Judah who were gathered to Jerusalem because of Shishak. And <hi>he</hi> said to them, So says the LORD, You have forsaken Me, and therefore I also have left you in the hand of Shishak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:6
verses.text: And the rulers of Israel and the king humbled themselves. And they said, The LORD <hi>is</hi> righteous.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:7
verses.text: And when the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will give them some deliverance. And My wrath shall not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:8
verses.text: But they shall be his servants, so that they may know My service, and the service of the kings of the countries.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:9
verses.text: And Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took away the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house. He took all. And he carried away the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:10
verses.text: In place of these king Rehoboam made shields of bronze, and gave <hi>them</hi> into the hands of the chief of the guard who kept the entrance of the king's house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:11
verses.text: And when the king entered into the house of the LORD, the guard came and carried them and brought them again into the guardroom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:12
verses.text: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the LORD turned from him so that He would not destroy <hi>him</hi> altogether. And also things went well in Judah.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:13
verses.text: And king Rehoboam strengthened himself at Jerusalem, and reigned. For Rehoboam <hi>was</hi> forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Naamah the Ammonitess.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:14
verses.text: And he did the evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:15
verses.text: And the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And the wars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam <hi>lasted</hi> all their days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:16
verses.text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David. And his son Abijah reigned in his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:1
verses.text: And in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam Abijah began to reign over Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:2
verses.text: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also <hi>was</hi> Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:3
verses.text: And Abijah set the battle in order with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men. Jeroboam also set the battle in order against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty men of valor.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:4
verses.text: And Abijah stood up on mount Zemaraim, in the hills of Ephraim, and said, Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:5
verses.text: Should you not know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:6
verses.text: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, has risen up and has rebelled against his lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:7
verses.text: And there are gathered to him vain men, the sons of Belial, and have made themselves strong against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, and Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted and could not withstand them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:8
verses.text: And now you think to withstand the kingdom of the LORD in the hands of the sons of David. And you <hi>are</hi> a great multitude, and there <hi>are</hi> with you golden calves which Jeroboam made you for gods.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:9
verses.text: Have you not cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made priests to yourselves like the peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams, he may be a priest of <hi>those who are</hi> no gods.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:10
verses.text: But as for us, Jehovah <hi>is</hi> our God, and we have not forsaken Him. And the priests who minister to the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in the work.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:11
verses.text: And they burn to the Lord every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense, and the showbread on the pure table, and the lampstand of gold with its lamps, to burn every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God. But you have forsaken Him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:12
verses.text: And behold, God Himself <hi>is</hi> with us as Commander, and His priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O sons of Israel, do not fight against the LORD God of your fathers, for you shall not prosper!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:13
verses.text: But Jeroboam caused an ambush to come around behind them, so that they were in front of Judah, and the ambush <hi>was</hi> behind them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:14
verses.text: And Judah turned, and, behold, the battle <hi>was</hi> before and behind. And they cried to the LORD, and the priests sounded with the trumpets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:15
verses.text: And the men of Judah shouted. And it happened as the men of Judah shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:16
verses.text: And the sons of Israel fled before Judah. And God delivered them into their hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:17
verses.text: And Abijah and his people killed them with a great slaughter. And there fell down dead five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:18
verses.text: And the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah won because they relied on the LORD God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:19
verses.text: And Abijah pursued Jeroboam, and took cities from him, Bethel with its villages, and Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephrain with its villages.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:20
verses.text: And Jeroboam did not recover strength again <hi>in</hi> the days of Abijah. And the LORD struck him and he died.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:21
verses.text: And Abijah became mighty, and married fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:22
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and his sayings, <hi>are</hi> written in the inquiry of the prophet Iddo.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:1
verses.text: And Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And his son Asa reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet ten years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:2
verses.text: And Asa did the good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:3
verses.text: For he took away the altars of the strange <hi>gods</hi>, and the high places, and broke down the images, and cut down the Asherahs.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:4
verses.text: And he commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:5
verses.text: He also took out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images. And the kingdom was quiet before him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:6
verses.text: And he built fortified cities in Judah. For the land had rest, and he had no war in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:7
verses.text: And he said to Judah, Let us build these cities and make walls around <hi>them</hi>, and towers, gates and bars, while the land <hi>is</hi> still before us. Because we have sought the LORD our God, we have sought, and He has given us rest on every side. And they built and were blessed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:8
verses.text: And Asa had an army which bore bucklers and spears, three hundred thousand out of Judah. And out of Benjamin there <hi>were</hi> two hundred and eighty thousand who bore shields and drew bows; all these mighty men of valor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:9
verses.text: And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men, and three hundred chariots. And he came to Mareshah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:10
verses.text: And Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in order in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:11
verses.text: And Asa cried to the LORD his God and said, LORD, <hi>it is</hi> nothing with You to help, whether with many or with him who has no power. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rest on You, and in Your name we go against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God. Do not let man prevail against You.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:12
verses.text: And the LORD struck the Cushites before Asa and before Judah. And the Cushites fled.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:13
verses.text: And Asa and the people with him pursued them to Gerar. And the Cushites fell, for none was left alive of them. For they were destroyed before the LORD and before His army. And they carried away very much plunder.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:14
verses.text: And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the LORD came on them. And they plundered all the cities, for there was very much plunder in them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:15
verses.text: And they struck the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance and returned to Jerusalem.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:1
verses.text: And the Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:2
verses.text: And he went out to meet Asa, and said to him, Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD <hi>is</hi> with you while you are with Him. And if you seek Him, He will be found by you. But if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:3
verses.text: And for a long time Israel <hi>had been</hi> without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:4
verses.text: And when they turned in their trouble to the LORD God of Israel, and sought Him, He was found by them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:5
verses.text: And in those times <hi>there was</hi> no peace to him who went out, nor to him who came in, but great tumult <hi>was</hi> on all the people of the lands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:6
verses.text: And nation was beaten by nation, and city by city, for God troubled them with every distress.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:7
verses.text: But you be strong and do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:8
verses.text: And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim. And he renewed the altar of the LORD before the porch of the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:9
verses.text: And <hi>he</hi> gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon. For they fell to him out of Israel in great numbers, when they saw that the LORD his God <hi>was</hi> with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:10
verses.text: And they gathered to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:11
verses.text: And <hi>they</hi> offered to the LORD in that day part of the plunder which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:12
verses.text: And they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul,

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:13
verses.text: and that whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:14
verses.text: And they swore to the LORD with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with ram's horns.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:15
verses.text: And all Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought Him with their whole desire. And He was found by them, and the LORD gave them rest all around.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:16
verses.text: And also <hi>as to</hi> Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from <hi>being</hi> queen mother, because she had made an idol in a grove. And Asa cut down her idol and stamped it and burned <hi>it</hi> at the brook Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:17
verses.text: But the high places were not taken away out of Israel. But the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:18
verses.text: And he brought into the house of God the things which his father had dedicated, and which he himself had dedicated, silver and gold and vessels.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:19
verses.text: And there was no war to the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:1
verses.text: In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, so that he might let no one go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:2
verses.text: And Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the king's house and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who lived at Damascus, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:3
verses.text: A treaty between you and me, as <hi>there was</hi> between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he may depart from me.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:4
verses.text: And Ben-hadad listened to king Asa, and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. And they struck Ijon and Dan, and Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:5
verses.text: And it happened when Baasha heard, he left off building Ramah, and let his work stop.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:6
verses.text: And Asa the king took all Judah. And they carried away the stones of Ramah, and timber with which Baasha was building. And he built with it Geba and Mizpah.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:7
verses.text: And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on the LORD your God, therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped out of your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:8
verses.text: Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a huge army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet, because you relied on the LORD, he delivered them into your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:9
verses.text: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro in all the whole earth to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart <hi>is</hi> perfect toward Him. You have done foolishly in this; therefore from now on you shall have wars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:10
verses.text: And Asa was angry with the seer and put him in a prison-house. For <hi>he was</hi> in a rage with him because of this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:11
verses.text: And behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they <hi>are</hi> written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:12
verses.text: And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa <hi>was</hi> diseased in his feet, until his disease <hi>was</hi> very grievous. Yet in his disease he did not seek to the LORD, but to the physicians.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:13
verses.text: And Asa slept with his fathers and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:14
verses.text: And they buried him in his own tomb, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odors and kinds <hi>of spices</hi> prepared by the perfumers art. And they made a very great burning for him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:1
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place. And he made himself strong against Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:2
verses.text: And <hi>he</hi> placed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set troops in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim which Asa his father had taken.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:3
verses.text: And the LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David and did not seek to Baals.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:4
verses.text: But he looked to the God of his father, and walked in His commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:5
verses.text: And the LORD made the kingdom sure in his hand. And all Judah brought presents to Jehoshaphat. And he had great riches and honor.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:6
verses.text: And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD. And he took away the high places and Asherahs out of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:7
verses.text: And in the third year of his reign he sent to his rulers, to Benhail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:8
verses.text: And with them <hi>he sent</hi> Levites, Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, Levites. And with them he sent Elishama and Jehoram the priests.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:9
verses.text: And they taught in Judah and <hi>had</hi> the book of the law of the LORD with them, and went around throughout all the cities of Judah and taught the people.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:10
verses.text: And the fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:11
verses.text: And from the Philistines they brought Jehoshaphat presents and silver for tribute. Also the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand and seven hundred rams, and seven thousand and seven hundred he-goats.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:12
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat became exceedingly great. And he built fortresses in Judah, and store cities.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:13
verses.text: And he had much business in the cities of Judah. And the men of war, mighty men of valor, <hi>were</hi> in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:14
verses.text: And these <hi>were</hi> their numbers, for the house of their fathers from Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the chief, and with him were three hundred thousand mighty men of valor.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:15
verses.text: And on his hand, Jehohanan the chief, and with him were two hundred and eighty thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:16
verses.text: And on his hand, Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:17
verses.text: And from Benjamin <hi>was</hi> Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:18
verses.text: And on his hand, Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand ready and prepared for war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:19
verses.text: These waited on the king, besides <hi>those</hi> whom the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:1
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he contracted a marriage with Ahab.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:2
verses.text: And after <hi>some</hi> years <hi>he</hi> went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen in abundance for him, and for the people that were with him. And he persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:3
verses.text: And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead? And he answered him, I <hi>am</hi> as you, and my people are as your people, and <hi>we</hi> with you in the war.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:4
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Please inquire at the word of the LORD today.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:5
verses.text: And the king of Israel gathered four hundred men of the prophets and said to them, Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I wait? And they said, Go up, for God will deliver <hi>it</hi> into the king's hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:6
verses.text: But Jehoshaphat said, <hi>Is there</hi> not a prophet of Jehovah here besides, so that we might ask of Him?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:7
verses.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, <hi>There is</hi> yet one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD. But I hate him, for he never prophesied good to me, but always evil. The same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:8
verses.text: And the king of Israel called to a certain eunuch and said, Bring quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:9
verses.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat each of them on his throne, clothed in robes. And <hi>they</hi> sat in a grain floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria. And all the prophets prophesied before them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:10
verses.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah had made horns of iron for himself. And he said, And says the LORD, With these you shall push Syria until they are crushed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:11
verses.text: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead and be blessed. For the LORD shall deliver <hi>it</hi> into the king's hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:12
verses.text: And the messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets <hi>declare</hi> good to the king with one Mouth, and please let your word be like one of theirs, and speak good.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:13
verses.text: And Micaiah said, <hi>As</hi> the Lord lives, even what my God says, that I will speak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:14
verses.text: And he came to the king. And the king said to him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I wait? And he said, Go up and be blessed. And they shall be delivered into your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:15
verses.text: And the king said to him, How many times shall I warn you that you say nothing but the truth to me in the name of Jehovah?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:16
verses.text: And he said, I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that <hi>have</hi> no shepherd. And the LORD said, These <hi>have</hi> no master; let them return, each man to his own house in peace.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:17
verses.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell you he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:18
verses.text: Again he said, And hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of Heaven were standing on His right hand and <hi>on</hi> His left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:19
verses.text: And the LORD said, Who shall tempt Ahab king of Israel so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one spoke saying in one way, and another saying in another way.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:20
verses.text: And a spirit came out and stood before the LORD and said, I will tempt him. And the LORD said, With what?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:21
verses.text: And he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And <hi>the LORD</hi> said, You shall tempt him, and you are able. Go out and do so.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:22
verses.text: And now behold, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets, and the LORD has spoken evil against you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:23
verses.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek. And he said, Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go from me to speak to you?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:24
verses.text: And Micaiah said, Behold, you shall see on that day when you shall go into an inner room to hide yourself.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:25
verses.text: And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:26
verses.text: And you shall say, So says the king, Put this <hi>fellow</hi> in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction until I return in peace.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:27
verses.text: And Micaiah said, If you certainly return in peace, <hi>then</hi> the LORD has not spoken by me. And he said, Listen, all you people.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:28
verses.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:29
verses.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself and will go to the battle. But you put on your robes. And the king of Israel disguised himself. And they went to the battle.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:30
verses.text: And the king of Syria had commanded the commanders of the chariots with him, saying, Do not fight with small or great, but only with the king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:31
verses.text: And it happened when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, It <hi>is</hi> the king of Israel. And they surrounded him to fight. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. And God moved them <hi>to leave</hi> him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:32
verses.text: For it happened when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back again from pursuing him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:33
verses.text: And a <hi>certain</hi> man drew a bow at random, and struck the king of Israel between the joinings and the breastplate. And he said to the charioteer, Turn your hand, and you shall bring me out of the army, for I am wounded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:34
verses.text: And the battle increased that day; and the king of Israel was made to stand up in <hi>his</hi> chariot against the Syrians until the evening. And about the time of the sunset he died.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:1
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:2
verses.text: And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him. And he said to king Jehoshaphat, Should you help the ungodly and love those who hate the LORD? And by this <hi>bring</hi> wrath on you from before the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:3
verses.text: But there are good things found in you, in that you have taken away the Asherahs out of the land and have prepared your heart to seek God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:4
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem. And he went out again among the people from Beer-sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD God of their fathers.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:5
verses.text: And he set judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:6
verses.text: And he said to the judges, Take heed what you do. For you do not judge for man, but for the LORD, who <hi>is</hi> with you in the judgment.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:7
verses.text: And now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Be careful and act wisely, for <hi>there is</hi> no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:8
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat set some of the Levites and <hi>of</hi> the priests and of the chief of the fathers of Israel in Jerusalem for the judgment of the LORD, and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:9
verses.text: And he charged them, saying, And you shall act in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a perfect heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:10
verses.text: And whatever cause shall come to you from your brothers that dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments, you shall even warn them so that they do not sin against the LORD, and wrath come on you and your brothers. Do this and you shall not sin.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:11
verses.text: And behold, Amariah the chief priest <hi>is</hi> over you in all matters of the LORD. And Zebadiah the son of Ishmael is the ruler of the house of Judah for all the king's matters. Also the Levites <hi>shall be</hi> officers before you. Take courage and act, and the LORD shall be with the good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:1
verses.text: And it happened after this the sons of Moab, and the sons of Ammon came in, and with them <hi>others</hi> besides the Ammonites, to battle against Jehoshaphat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:2
verses.text: And they came in and spoke to Jehoshaphat, saying, A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea on this side of Syria. And behold, they <hi>are</hi> in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:3
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat feared and set himself to seek the LORD, and called for a fast throughout all Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:4
verses.text: And Judah gathered themselves to ask of the LORD. Even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:5
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:6
verses.text: and said, O LORD God of our Fathers, <hi>are</hi> You not God in Heaven? And do You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? And <hi>is there</hi> power and might in Your hand, so that none is able to withstand You?

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:7
verses.text: <hi> Are</hi> You not our God? Did <hi>You</hi> not drive out the people of this land before Israel, and give it to the seed of Your friend Abraham forever?

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:8
verses.text: And they lived in it. And they have built You a temple in it for Your name, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:9
verses.text: If evil comes on us, <hi>whether</hi> the sword, judgment, or plague, or famine, and we stand before this house and in Your presence (for Your name <hi>is</hi> in this house) and cry to You in our affliction, then You will hear and help.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:10
verses.text: And now, behold, the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom You would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them and did not destroy them,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:11
verses.text: behold, they reward us by coming to cast us out of Your possession, which You have given us to inherit.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:12
verses.text: O our God, will You not judge them? For we have no might against this great company which comes against us. Nor do we know what to do, but our eyes <hi>are</hi> on You.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:13
verses.text: And all Judah stood before the LORD with their little ones, their wives, and their sons.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:14
verses.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the congregation.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:15
verses.text: And he said, Listen, all Judah, and you people of Jerusalem, and king Jehoshaphat! So says the LORD to you, Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude. For the battle <hi>is</hi> not yours, but God's.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:16
verses.text: Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz. And you shall find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:17
verses.text: You shall not fight in this <hi>battle</hi>. Set yourselves and stand, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear nor be dismayed. Tomorrow go out against them, for the LORD <hi>will be</hi> with you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:18
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat bowed his face to the ground. And all Judah and the people of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:19
verses.text: And the Levites, of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korhites, stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice on high.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:20
verses.text: And they rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. And as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and you people of Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, and so you shall be established. Believe His prophets, and so you shall be blessed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:21
verses.text: And he consulted with the people, and he appointed singers to the LORD and praisers to praise the beauty of holiness as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the LORD, for His mercy <hi>endures</hi> forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:22
verses.text: And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, who had come against Judah. And they were beaten.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:23
verses.text: For the sons of Ammon and Moab stood up against the people of mount Seir to completely kill and destroy. And when they had made an end of the people of Seir, everyone helped to destroy another.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:24
verses.text: And when Judah came to the watchtower in the wilderness, they looked at the multitude. And behold! They <hi>were</hi> dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:25
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their plunder, they found among them in abundance both riches and precious jewels in great number with the dead bodies, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away. And they were three days in gathering of the plunder, it was so much.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:26
verses.text: And on the fourth day they gathered themselves in the Valley of Blessing. For there they blessed the LORD. And the name of the same place was called the Valley of Blessing until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:27
verses.text: And they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in front of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy. For the LORD had made them to rejoice over their enemies.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:28
verses.text: And they came into Jerusalem with harps and with lyres, and with trumpets to the house of the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:29
verses.text: And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of <hi>those</hi> countries, when they had heard that the LORD fought against the enemies of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:30
verses.text: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet. For his God gave him rest round about.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:31
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah, thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name <hi>was</hi> Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:32
verses.text: And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and did not depart from it, doing the right in the sight of the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:33
verses.text: But, the high places were not taken away, for as yet the people had not prepared their hearts to the God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:34
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, behold, they <hi>are</hi> written in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, which <hi>were</hi> taken up in the /Book of the Kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:35
verses.text: And after this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel; he did wickedly to do so.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:36
verses.text: And he joined himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish. And they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:37
verses.text: And Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works. And the ships were broken so that they were not able to go to Tarshish.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:1
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:2
verses.text: And he had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat, Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah. All these <hi>were</hi> the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:3
verses.text: And their father gave them great gifts of silver and of gold and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah. But the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, because he <hi>was</hi> the first-born.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:4
verses.text: And when Jehoram had risen up to the kingdom of his father, he made himself strong and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also <hi>many</hi> of the rulers of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:5
verses.text: Jehoram <hi>was</hi> thirty-two years old when he began to reign. And he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:6
verses.text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like the house of Ahab for he had the daughter of Ahab for a wife. And he did the evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:7
verses.text: And the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that He had made with David, and as He promised to give a light to him and to his sons forever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:8
verses.text: In his days Edom revolted from under the rule of Judah, and made themselves a king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:9
verses.text: And Jehoram went forth with his rulers, and all his chariots with him. And he rose up by night and struck the Edomites who surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:10
verses.text: And the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah until this day. The same time Libnah revolted from under his hand, because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:11
verses.text: Besides he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the people of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and led astray Judah.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:12
