verses.text: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:3
verses.text: And Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and begged him with tears to put away the evil of Haman the Agagite, and his plot which he had plotted against the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:4
verses.text: Then the king held out the golden scepter toward Esther. And Esther arose and stood before the king,

verses.name: Esther 8:5
verses.text: and said, If it please the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and if the thing <hi>is</hi> right before the king, and if I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to bring back the documents (a sly plan by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite) which he wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.

verses.name: Esther 8:6
verses.text: For how can I bear to see the evil that shall come on my people? Or how can I endure to see the slaughter of my kindred?

verses.name: Esther 8:7
verses.text: And king Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and have hanged him on the wooden <hi>gallows</hi>, because he laid his hand on the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:8
verses.text: And you write for the Jews as it pleases you, in the king's name, and seal <hi>it</hi> with the king's ring. For the writing which is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring, no man may turn back.

verses.name: Esther 8:9
verses.text: Then the king's scribes were called at that time in the third month, the month Sivan, on the twenty-third of it. And it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the lieutenants and the governors and rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to the writing of it, and to every people in their writing, and to the Jews according to their writing and according to their language.

verses.name: Esther 8:10
verses.text: And he wrote in the name of king Ahasuerus and sealed <hi>it</hi> with the king's ring. And he sent letters by riders on horseback, riders on royal steeds, stallions, even sons of mares.

verses.name: Esther 8:11
verses.text: In <hi>them</hi> the king granted the Jews in every city to gather themselves, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to kill and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province who desired to attack them, little ones and women, and <hi>to take</hi> what they owned for a prize,

verses.name: Esther 8:12
verses.text: on one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which <hi>is</hi> the month Adar.

verses.name: Esther 8:13
verses.text: The copy of the writing for a command to be given in every province <hi>was</hi> announced to all people, even that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

verses.name: Esther 8:14
verses.text: The runners, riders on stallions, royal steeds, went out, being hurried and pressed on by the king's command. And the order was given at Shushan the palace.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:15
verses.text: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown <hi>of</hi> gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple. And the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.

verses.name: Esther 8:16
verses.text: The Jews had light and gladness and joy and honor.

verses.name: Esther 8:17
verses.text: And in every province, and in every city where the king's command and his order came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell on them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:1
verses.text: And in the twelfth month, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's command and his order came to be done, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them; though it was turned around, so that the Jews had rule over the ones who hated them.

verses.name: Esther 9:2
verses.text: The Jews gathered themselves in their cities throughout all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, in order to lay hand on any who sought their harm. And no man could withstand them, for the fear of them fell on all people.

verses.name: Esther 9:3
verses.text: And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants and the governors and officers of the king helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai fell on them.

verses.name: Esther 9:4
verses.text: For Mordecai <hi>was</hi> great in the house of the king, and his fame went throughout all the provinces. For this man Mordecai was going on and growing greater.

verses.name: Esther 9:5
verses.text: And the Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would to those who hated them.

verses.name: Esther 9:6
verses.text: And in Shushan the palace the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.

verses.name: Esther 9:7
verses.text: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:8
verses.text: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:9
verses.text: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:10
verses.text: they killed the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

verses.name: Esther 9:11
verses.text: On that day the number of those who were killed in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.

verses.name: Esther 9:12
verses.text: And the king said to Esther the queen, The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? And what <hi>is</hi> your petition, that it may be granted you? Or what further request do you have? And it shall be done.

verses.name: Esther 9:13
verses.text: Then Esther said, If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews in Shushan to do tomorrow also according to this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the wooden <hi>gallows</hi>.

verses.name: Esther 9:14
verses.text: And the king commanded it to be done. And the order was given at Shushan, and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

verses.name: Esther 9:15
verses.text: For the Jews in Shushan gathered themselves on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men at Shushan. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

verses.name: Esther 9:16
verses.text: But the rest of the Jews in the king's provinces gathered themselves and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of their foes. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

verses.name: Esther 9:17
verses.text: And on the thirteenth day of the month Adar, and on the fourteenth day of the same, they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.name: Esther 9:18
verses.text: But the Jews at Shushan gathered on the thirteenth of it and on the fourteenth of it. And on the fifteenth of the same, they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.name: Esther 9:19
verses.text: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who lived in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar <hi>a day of</hi> gladness and feasting, and a good day, and <hi>a day of</hi> sending portions to one another.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:20
verses.text: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, near and far,

verses.name: Esther 9:21
verses.text: to establish among them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

verses.name: Esther 9:22
verses.text: as the days in which the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions to one another, and gifts to the poor.

verses.name: Esther 9:23
verses.text: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written to them

verses.name: Esther 9:24
verses.text: because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, the lot, to finish them and to destroy them.

verses.name: Esther 9:25
verses.text: But when <hi>Esther</hi> came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plot which he had plotted against the Jews should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the wooden <hi>gallows</hi>.

verses.name: Esther 9:26
verses.text: Therefore, they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore, for all the words of this letter, and which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come to them,

verses.name: Esther 9:27
verses.text: the Jews ordained, and took on them and on their seed, and on all such as joined themselves to them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their time every year

verses.name: Esther 9:28
verses.text: and <hi>that</hi> these days <hi>should be</hi> remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city and these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

verses.name: Esther 9:29
verses.text: And Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

verses.name: Esther 9:30
verses.text: And he sent the letters to all the Jews, to the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, <hi>with</hi> words of peace and truth,

verses.name: Esther 9:31
verses.text: in order to confirm these days of Purim in their <hi>set</hi> times, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had ordered them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed the matters of the fastings and of their cry.

verses.name: Esther 9:32
verses.text: And the order of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim. And it was written in the book.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Esther 10:1
verses.text: And king Ahasuerus laid a tax on the land and <hi>on</hi> the isles of the sea.

verses.name: Esther 10:2
verses.text: And all the acts of his power and of might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, with which the king made him great, <hi>are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

verses.name: Esther 10:3
verses.text: For Mordecai the Jew <hi>was</hi> next to king Ahasuerus and great among the Jews, and pleasing to the multitude of his brothers, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 1:1
verses.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name <hi>was</hi> Job. And that man was perfect and upright, and one who feared God and turned aside from evil.

verses.name: Job 1:2
verses.text: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

verses.name: Job 1:3
verses.text: And his possessions were seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household, so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 1:4
verses.text: And his sons went and feasted in the house of each one on his day. And they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

verses.name: Job 1:5
verses.text: And when they had gone around the day of feasting, Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning and offered burnt offerings <hi>according to</hi> the number of them all. For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts. So Job did always.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 1:6
verses.text: And a day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. And Satan also came among them.

verses.name: Job 1:7
verses.text: And the LORD said to Satan, From where do you come? Then Satan answered the LORD and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

verses.name: Job 1:8
verses.text: And the LORD said to Satan, Have you set your heart against My servant Job, because <hi>there is</hi> none like him in the earth, a perfect and upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil?

verses.name: Job 1:9
verses.text: And Satan answered the LORD and said, Does Job fear God for nothing?

verses.name: Job 1:10
verses.text: Have You not made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have increased in the land.

verses.name: Job 1:11
verses.text: But put forth Your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will curse You to Your face.

verses.name: Job 1:12
verses.text: And the LORD said to Satan, Behold, all that he has <hi>is</hi> in your power. Only do not lay your hand upon him. And Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 1:13
verses.text: And a day came when his sons and his daughters <hi>were</hi> eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.

verses.name: Job 1:14
verses.text: And there came a messenger to Job and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them.

verses.name: Job 1:15
verses.text: And the Sabeans fell <hi>on</hi> and took them away. Yea, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

verses.name: Job 1:16
verses.text: While he <hi>was</hi> still speaking, there also came <hi>another</hi> and said, The fire of God has fallen from the heavens and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and destroyed them. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

verses.name: Job 1:17
verses.text: While he <hi>was</hi> still speaking, there also came <hi>another</hi> and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands and swooped down upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and have killed the servants with the edge of the sword. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

verses.name: Job 1:18
verses.text: While he <hi>was</hi> still speaking, there also came another and said, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.

verses.name: Job 1:19
verses.text: And, behold, a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 1:20
verses.text: And Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground and worshiped.

verses.name: Job 1:21
verses.text: And he said, I came naked out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed <hi>be</hi> the name of the LORD.

verses.name: Job 1:22
verses.text: In all this Job did not sin, nor charge God foolishly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 2:1
verses.text: And it happened that a day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. And Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.

verses.name: Job 2:2
verses.text: And the LORD said to Satan, From where do you come? And Satan answered the LORD and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

verses.name: Job 2:3
verses.text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Have you set your heart on My servant Job, that <hi>there is</hi> none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil? And still he is keeping hold of his integrity, although you moved Me against him to destroy him without cause.

verses.name: Job 2:4
verses.text: And Satan answered the LORD and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man has he will give for his life.

verses.name: Job 2:5
verses.text: But indeed put forth Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse You to Your face.

verses.name: Job 2:6
verses.text: And the LORD said to Satan, Behold, he <hi>is</hi> in your hand, but save his life.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 2:7
verses.text: And Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

verses.name: Job 2:8
verses.text: And he took a broken piece of pottery to scrape himself with. And he sat down among the ashes.

verses.name: Job 2:9
verses.text: And his wife said to him, Do you still hold to your integrity? Curse God and die!

verses.name: Job 2:10
verses.text: But he said to her, You speak as one of the foolish ones speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this Job did not sin with his lips.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 2:11
verses.text: And Job's three friends heard <hi>of</hi> all this evil that had come upon him, and they each one came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. For they had met together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

verses.name: Job 2:12
verses.text: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and did not know him, they lifted up their voice and wept. And each one tore his robe, and <hi>they</hi> sprinkled dust upon their heads toward Heaven.

verses.name: Job 2:13
verses.text: And they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights. And no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that <hi>his</hi> grief was very great.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 3:1
verses.text: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.

verses.name: Job 3:2
verses.text: And Job spoke and said,

verses.name: Job 3:3
verses.text: Let the day perish in <hi>which</hi> I was born, and the night <hi>which</hi> said, A man-child is conceived.

verses.name: Job 3:4
verses.text: Let that day be darkness. Let not God look upon it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

verses.name: Job 3:5
verses.text: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it. Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let the blackness of the day terrify it.

verses.name: Job 3:6
verses.text: As <hi>for</hi> that night, let darkness seize upon it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year, Let it not come into the number of the months.

verses.name: Job 3:7
verses.text: Lo, let that night be barren; let no joyful voice come in it.

verses.name: Job 3:8
verses.text: Let those curse it who curse the day, who are ready to stir up Leviathan.

verses.name: Job 3:9
verses.text: Let the stars of its twilight be dark; let it look for light, but have none. Let it not see the eyelids of the dawn.

verses.name: Job 3:10
verses.text: For it did not shut up the doors of my <hi>mother's</hi> womb, nor hide sorrow from my eyes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 3:11
verses.text: Why did I not die from the womb, come from the womb and expire?

verses.name: Job 3:12
verses.text: Why did the knees go before me; or why the breasts, that I should suck?

verses.name: Job 3:13
verses.text: For now I should have lain still and been quiet; I should have slept. Then I would have been at rest

verses.name: Job 3:14
verses.text: with kings and wise men of the earth, who built ruins for themselves,

verses.name: Job 3:15
verses.text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;

verses.name: Job 3:16
verses.text: or as a hidden untimely birth I would not have been, like infants who did not see light.

verses.name: Job 3:17
verses.text: There the wicked cease <hi>from</hi> troubling, and there the weary are at rest;

verses.name: Job 3:18
verses.text: the prisoners are at rest together; they hear not the voice of the slave driver.

verses.name: Job 3:19
verses.text: The small and the great are there, and the slave <hi>is</hi> free from his master.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 3:20
verses.text: Why is light given to one who is in misery, and life to the bitter <hi>in</hi> soul,

verses.name: Job 3:21
verses.text: who is waiting for death, but <hi>it</hi> comes not; and dig for it more than <hi>for</hi> treasures?

verses.name: Job 3:22
verses.text: They are rejoicing to exultation. They are glad when they can find the grave.

verses.name: Job 3:23
verses.text: To a man whose way is hidden, God has made a hedge about him.

verses.name: Job 3:24
verses.text: For my sighing comes before I eat, and my groanings are poured out like the waters.

verses.name: Job 3:25
verses.text: For the thing which I greatly feared has come upon me, and that which I was afraid of has come to me.

verses.name: Job 3:26
verses.text: I was not in safety, nor did I have rest, nor was I quiet; yet trouble comes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 4:1
verses.text: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered:

verses.name: Job 4:2
verses.text: Shall one try a word with you, you <hi>who</hi> are weary? But who can hold back with words?

verses.name: Job 4:3
verses.text: Behold, you have instructed many, and you have made the weak hands strong.

verses.name: Job 4:4
verses.text: Your words have upheld him who was falling, and you have made strong the feeble knees.

verses.name: Job 4:5
verses.text: But now it has come upon you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

verses.name: Job 4:6
verses.text: <hi> Is</hi> not your reverence your hope? Is not your hope the uprightness of your ways?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 4:7
verses.text: Remember, please, who <hi>ever</hi> perished, being innocent? Or where were the righteous cut off?

verses.name: Job 4:8
verses.text: As I have seen, the ones who plow iniquity and sow wickedness reap the same.

verses.name: Job 4:9
verses.text: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of His nostrils they are destroyed.

verses.name: Job 4:10
verses.text: The roar of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

verses.name: Job 4:11
verses.text: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the strong lion's cubs are scattered abroad.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 4:12
verses.text: And a word was secretly brought to me, and my ear received a little of it.

verses.name: Job 4:13
verses.text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men,

verses.name: Job 4:14
verses.text: fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

verses.name: Job 4:15
verses.text: And a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.

verses.name: Job 4:16
verses.text: It stood still, but I could not tell the form of it. An image <hi>was</hi> before my eyes; silence; then I heard a voice,

verses.name: Job 4:17
verses.text: Shall mortal <hi>man</hi> be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

verses.name: Job 4:18
verses.text: Behold, He puts no trust in His servants, and His angels He charges with folly!

verses.name: Job 4:19
verses.text: How much less <hi>in</hi> those who live in houses of clay, whose foundation <hi>is</hi> in the dust, <hi>who</hi> are crushed before the moth?

verses.name: Job 4:20
verses.text: They are destroyed from morning till evening; they perish forever without anyone caring.

verses.name: Job 4:21
verses.text: Is not their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, but not with wisdom.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 5:1
verses.text: Call now, is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the saints will you turn?

verses.name: Job 5:2
verses.text: For vexation kills the fool, and envy slays the simple one.

verses.name: Job 5:3
verses.text: I have seen the fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling place.

verses.name: Job 5:4
verses.text: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, nor <hi>is there</hi> any to deliver <hi>them</hi>.

verses.name: Job 5:5
verses.text: Their harvest the hungry eats, and takes it even out of the thorns; and the snare swallows up their wealth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 5:6
verses.text: For affliction does not come forth from the dust, nor does trouble spring up out of the ground;

verses.name: Job 5:7
verses.text: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

verses.name: Job 5:8
verses.text: Truly, I would seek to God, and to God I would put my plea,

verses.name: Job 5:9
verses.text: <hi> Who is</hi> doing great things, even beyond searching; marvelous things without number,

verses.name: Job 5:10
verses.text: who gives rain on the earth and sends waters on the field,

verses.name: Job 5:11
verses.text: to set on high those who are low, so that those who mourn may be lifted up <hi>to</hi> safety;

verses.name: Job 5:12
verses.text: frustrating the plans of the crafty, nor did their hands do wisely.

verses.name: Job 5:13
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> takes the wise in their own craftiness; and the counsel of the wily is carried headlong.

verses.name: Job 5:14
verses.text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

verses.name: Job 5:15
verses.text: But He saves the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

verses.name: Job 5:16
verses.text: And there is hope for the weak, and injustice shuts her mouth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 5:17
verses.text: Behold, blessed <hi>is</hi> the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 5:18
verses.text: For He makes sore, and binds up; He wounds, and His hands make whole.

verses.name: Job 5:19
verses.text: He will deliver you in six troubles; yea, in seven no evil shall touch you.

verses.name: Job 5:20
verses.text: In famine He shall redeem you from death; and in war from the power of the sword.

verses.name: Job 5:21
verses.text: You shall be hidden from the whip of the tongue; neither shall you be afraid of robbery when it comes.

verses.name: Job 5:22
verses.text: At destruction and famine you shall laugh; neither shall you be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

verses.name: Job 5:23
verses.text: For you <hi>shall be</hi> in covenant with the stones of the field; and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.

verses.name: Job 5:24
verses.text: And you shall know that your tent <hi>is in</hi> peace; and you shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

verses.name: Job 5:25
verses.text: And <hi>you</hi> shall know that your seed <hi>will be</hi> numerous, and your offspring as the grass of the earth.

verses.name: Job 5:26
verses.text: You shall come to <hi>your</hi> grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

verses.name: Job 5:27
verses.text: Behold this: we have searched it; it is so. Hear it and know for yourself.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 6:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 6:2
verses.text: Oh that my grief were but weighed, and my ruin laid in the balances together!

verses.name: Job 6:3
verses.text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words have been rash.

verses.name: Job 6:4
verses.text: For the arrows of the Almighty <hi>are</hi> within me, their fury <hi>is</hi> drinking my spirit; the terrors of God are set against me.

verses.name: Job 6:5
verses.text: Does the wild ass bray <hi>when he has</hi> grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

verses.name: Job 6:6
verses.text: Can that which has no taste be eaten without salt? Or is there taste in the white of an egg?

verses.name: Job 6:7
verses.text: My soul refuses to touch them; they <hi>are</hi> sickening food to me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 6:8
verses.text: Oh that I might have my desire, and that God would grant the thing that I long for!

verses.name: Job 6:9
verses.text: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that He would loose His hand and cut me off!

verses.name: Job 6:10
verses.text: And it is yet my comfort; yea, I would rejoice in pain, though He did not spare me; for I have not hidden the words of the Holy One.

verses.name: Job 6:11
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> my strength, that I should hope? And what <hi>is</hi> my end, that I should be patient?

verses.name: Job 6:12
verses.text: <hi> Is</hi> my strength the strength of stones? Or <hi>is</hi> my flesh bronze?

verses.name: Job 6:13
verses.text: <hi> Is</hi> not my help in me? And is wisdom fully driven away from me?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 6:14
verses.text: To him who is afflicted, pity is <hi>due</hi> from his friend, but he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 6:15
verses.text: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a torrent; they pass away as the streams of torrents,

verses.name: Job 6:16
verses.text: <hi> torrents</hi> black from ice, in which the snow hides itself.

verses.name: Job 6:17
verses.text: When they become warm, they go away; when it is hot, they vanish out of their place.

verses.name: Job 6:18
verses.text: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing and are lost.

verses.name: Job 6:19
verses.text: The troops of Tema looked; the companies of Sheba hoped for them.

verses.name: Job 6:20
verses.text: They were ashamed because they had hoped; they came there and were ashamed.

verses.name: Job 6:21
verses.text: Surely now you are like them; you see <hi>my</hi> casting down, and are afraid.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 6:22
verses.text: Did I say, Give to me? or, Offer a bribe for me from your wealth;

verses.name: Job 6:23
verses.text: or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand; or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

verses.name: Job 6:24
verses.text: Teach me, and I will be silent; and cause me to understand where I have gone astray.

verses.name: Job 6:25
verses.text: Right words are powerful, but what does your arguing argue?

verses.name: Job 6:26
verses.text: Do you intend to criticize words, and the speeches of one who is hopeless, <hi>that are</hi> as wind?

verses.name: Job 6:27
verses.text: Yea, you cause <hi>anger</hi> to fall on the fatherless, and you dig <hi>a pit</hi> for your friend.

verses.name: Job 6:28
verses.text: And now, please look on me; for if I lie, <hi>it is</hi> before your face.

verses.name: Job 6:29
verses.text: Turn back, please let there be no sin; yea, return again, my righteousness <hi>is</hi> in this matter.

verses.name: Job 6:30
verses.text: Is there wrong in my tongue? Cannot my taste discern desirable things?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 7:1
verses.text: <hi> Is there</hi> not a warfare to man on earth? <hi>Are</hi> not his days also like the days of a hireling?

verses.name: Job 7:2
verses.text: As a servant earnestly desires the shadow, and as a hireling looks for his wages,

verses.name: Job 7:3
verses.text: so I am made to possess months of vanity, and weary nights are appointed to me.

verses.name: Job 7:4
verses.text: When I lie down, I say, When shall I rise? But the night is long, and I am full of tossing to and fro until the dawning of the day.

verses.name: Job 7:5
verses.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken and has run <hi>afresh</hi>.

verses.name: Job 7:6
verses.text: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are ended without hope.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 7:7
verses.text: Remember that my life <hi>is</hi> a breath; my eye shall no more see good.

verses.name: Job 7:8
verses.text: The eye of him who has seen me shall see me no <hi>more</hi>; Your eyes <hi>are</hi> on me, and I <hi>am</hi> gone.

verses.name: Job 7:9
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> the cloud falls and vanishes away, so he who goes down to the grave shall come up no <hi>more</hi>.

verses.name: Job 7:10
verses.text: He shall return no more to his house, nor shall his place know him any more.

verses.name: Job 7:11
verses.text: Therefore I will not hold my mouth; I will speak in the trouble of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.name: Job 7:12
verses.text: Am I like the sea, or a whale, that You set a watch over me?

verses.name: Job 7:13
verses.text: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint,

verses.name: Job 7:14
verses.text: then You scare me with dreams, and terrify me with visions;

verses.name: Job 7:15
verses.text: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my life.

verses.name: Job 7:16
verses.text: I despise <hi>them</hi>; I will not live always; let me alone, for my days <hi>are</hi> vanity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 7:17
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> man, that You should magnify him, and that You should set Your heart on him,

verses.name: Job 7:18
verses.text: and visit him every morning, trying him every moment?

verses.name: Job 7:19
verses.text: Until when will You look away from me, nor let me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

verses.name: Job 7:20
verses.text: I have sinned. What shall I do to You, O Watcher of men? Why have You set me as a target for You, so that I am a burden to myself?

verses.name: Job 7:21
verses.text: And why do You not pardon my transgression, and take away my iniquity? For now I shall sleep in the dust, and You shall seek me in the morning, but I <hi>shall</hi> not be.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 8:1
verses.text: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 8:2
verses.text: How long will you speak these things, since the words of your mouth <hi>are like</hi> a strong wind?

verses.name: Job 8:3
verses.text: Does God pervert judgment? Or does the Almighty pervert justice?

verses.name: Job 8:4
verses.text: If your sons have sinned against Him, and if He has cast them away for their transgression,

verses.name: Job 8:5
verses.text: if you would seek earnestly to God and make your prayer to the Almighty;

verses.name: Job 8:6
verses.text: if you <hi>were</hi> pure and upright, surely now He would awake for you, and make the dwelling-place of your righteousness blessed.

verses.name: Job 8:7
verses.text: And if your beginning was small, yet your end would greatly increase.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 8:8
verses.text: For please ask of the former age, and prepare yourself to the search of their fathers,

verses.name: Job 8:9
verses.text: for we <hi>are but of</hi> yesterday and know nothing, because our days on earth <hi>are</hi> a shadow.

verses.name: Job 8:10
verses.text: Shall they not teach you, <hi>and</hi> tell you, and speak words out of their heart?

verses.name: Job 8:11
verses.text: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the reed-grass grow without water?

verses.name: Job 8:12
verses.text: While it <hi>is</hi> yet in its greenness, and not cut down, it dries out before any <hi>other</hi> herb.

verses.name: Job 8:13
verses.text: So are the paths of all who forget God; and the hope of the ungodly shall perish.

verses.name: Job 8:14
verses.text: His hope shall be cut off, and his trust <hi>shall be</hi> in a spider's web.

verses.name: Job 8:15
verses.text: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand; he shall hold fast to it, but it shall not endure.

verses.name: Job 8:16
verses.text: He <hi>is</hi> moist before the sun, and his branches shoot forth in his garden.

verses.name: Job 8:17
verses.text: His roots are wrapped around the heap, <hi>and</hi> he sees the place of stones.

verses.name: Job 8:18
verses.text: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him: I have not seen you.

verses.name: Job 8:19
verses.text: Behold, this <hi>is</hi> the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 8:20
verses.text: Behold, God will not cast away the innocent, nor will He help the evildoers,

verses.name: Job 8:21
verses.text: until He fills your mouth with laughter, and your lips with rejoicing.

verses.name: Job 8:22
verses.text: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame; and the tent of the wicked <hi>shall be</hi> no more.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 9:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 9:2
verses.text: Truly I know <hi>it is so</hi>, but how can man be just with God?

verses.name: Job 9:3
verses.text: If he will argue with Him, he cannot answer Him one of a thousand.

verses.name: Job 9:4
verses.text: <hi> He is</hi> wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened <hi>himself</hi> against Him and been blessed;

verses.name: Job 9:5
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> who removes the mountains, and they know it not, when He overturns them in His anger;

verses.name: Job 9:6
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> who shakes the earth out of its place, and the pillars of it tremble;

verses.name: Job 9:7
verses.text: the one speaking to the sun, and it does not rise; and seals up the stars;

verses.name: Job 9:8
verses.text: who alone stretches out the heavens, and walks on the waves of the sea;

verses.name: Job 9:9
verses.text: who made the Bear, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;

verses.name: Job 9:10
verses.text: who is doing great things past finding out; yea, marvelous things without number?

verses.name: Job 9:11
verses.text: Behold! He goes by me, and I do not see <hi>Him</hi>; He passes on also, but I do not perceive Him.

verses.name: Job 9:12
verses.text: Behold, He takes away; who can turn Him back? Who will say to Him, What are You doing?

verses.name: Job 9:13
verses.text: God will not withdraw His anger; the helpers of pride stoop under Him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 9:14
verses.text: How much less shall I answer Him, <hi>and</hi> choose my arguments with Him?

verses.name: Job 9:15
verses.text: Whom, though I were righteous, <hi>yet</hi> I would not answer; I seek mercy for my judgment.

verses.name: Job 9:16
verses.text: If I had called and He had answered me, yet would I not believe that He had listened to my voice;

verses.name: Job 9:17
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> who breaks me with a tempest, and multiplies my wounds without cause;

verses.name: Job 9:18
verses.text: <hi> who</hi> will not allow me to take my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

verses.name: Job 9:19
verses.text: If <hi>I speak</hi> of strength, lo, <hi>He is</hi> mighty! And if of judgment, who shall set me a time?

verses.name: Job 9:20
verses.text: If I justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me; <hi>though</hi> I <hi>am</hi> perfect, He shall declare me perverse.

verses.name: Job 9:21
verses.text: <hi> Though</hi> I <hi>were</hi> perfect, yet I would not know my soul. I would despise my life.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 9:22
verses.text: It <hi>is</hi> One, therefore I said, He is consuming the perfect and the wicked.

verses.name: Job 9:23
verses.text: If the whip kills suddenly, He will mock at the calamity of the innocent.

verses.name: Job 9:24
verses.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covers the faces of its judges; if it <hi>is</hi> not <hi>He</hi>, then who <hi>is</hi> it?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 9:25
verses.text: Now my days are swifter than a runner; they flee away, they see no good.

verses.name: Job 9:26
verses.text: They have passed away like the swift ships; like the eagle who swoops on the prey.

verses.name: Job 9:27
verses.text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will depart from my heaviness and be of good cheer,

verses.name: Job 9:28
verses.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows; I know that You will not hold me innocent.

verses.name: Job 9:29
verses.text: I have been condemned; why then should I labor in vain?

verses.name: Job 9:30
verses.text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands ever so clean,

verses.name: Job 9:31
verses.text: yet You will plunge me into the ditch and my own clothes shall despise me.

verses.name: Job 9:32
verses.text: For <hi>He is</hi> not a man, as I <hi>am, that</hi> I should answer Him, <hi>that</hi> we should come together in judgment;

verses.name: Job 9:33
verses.text: there is no mediator between us, <hi>who</hi> might lay his hand on us both.

verses.name: Job 9:34
verses.text: Let Him take His rod away from me, and let not His fear make me afraid;

verses.name: Job 9:35
verses.text: <hi> then</hi> would I speak and not fear Him; for <hi>it is</hi> not so with me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 10:1
verses.text: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint on my self; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.name: Job 10:2
verses.text: I will say to God, Do not condemn me; make me know why You contend with me.

verses.name: Job 10:3
verses.text: Is <hi>it</hi> good to You that You should press down, that You should despise the work of Your hands, and shine on the counsel of the wicked?

verses.name: Job 10:4
verses.text: <hi> Have</hi> You eyes of flesh? Or do You see as a man sees?

verses.name: Job 10:5
verses.text: <hi> Are</hi> Your days like the days of man? <hi>Are</hi> Your years like man's days,

verses.name: Job 10:6
verses.text: that You seek out my iniquity, and search for my sin?

verses.name: Job 10:7
verses.text: You know that I am not wicked; and <hi>there is</hi> none who can deliver out of Your hand.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 10:8
verses.text: Your hands have made me and shaped me, together all around; yet You destroy me.

verses.name: Job 10:9
verses.text: Remember, I beseech You, that You have formed me as the clay; and will You bring me into the dust again?

verses.name: Job 10:10
verses.text: Have You not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

verses.name: Job 10:11
verses.text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and have fenced me with bones and sinews.

verses.name: Job 10:12
verses.text: You have granted me life and favor, and Your providence has preserved my spirit.

verses.name: Job 10:13
verses.text: And these have You hidden in Your heart; I know that this <hi>was</hi> with You.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 10:14
verses.text: If I sin, then You mark me, and You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

verses.name: Job 10:15
verses.text: If I am wicked, woe to me; and <hi>if</hi> I am righteous, I will not lift up my head <hi>being</hi> filled with shame, and looking on my affliction.

verses.name: Job 10:16
verses.text: For it increases! You hunt me as a fierce lion; and again You show Yourself marvelous on me.

verses.name: Job 10:17
verses.text: You renew Your witnesses against me, and increase Your anger on me; changes and warfare <hi>are</hi> against me.

verses.name: Job 10:18
verses.text: Why then have You brought me from the womb? Oh that I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me!

verses.name: Job 10:19
verses.text: I should have been as though I had not been; I would have been carried from the womb to the grave.

verses.name: Job 10:20
verses.text: Are not my days few? Cease <hi>then, and</hi> let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

verses.name: Job 10:21
verses.text: before I go, and I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

verses.name: Job 10:22
verses.text: a land of obscurity, the darkness of the shadow of death, without any order, and the shining <hi>is</hi> as darkness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 11:1
verses.text: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 11:2
verses.text: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?

verses.name: Job 11:3
verses.text: Should your lies make men silent? And will you mock and no one make <hi>you</hi> ashamed?

verses.name: Job 11:4
verses.text: For you have said, My doctrine <hi>is</hi> pure, and I am clean in Your eyes.

verses.name: Job 11:5
verses.text: But who will grant that God would speak, and open His lips against you,

verses.name: Job 11:6
verses.text: and would tell you the secrets of His wisdom, that sound wisdom <hi>is</hi> manifold? Know therefore that God forgets for you <hi>some</hi> of your iniquity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 11:7
verses.text: Can you by searching find out God? Can you perfectly find out the Almighty?

verses.name: Job 11:8
verses.text: Heights of the heavens! What can you do? <hi>It is</hi> deeper than hell, what can you know?

verses.name: Job 11:9
verses.text: The measure of it <hi>is</hi> longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

verses.name: Job 11:10
verses.text: If He passes through and shuts up, or gathers together, then who can turn Him back?

verses.name: Job 11:11
verses.text: For He knows vain men; and when He sees wickedness, will He not search <hi>it</hi>?

verses.name: Job 11:12
verses.text: For foolish man would be wise, and man is born a wild ass's colt.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 11:13
verses.text: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward Him;

verses.name: Job 11:14
verses.text: if iniquity <hi>is</hi> in your hand, put it far away, and do not let wickedness dwell in your tents;

verses.name: Job 11:15
verses.text: surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; yea, you shall be steadfast and shall not fear;

verses.name: Job 11:16
verses.text: for you shall forget <hi>your</hi> misery, and you shall remember <hi>it</hi> as waters that pass away.

verses.name: Job 11:17
verses.text: And <hi>your</hi> lifetime shall be clearer than the noonday; though <hi>there be</hi> darkness, you shall be as the morning.

verses.name: Job 11:18
verses.text: And you shall be safe, because there is hope; yea, you shall look around <hi>you</hi>, and you shall take your rest in safety.

verses.name: Job 11:19
verses.text: You shall lie down, and none <hi>shall</hi> make you afraid. Yea, many shall seek your favor.

verses.name: Job 11:20
verses.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall have no escape, and their hope <hi>shall be like</hi> the giving up of the spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 12:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 12:2
verses.text: For truly you <hi>are</hi> the people, and wisdom will die with you.

verses.name: Job 12:3
verses.text: But I have understanding as well as you; I do not fall <hi>short</hi> of you; yes, who does not know such things as these?

verses.name: Job 12:4
verses.text: I <hi>am</hi> a laughing-stock to his friends; who calls on God, and He answers him; the just, the upright one <hi>is</hi> a mockery;

verses.name: Job 12:5
verses.text: a flaming brand despised in the thoughts of him who feels secure; <hi>it is</hi> ready for those with slipping feet.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 12:6
verses.text: The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God <hi>are</hi> secure, in whatever God brings to their hand.

verses.name: Job 12:7
verses.text: But now ask the animals, and they shall teach you; and the birds of the air, and they shall tell you;

verses.name: Job 12:8
verses.text: or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you; and the fish of the sea shall declare <hi>it</hi> to you;

verses.name: Job 12:9
verses.text: who of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?

verses.name: Job 12:10
verses.text: In whose hand <hi>is</hi> the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all flesh, <hi>even</hi> of man?

verses.name: Job 12:11
verses.text: Does not the ear try words? And does not the mouth taste its food?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 12:12
verses.text: With the aged <hi>is</hi> wisdom, and understanding in length of days.

verses.name: Job 12:13
verses.text: With Him <hi>is</hi> wisdom and strength; He has wisdom and understanding.

verses.name: Job 12:14
verses.text: Behold, He breaks down, and it can not be built up again; He shuts up a man, and no one opens.

verses.name: Job 12:15
verses.text: Behold, He withholds the waters, and they dry up; also He sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

verses.name: Job 12:16
verses.text: With Him <hi>is</hi> strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver <hi>are</hi> His.

verses.name: Job 12:17
verses.text: He leads wise men away stripped, and makes the judges fools.

verses.name: Job 12:18
verses.text: He cuts away the bonds of kings, and binds their loins with a girdle.

verses.name: Job 12:19
verses.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

verses.name: Job 12:20
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> removes the speech of the men of trust, and takes away the understanding of the aged.

verses.name: Job 12:21
verses.text: He pours scorn on princes, and unties the belt of the mighty.

verses.name: Job 12:22
verses.text: He discovers deep things out of darkness, and brings the shadow of death to light.

verses.name: Job 12:23
verses.text: He gives greatness to the nations, and destroys them. He spreads out the nations, and leads them away.

verses.name: Job 12:24
verses.text: He takes away the heart of the chief of the people of the land, and causes them to wander in a wilderness <hi>where there is</hi> no path.

verses.name: Job 12:25
verses.text: They grope in the dark without light, and He makes them to stagger like <hi>a</hi> drunkard.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 13:1
verses.text: Lo, my eye has seen all this, my ear has heard and understood it.

verses.name: Job 13:2
verses.text: What you know, I know <hi>also</hi>; I do not fall <hi>short</hi> of you.

verses.name: Job 13:3
verses.text: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case before God.

verses.name: Job 13:4
verses.text: But you <hi>are</hi> imputers of lies; you <hi>are</hi> all worthless healers.

verses.name: Job 13:5
verses.text: Oh that you would stop speaking entirely! And it would be your wisdom.

verses.name: Job 13:6
verses.text: Hear now my reasoning, and listen to the pleadings of my lips.

verses.name: Job 13:7
verses.text: Would you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for Him?

verses.name: Job 13:8
verses.text: Will you lift up His person, or contend for God?

verses.name: Job 13:9
verses.text: Is it good that He should search you out? Or as one man mocks another, do you mock Him?

verses.name: Job 13:10
verses.text: He will surely blame you, if you secretly lift up persons.

verses.name: Job 13:11
verses.text: Shall not His highness make you afraid, and His dread fall on you?

verses.name: Job 13:12
verses.text: Your remembered sayings <hi>are</hi> like ashes, your bodies like bodies of clay.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 13:13
verses.text: Be quiet. Let me alone so that I may speak, and let come on me what may.

verses.name: Job 13:14
verses.text: Why do I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hand?

verses.name: Job 13:15
verses.text: Though he slay me, I will not wait, but I will maintain my own ways before Him.

verses.name: Job 13:16
verses.text: He also <hi>is</hi> my salvation, for an ungodly one shall not come before Him.

verses.name: Job 13:17
verses.text: Listen carefully to my words, and let what I say be in your ears.

verses.name: Job 13:18
verses.text: Behold now, I have set <hi>my</hi> cause in order; I know that I shall be justified.

verses.name: Job 13:19
verses.text: Who <hi>is</hi> he <hi>that</hi> will plead for me, for now, I would be quiet and expire.

verses.name: Job 13:20
verses.text: Only do not do two <hi>things</hi> to me; then I will not hide myself from You.

verses.name: Job 13:21
verses.text: Withdraw Your hand far from me, and let not Your fear make me afraid.

verses.name: Job 13:22
verses.text: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and answer You me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 13:23
verses.text: How many <hi>are</hi> my iniquities and sins? Make known my transgressions and my sin.

verses.name: Job 13:24
verses.text: Why do You hide Your face, and hold me for Your enemy?

verses.name: Job 13:25
verses.text: Will You terrify a leaf driven to and fro? Will You pursue the dry stubble?

verses.name: Job 13:26
verses.text: For You write bitter things against me, and make me to possess the sins of my youth.

verses.name: Job 13:27
verses.text: You put my feet also in the stocks, and look closely to all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.

verses.name: Job 13:28
verses.text: And he wears out like a rotten thing, like a garment that a moth eats.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 14:1
verses.text: Man born of woman <hi>is</hi> of few days, and full of trouble.

verses.name: Job 14:2
verses.text: He comes forth like a flower, and withers; he also flees as a shadow, and does not stand.

verses.name: Job 14:3
verses.text: And You open Your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with You.

verses.name: Job 14:4
verses.text: Who can bring a clean <hi>thing</hi> out of an unclean? No one!

verses.name: Job 14:5
verses.text: For his days <hi>are</hi> fixed, the number of his months <hi>is</hi> with You, and You have set his bounds so that he cannot pass;

verses.name: Job 14:6
verses.text: look away from him, so that he may rest until he shall finish his day, as a hireling.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 14:7
verses.text: For there is hope of a tree, if it is cut down, that it will sprout again, and its tender branch will not cease.

verses.name: Job 14:8
verses.text: Though its root becomes old in the earth, and its stump dies in the dust,

verses.name: Job 14:9
verses.text: <hi> yet</hi> at the scent of water it will bud and bring forth branches like a plant.

verses.name: Job 14:10
verses.text: But man dies and is cut off; and man expires, and where <hi>is</hi> he?

verses.name: Job 14:11
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> the waters fail from the sea, and a river falls away and dries up,

verses.name: Job 14:12
verses.text: so man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens <hi>are</hi> no more, they shall not awake, nor be awakened out of their sleep.

verses.name: Job 14:13
verses.text: Who will grant <hi>that</hi> You would hide me in the grave, that You would keep me secret, until Your wrath is past, that You would set me a fixed time and remember me?

verses.name: Job 14:14
verses.text: If a man die, shall he revive? All the days of my warfare I will wait, until my change comes.

verses.name: Job 14:15
verses.text: You shall call, and I will answer You; You shall have a desire to the work of Your hands.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 14:16
verses.text: For now You number my steps; do You not watch over my sin?

verses.name: Job 14:17
verses.text: My transgression <hi>is</hi> sealed up in a bag, and You cover over my iniquity.

verses.name: Job 14:18
verses.text: And surely a falling mountain crumbles away, and the rock moves out of its place.

verses.name: Job 14:19
verses.text: The waters wear away the stones; the outpouring of it washes the dust of the earth; and You cause the hope of man to perish.

verses.name: Job 14:20
verses.text: You overpower him forever, and he passes; You change his face, and send him away.

verses.name: Job 14:21
verses.text: His sons come to honor, and he knows it not; they fall, but he does not mark <hi>it</hi>.

verses.name: Job 14:22
verses.text: But his flesh is pained within him; and his soul mourns over him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 15:1
verses.text: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 15:2
verses.text: <hi> Should</hi> a wise man answer with windy knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?

verses.name: Job 15:3
verses.text: Should he reason with talk <hi>that is</hi> not useful, or with speeches which have no profit?

verses.name: Job 15:4
verses.text: Yea, you do away with fear, and take away prayer before God.

verses.name: Job 15:5
verses.text: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

verses.name: Job 15:6
verses.text: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; yes, your own lips testify against you.

verses.name: Job 15:7
verses.text: <hi> Were</hi> you the first man born? Or were you made before the hills?

verses.name: Job 15:8
verses.text: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? And do you limit wisdom to yourself?

verses.name: Job 15:9
verses.text: What do you know that we do not know, or understand that is not with us?

verses.name: Job 15:10
verses.text: With us <hi>are</hi> both the gray-headed and aged, mightier than your father <hi>as to</hi> days.

verses.name: Job 15:11
verses.text: <hi> Are</hi> the comforts of God small with you, and a word <hi>dealing</hi> gently with you?

verses.name: Job 15:12
verses.text: Why does your heart carry you away? And what do your eyes wink at,

verses.name: Job 15:13
verses.text: that you turn your spirit against God, and let <hi>such</hi> words go out of your mouth?

verses.name: Job 15:14
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> man, that he should be clean? And <hi>what is he</hi> born of a woman that he should be righteous?

verses.name: Job 15:15
verses.text: Behold, He puts no trust in His saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in His sight.

verses.name: Job 15:16
verses.text: How much more hateful and filthy <hi>is</hi> man, who drinks iniquity like water?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 15:17
verses.text: I will show you; hear me; and what I have seen I will declare,

verses.name: Job 15:18
verses.text: that which wise men have told, and have not hidden from their fathers;

verses.name: Job 15:19
verses.text: to them alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.

verses.name: Job 15:20
verses.text: The wicked man labors in pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden for the ruthless one.

verses.name: Job 15:21
verses.text: A dreadful sound of things <hi>is</hi> in his ears; the destroyer shall come to him in peace.

verses.name: Job 15:22
verses.text: He does not believe in a return from darkness, but he <hi>is</hi> awaited by the sword.

verses.name: Job 15:23
verses.text: He wanders for bread, saying, Where <hi>is it</hi>? He knows that the day of darkness is ready at hand.

verses.name: Job 15:24
verses.text: Trouble and pain shall terrify him; they shall overpower him, as a king ready for the battle;

verses.name: Job 15:25
verses.text: because he stretches out his hand against God, and sets himself against the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 15:26
verses.text: He runs at him, with a <hi>stiff</hi> neck, with the thick layers of his shields,

verses.name: Job 15:27
verses.text: because he has covered his face with fat; he has put fat on <hi>his</hi> loins.

verses.name: Job 15:28
verses.text: And he lives <hi>in</hi> cut off cities, <hi>in</hi> houses where none <hi>are</hi> living, which are ready <hi>to become</hi> heaps.

verses.name: Job 15:29
verses.text: He shall not be rich, nor shall his wealth hold out, nor shall he stretch out his gain on the earth.

verses.name: Job 15:30
verses.text: He shall not escape from darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and at the breath of his mouth he shall turn away.

verses.name: Job 15:31
verses.text: Let not <hi>he</hi> being deceived trust in vanity; for vanity shall be his reward.

verses.name: Job 15:32
verses.text: It shall be done before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

verses.name: Job 15:33
verses.text: He shall shake off its unripe grape, as the vine; and shall cast off his flower like the olive.

verses.name: Job 15:34
verses.text: For the company of the ungodly <hi>shall be</hi> barren, and fire shall devour the tents of bribery.

verses.name: Job 15:35
verses.text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth evil, and their belly prepares deceit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 16:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 16:2
verses.text: I have heard many such <hi>things</hi>. You <hi>are</hi> all miserable comforters.

verses.name: Job 16:3
verses.text: <hi> Shall</hi> words of wind <hi>have</hi> an end? Or what provokes you that you should answer?

verses.name: Job 16:4
verses.text: I also could speak as you <hi>do</hi>; if your soul were in my soul's place. I could heap up words against you, and shake my head at you.

verses.name: Job 16:5
verses.text: I might make you strong with my mouth, and the moving of my lips would spare you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 16:6
verses.text: Though I speak, my pain is not held back, and <hi>though</hi> I forbear, in what way am I eased?

verses.name: Job 16:7
verses.text: But now He has made me weary; You have made all my company desolate.

verses.name: Job 16:8
verses.text: And You have plucked me, for it is a witness, and my failure rises up against me, and it answers to my face.

verses.name: Job 16:9
verses.text: His anger has torn and hated <hi>me</hi>; He gnashes on me with His teeth; my enemy sharpens his eyes at me;

verses.name: Job 16:10
verses.text: They have gaped on me with their mouth; and have scornfully beaten me on the cheek; they gather themselves against me.

verses.name: Job 16:11
verses.text: God has delivered me to the perverse; and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.

verses.name: Job 16:12
verses.text: I was at ease, but He has broken me in pieces; yea, <hi>He has</hi> also taken <hi>me</hi> by my neck and shaken me to pieces and set me up for His mark.

verses.name: Job 16:13
verses.text: His archers hem me in; He splits my inward parts, and does not spare; He pours out my gall on the ground.

verses.name: Job 16:14
verses.text: He breaks me with break on break; He runs on me like a giant.

verses.name: Job 16:15
verses.text: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin and thrust my horn in the dust.

verses.name: Job 16:16
verses.text: My face is reddened from weeping, and on my eyelids <hi>is</hi> the shadow of death;  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 16:17
verses.text: though no violence <hi>is</hi> in my hand, and my prayer <hi>is</hi> pure.

verses.name: Job 16:18
verses.text: Oh earth, do not cover my blood, and let not my cry have a place.

verses.name: Job 16:19
verses.text: Also now, behold, my Witness <hi>is</hi> in Heaven, and He who testifies of me <hi>is</hi> on high.

verses.name: Job 16:20
verses.text: My friends scorn me; my eye pours out <hi>tears</hi> to God.

verses.name: Job 16:21
verses.text: Oh that one might plead for a man with God, as a man <hi>pleads</hi> for his neighbor!

verses.name: Job 16:22
verses.text: For the years <hi>that are few</hi> will come, and I shall go the way from where I shall not return.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 17:1
verses.text: My spirit is broken, my days are ended, the graves <hi>are</hi> ready for me.

verses.name: Job 17:2
verses.text: <hi> Are</hi> not mockeries with me? Yea, my eye rests on their insults.

verses.name: Job 17:3
verses.text: Please lay down a pledge for me with Yourself; who <hi>is</hi> he <hi>who</hi> will strike hands with me?

verses.name: Job 17:4
verses.text: For You have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore You shall not lift <hi>them</hi> up.

verses.name: Job 17:5
verses.text: He who for a share informs <hi>against</hi> friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

verses.name: Job 17:6
verses.text: He has made me also a byword of the peoples; and I am one in whose face they spit.

verses.name: Job 17:7
verses.text: My eye also is dim from grief; and all my members <hi>are</hi> like a shadow.

verses.name: Job 17:8
verses.text: Upright ones shall be amazed at this, and the innocent shall stir himself up against the ungodly.

verses.name: Job 17:9
verses.text: The righteous also shall hold <hi>on</hi> his way, and he who has clean hands adds strength.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 17:10
verses.text: And now all of them, go back, and please come again; and I shall not find among you a wise man.

verses.name: Job 17:11
verses.text: My days are past, my purposes <hi>are</hi> broken off, the desires of my heart.

verses.name: Job 17:12
verses.text: They set night for day; the light <hi>is</hi> near in the face of darkness.

verses.name: Job 17:13
verses.text: If I wait for the grave <hi>as</hi> my home, I have made my bed in the darkness;

verses.name: Job 17:14
verses.text: I have said to corruption, You <hi>are</hi> my father; to the worm, My mother and my sister!

verses.name: Job 17:15
verses.text: And where then <hi>is</hi> my hope? And <hi>as for</hi> my hope, who shall see it?

verses.name: Job 17:16
verses.text: They shall go down <hi>to</hi> the bars of the pit, when <hi>our</hi> descent together <hi>is</hi> in the dust.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 18:1
verses.text: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 18:2
verses.text: Until when will you set a snare for words? Understand, and afterwards we will speak.

verses.name: Job 18:3
verses.text: Why are we counted as cattle, or seem stupid in your sight?

verses.name: Job 18:4
verses.text: He tears himself in his anger; <hi>shall</hi> the earth <hi>be</hi> forsaken for you? And shall the rock be moved out of its place?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 18:5
verses.text: Yes, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.

verses.name: Job 18:6
verses.text: The light shall be dark in his tent, and his lamp shall be put out with him.

verses.name: Job 18:7
verses.text: The steps of his strength shall be hampered, and his own plans shall throw him down.

verses.name: Job 18:8
verses.text: For he is thrown into a net by his own feet, and he walks on a net.

verses.name: Job 18:9
verses.text: The trap shall take <hi>him</hi> by the heel, and the noose shall hold sway over him.

verses.name: Job 18:10
verses.text: The pitfall <hi>is</hi> laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 18:11
verses.text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall dash him at his feet.

verses.name: Job 18:12
verses.text: His strength shall be hunger-bitten, and trouble shall be ready at his side.

verses.name: Job 18:13
verses.text: It shall devour the parts of his skin; the first-born of death consumes his parts.

verses.name: Job 18:14
verses.text: His hope shall be rooted out of his tent, and you marched to the king of terrors.

verses.name: Job 18:15
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> not his shall dwell in his tent; brimstone shall be scattered on his home.

verses.name: Job 18:16
verses.text: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and his branch shall wither above.

verses.name: Job 18:17
verses.text: His memory shall perish from the earth, and there is no name to him on the face of the street.

verses.name: Job 18:18
verses.text: They drive him from light to darkness, and they make him flee from the world.

verses.name: Job 18:19
verses.text: He shall have neither son nor kinsman among his people, nor <hi>any</hi> remaining in his dwellings.

verses.name: Job 18:20
verses.text: Those after him shall be amazed at his day; and those before were seized <hi>with</hi> horror.

verses.name: Job 18:21
verses.text: Surely these <hi>are</hi> the dwellings of the perverse, and this the place <hi>that</hi> has not known God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 19:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 19:2
verses.text: How long will you torment my soul and break me in pieces with words?

verses.name: Job 19:3
verses.text: <hi> And</hi> this, ten times you have blamed me; you are not ashamed that you have wronged me.

verses.name: Job 19:4
verses.text: And <hi>if</hi> indeed I have erred, my error remains with me.

verses.name: Job 19:5
verses.text: If indeed you magnify yourself against me, and plead against me my misery,

verses.name: Job 19:6
verses.text: know now that God has overthrown me, and His net has closed on me.

verses.name: Job 19:7
verses.text: Behold, I cry out, Violence! And I am not answered. I cry aloud, but there is no justice.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 19:8
verses.text: He has fenced up my way so that I cannot pass, and He has set darkness in my paths.

verses.name: Job 19:9
verses.text: He has stripped me of my glory, and has taken the crown from my head.

verses.name: Job 19:10
verses.text: He has broken me on every side, and I am gone, and He has uprooted my hope like a tree.

verses.name: Job 19:11
verses.text: He has also kindled His wrath against me, and to Himself He counts me as His enemy.

verses.name: Job 19:12
verses.text: His troops come together and raise up their way against me, and camp around my tent.

verses.name: Job 19:13
verses.text: He has put my brothers far from me, and my friends have truly turned away from me.

verses.name: Job 19:14
verses.text: My people have fallen away, and my familiar friends have forgotten me.

verses.name: Job 19:15
verses.text: Those who dwell in my house, and my slave-girls, count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.

verses.name: Job 19:16
verses.text: I called my servant, and he gave no answer; I must beg him with my mouth.

verses.name: Job 19:17
verses.text: My breath is hated by my wife, and I must beg to the sons of my <hi>mother's</hi> womb.

verses.name: Job 19:18
verses.text: Even young children despise me; I arise, and they speak against me.

verses.name: Job 19:19
verses.text: All the men of my counsel detest me, even this one I loved has turned against me.

verses.name: Job 19:20
verses.text: My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped with the skin of my teeth.

verses.name: Job 19:21
verses.text: Have pity on me! Have pity on me, my friends! For the hand of God has touched me.

verses.name: Job 19:22
verses.text: Why do you, like God, persecute me and are not satisfied with my flesh?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 19:23
verses.text: Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were engraved in a book!

verses.name: Job 19:24
verses.text: <hi> Oh that</hi> they were cut with an iron pen and lead in the rock forever!

verses.name: Job 19:25
verses.text: For I know <hi>that</hi> my Redeemer lives, and He shall rise on the earth at the last;

verses.name: Job 19:26
verses.text: and even after they corrupt my skin, yet this: in my flesh I shall see God,

verses.name: Job 19:27
verses.text: whom I shall see for myself, and my eyes shall behold, and not a stranger's; <hi>though</hi> My heart be exhausted in my bosom.

verses.name: Job 19:28
verses.text: For you ought to say, Why do we persecute him, since the root of the matter is found in me?

verses.name: Job 19:29
verses.text: Fear for yourselves because of the sword; for wrath <hi>brings</hi> the punishments of the sword, so that you may know <hi>there is</hi> a judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 20:1
verses.text: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 20:2
verses.text: Therefore my thoughts cause me to answer, even because of my haste in me.

verses.name: Job 20:3
verses.text: I have heard the rebuke meant to shame me, and the spirit of my understanding causes me to answer.

verses.name: Job 20:4
verses.text: Do you know this from <hi>days</hi> of old, from the setting of man on earth,

verses.name: Job 20:5
verses.text: that the exulting of the wicked <hi>is</hi> short, and the joy of the ungodly <hi>is</hi> for a moment?

verses.name: Job 20:6
verses.text: Though his honor mounts up to the heavens, and his head reaches to the clouds,

verses.name: Job 20:7
verses.text: he shall perish forever like his dung; they who see him shall say, Where <hi>is</hi> he?

verses.name: Job 20:8
verses.text: He flies away like a dream, and shall not be found, and shall be chased away like a vision of the night.

verses.name: Job 20:9
verses.text: An eye glimpsed him, but will not again; yea, his place shall not see him again.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 20:10
verses.text: His sons shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore his wealth.

verses.name: Job 20:11
verses.text: His bones are full of his youthful vigor, but it lies down with him in the dust.

verses.name: Job 20:12
verses.text: Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, <hi>though</hi> he hides it under his tongue;

verses.name: Job 20:13
verses.text: <hi> though</hi> he spares it and will not leave it; yea, keeps it still in his mouth;

verses.name: Job 20:14
verses.text: <hi> yet</hi> his food in his belly shall be turned; the gall of asps <hi>is</hi> within him.

verses.name: Job 20:15
verses.text: He swallows riches, but vomits it; God shall cast them out of his belly.

verses.name: Job 20:16
verses.text: He shall suck the poison of asps; the viper's tongue shall slay him.

verses.name: Job 20:17
verses.text: He shall not see the rivers, the flowings of the brooks of honey and butter,

verses.name: Job 20:18
verses.text: giving back his gain, and he will not eat. As to the wealth of his trading, even he shall not enjoy <hi>it</hi>.

verses.name: Job 20:19
verses.text: For he pressed down <hi>and</hi> forsook the poor; he stole a house, but he had not built it.

verses.name: Job 20:20
verses.text: Surely he shall not know quietness in his belly; he will not escape with the things of desire.

verses.name: Job 20:21
verses.text: None of his food shall be left; therefore his good will not last.

verses.name: Job 20:22
verses.text: In the fullness of his plenty he shall be in trouble; every wretched one shall come on him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 20:23
verses.text: It shall happen at the filling of his belly, <hi>God</hi> shall cast the fury of His wrath on him, and He shall rain on him while he is eating.

verses.name: Job 20:24
verses.text: He shall flee from the iron weapon, a bow of bronze shall pierce him.

verses.name: Job 20:25
verses.text: One draws it, and treads it from behind, even lightning from his gall; terror <hi>is</hi> on him.

verses.name: Job 20:26
verses.text: All darkness <hi>shall be</hi> hidden in his secret places; a fire not blown shall consume him; those left in his tent shall be broken.

verses.name: Job 20:27
verses.text: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth rise up against him.

verses.name: Job 20:28
verses.text: The increase of his house shall depart, and shall flow <hi>away</hi> in the day of his wrath.

verses.name: Job 20:29
verses.text: This <hi>is</hi> the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance of his word from God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 21:1
verses.text: And Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 21:2
verses.text: Listen carefully to my speech, and let this be your comfort.

verses.name: Job 21:3
verses.text: Rise with me and I shall speak; and after I have spoken, mock on.

verses.name: Job 21:4
verses.text: <hi> As for</hi> me, is my complaint to man? And why should my spirit not be troubled?

verses.name: Job 21:5
verses.text: Turn to me and be amazed, and lay <hi>your</hi> hand on <hi>your</hi> mouth.

verses.name: Job 21:6
verses.text: And if I remember, I am afraid, and trembling takes hold on my flesh.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 21:7
verses.text: Why do the wicked live? They grow old and become mighty <hi>in</hi> power?

verses.name: Job 21:8
verses.text: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

verses.name: Job 21:9
verses.text: Their houses <hi>are</hi> in peace, without fear; nor <hi>is</hi> the rod of God on them.

verses.name: Job 21:10
verses.text: Their bull mates and does not fail; their cow calves, and does not cast her calf.

verses.name: Job 21:11
verses.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

verses.name: Job 21:12
verses.text: They lift up <hi>voice</hi> at the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the flute.

verses.name: Job 21:13
verses.text: They spend their days in good, and in a moment go down <hi>to</hi> the grave.

verses.name: Job 21:14
verses.text: And they say to God, Depart from us; for we do not desire the knowledge of your ways;

verses.name: Job 21:15
verses.text: what <hi>is</hi> the Almighty, that we should serve Him? And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?

verses.name: Job 21:16
verses.text: Behold, their good <hi>is</hi> not in their hand; the wisdom of the wicked is far from me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 21:17
verses.text: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and their trouble comes on them! He shares out pains in His anger;

verses.name: Job 21:18
verses.text: they are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff <hi>that</hi> the storm steals away.

verses.name: Job 21:19
verses.text: God lays up his iniquity for his children. He repays him, and he knows.

verses.name: Job 21:20
verses.text: His eyes shall see his ruin, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 21:21
verses.text: For what <hi>is</hi> his pleasure in his house after him, and the number of his months is cut off?

verses.name: Job 21:22
verses.text: Shall <hi>any</hi> teach God knowledge, since He shall judge the exalted?

verses.name: Job 21:23
verses.text: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

verses.name: Job 21:24
verses.text: His sides are full of milk, his bones are wet with marrow.

verses.name: Job 21:25
verses.text: And another dies with bitter soul, and never eats with pleasure.

verses.name: Job 21:26
verses.text: They lie down together in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Job 21:27
verses.text: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the plots which you wrongfully hatch against me.

verses.name: Job 21:28
