verses.text: Whoever despises the word shall be destroyed, but he who fears the commandment shall be rewarded.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:14
verses.text: The law of the wise <hi>is</hi> a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:15
verses.text: Good understanding gives favor, but the way of traitors <hi>is</hi> ever flowing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:16
verses.text: Every wise one deals with knowledge, but a fool lays open <hi>his</hi> folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:17
verses.text: A wicked messenger falls into mischief, but a faithful ambassador <hi>is</hi> health.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:18
verses.text: Poverty and shame <hi>shall be to</hi> him who refuses instruction, but he who listens to correction shall be honored.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:19
verses.text: The desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but <hi>it is</hi> hateful to fools to turn from evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:20
verses.text: He who walks with the wise shall be wise, but a companion <hi>with</hi> fools shall be destroyed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:21
verses.text: Evil pursues sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:22
verses.text: A good <hi>man</hi> leaves an inheritance to his sons' sons, and the wealth of the sinner <hi>is</hi> laid up for the just.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:23
verses.text: Much food <hi>is</hi> in the plowed ground of the poor, but when <hi>there is</hi> no justice, it is swept away.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:24
verses.text: He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him chastens him early.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:25
verses.text: The righteous eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall lack.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:1
verses.text: A wise woman builds her house, but the foolish plucks it down with her hands.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:2
verses.text: He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but <hi>he who is</hi> perverse in his ways despises Him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:3
verses.text: In the mouth of the foolish <hi>is</hi> a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise shall keep them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:4
verses.text: Where no cattle <hi>are</hi>, the stall <hi>is</hi> clean, but much gain <hi>is</hi> by the strength of the ox.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:5
verses.text: A faithful witness will not lie, but a false witness will speak lies.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:6
verses.text: A scorner seeks wisdom, and it is not <hi>found</hi>, but knowledge <hi>is</hi> easy to him who understands.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:7
verses.text: Go from the before a foolish man when you do not see <hi>in him</hi> the lips of knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:8
verses.text: The wisdom of the wise <hi>is</hi> to understand his way, but the folly of fools <hi>is</hi> deceit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:9
verses.text: Fools laugh at sin, but among the righteous <hi>there is</hi> favor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:10
verses.text: The heart knows its own bitterness, and a stranger does not share in its joy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:11
verses.text: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown, but the tent of the upright shall be blessed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:12
verses.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but the end of it <hi>is</hi> the ways of death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:13
verses.text: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, and the end of that joy <hi>is</hi> heaviness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:14
verses.text: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways, but a good man from himself.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:15
verses.text: The simple believes every word, but the wise man watches his step.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:16
verses.text: A wise one fears and departs from evil, but the fool rages and is sure.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:17
verses.text: He who <hi>is</hi> soon angry acts foolishly, and a man of wicked plots is hated.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:18
verses.text: The simple inherit folly, but the wise are crowned with knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:19
verses.text: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:20
verses.text: The poor is hated even by his own neighbor, but the rich <hi>has</hi> many friends.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:21
verses.text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has mercy on the poor, happy <hi>is</hi> he.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:22
verses.text: Do not those who think evil go astray? But mercy and truth shall be to those who think of good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:23
verses.text: In all labor there is gain, but the talk of the lips <hi>tends</hi> only to poverty.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:24
verses.text: The crown of the wise <hi>is</hi> their riches <hi>of wisdom</hi>; the foolishness of fools <hi>is</hi> folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:25
verses.text: A true witness delivers souls, but a deceitful witness speaks lies.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:26
verses.text: In the fear of the LORD <hi>is</hi> strong hope, and His sons shall have a place of refuge.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:27
verses.text: The fear of the LORD <hi>is</hi> a fountain of life to turn aside from the snares of death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:28
verses.text: In the multitude of people <hi>is</hi> the king's honor, but in the lack of people <hi>is</hi> the ruin of the prince.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:29
verses.text: <hi> He who is</hi> slow to wrath <hi>is</hi> of great understanding, but <hi>he who is</hi> hasty of spirit exalts folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:30
verses.text: A sound heart <hi>is</hi> the life of the flesh, but envy the rottenness of the bones.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:31
verses.text: He who presses the poor curses his Maker, but he who honors Him has mercy upon the poor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:32
verses.text: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness, but the righteous <hi>has</hi> hope in his death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:33
verses.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of him who has understanding, but among fools it is made known.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:34
verses.text: Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin <hi>is</hi> a shame to any people.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:35
verses.text: The king's favor <hi>is</hi> toward a wise servant, but his wrath is against him who causes shame.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:1
verses.text: A soft answer turns away wrath, but grievous words stir up anger.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:2
verses.text: The tongue of the wise uses knowledge rightly, but the mouth of fools pours out foolishness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:3
verses.text: The eyes of the LORD <hi>are</hi> in every place, beholding the evil and the good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:4
verses.text: A wholesome tongue <hi>is</hi> a tree of life, but crookedness in it <hi>is</hi> a break in the spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:5
verses.text: A fool despises his father's instruction, but he who listens to correction is wise.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:6
verses.text: In the house of the righteous <hi>is</hi> much treasure, but in the gain of the wicked <hi>is</hi> trouble.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:7
verses.text: The lips of the righteous send forth knowledge, but the heart of the foolish <hi>is</hi> not so.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:8
verses.text: The sacrifice of the wicked <hi>is</hi> a hateful thing to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright <hi>is</hi> His delight.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:9
verses.text: The way of the wicked <hi>is</hi> hateful to the LORD, but He loves him who pursues righteousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:10
verses.text: Correction <hi>is</hi> grievous to him who forsakes the way; he who hates reproof shall die.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:11
verses.text: Hell and destruction <hi>are</hi> before the LORD; even more the hearts of the sons of men?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:12
verses.text: A scorner does not love one who corrects him, nor will he go to the wise.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:13
verses.text: A merry heart makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:14
verses.text: The heart of him who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:15
verses.text: All the days of the afflicted <hi>are</hi> evil, but gladness of heart is a continual a feast.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:16
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and tumult with it.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:17
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> a dinner of vegetables where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred with it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:18
verses.text: A wrathful man stirs up fighting, but one slow to anger calms fighting.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:19
verses.text: The way of the lazy one <hi>is</hi> like a hedge of thorns, but the way of the righteous <hi>is</hi> made plain.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:20
verses.text: A wise son makes a glad father, but a foolish man despises his mother.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:21
verses.text: Folly <hi>is</hi> joy to him who is without any wisdom, but a man of understanding walks uprightly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:22
verses.text: Without wisdom, purposes are defeated, but by many wise men they are established.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:23
verses.text: A man <hi>has</hi> joy by the answer of his mouth, and a word in due season, how good <hi>it is</hi>!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:24
verses.text: The way of life <hi>is</hi> above to the wise, so that he may turn away from hell below.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:25
verses.text: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud, but He will set up the border of the widow.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:26
verses.text: The thoughts of the wicked <hi>are</hi> very hateful to the LORD, but the words of the pure <hi>are</hi> pleasant words.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:27
verses.text: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes shall live.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:28
verses.text: The heart of the righteous studies to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:29
verses.text: The LORD <hi>is</hi> far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:30
verses.text: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart; a good report makes the bones fat.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:31
verses.text: The ear that hears the reproof of life shall remain among the wise.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:32
verses.text: He who refuses instruction despises his own soul, but he who hears reproof gets understanding.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:33
verses.text: The fear of the LORD <hi>is</hi> the instruction of wisdom, and before honor <hi>is</hi> humility.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:1
verses.text: The ordering of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, <hi>is</hi> from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:2
verses.text: All the ways of a man <hi>are</hi> clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:3
verses.text: Roll your works upon the LORD, and your thoughts shall be established.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:4
verses.text: The LORD has made all for His purpose; yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:5
verses.text: Everyone proud in heart <hi>is</hi> hateful to the LORD; though hand <hi>join</hi> in hand, he shall not be unpunished.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:6
verses.text: By mercy and truth, iniquity is purged, and by the fear of the LORD <hi>men</hi> turn away from evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:7
verses.text: When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:8
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> a little with righteousness than great gain without right.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:9
verses.text: A man's heart plans his way, but the LORD directs his steps.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:10
verses.text: A divine sentence <hi>is</hi> in the lips of the king; his mouth does not transgress in judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:11
verses.text: A just weight and balance <hi>are</hi> the LORD's; all the weights of the bag <hi>are</hi> His work.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:12
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> a hateful thing for kings to commit wickedness; for the throne <hi>is</hi> established by righteousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:13
verses.text: Righteous lips <hi>are</hi> the delight of kings, and they love him who speaks right.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:14
verses.text: The wrath of a king <hi>is as</hi> messengers of death, but a wise man will quiet it.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:15
verses.text: In the light of the king's face <hi>is</hi> life, and his favor <hi>is</hi> like a cloud of the latter rain.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:16
verses.text: How much better <hi>it is</hi> to get wisdom than gold! And to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:17
verses.text: The way of the upright <hi>is</hi> to turn away from evil; he who keeps his way guards his way.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:18
verses.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:19
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better <hi>to be</hi> of an humble spirit with the lowly than to divide the spoil with the proud.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:20
verses.text: He who handles a matter wisely shall find good, and whoever trusts in the LORD, happy <hi>is</hi> he.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:21
verses.text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent, and the sweetness of the lips increases learning.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:22
verses.text: Understanding <hi>is</hi> a fountain of life to him who has it, but the instruction of fools <hi>is</hi> folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:23
verses.text: The heart of the wise teaches his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:24
verses.text: Pleasant words <hi>are like</hi> a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:25
verses.text: There is a way <hi>that seems</hi> right to a man, but the end of it <hi>is</hi> the ways of death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:26
verses.text: He who labors works for himself, for his mouth craves it from him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:27
verses.text: An ungodly man plots evil, and his lips <hi>are</hi> like a burning fire.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:28
verses.text: A perverse man causes fighting, and a whisperer separates chief friends.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:29
verses.text: A violent man lures his neighbor and makes him go in a way not good.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:30
verses.text: He shuts his eyes to think of perverse things; moving his lips, he brings evil to pass.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:31
verses.text: The gray head <hi>is</hi> a crown of glory, <hi>if</hi> it is found in the way of righteousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:32
verses.text: He who is slow to anger <hi>is</hi> better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit is better than he who takes a city.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:33
verses.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing of it <hi>is</hi> from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:1
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> a dry piece of bread, and quietness with it, than a house full of sacrifices <hi>with</hi> fighting.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:2
verses.text: A wise servant shall have rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brothers.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:3
verses.text: The refining pot <hi>is</hi> for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tries the hearts.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:4
verses.text: A wicked doer gives heed to false lips; a liar gives ear to an evil tongue.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:5
verses.text: Whoever scorns the poor reviles his Maker; he who is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:6
verses.text: Sons of sons <hi>are</hi> the crown of old men, and the glory of sons <hi>are</hi> their fathers.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:7
verses.text: An excellent lip <hi>is</hi> not fitting for a fool; much less are lying lips fitting for a prince.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:8
verses.text: A bribe <hi>is</hi> like a precious stone in the eyes of him who has it; wherever he turns, he is prudent.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:9
verses.text: He who covers a transgression seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates friends.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:10
verses.text: A reproof enters more into a wise man than a thousand stripes into a fool.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:11
verses.text: An evil one seeks only rebellion; so a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:12
verses.text: Let a bear robbed <hi>of her cubs</hi> meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:13
verses.text: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:14
verses.text: The beginning of strife <hi>is like</hi> letting out water; therefore leave off fighting, before it breaks out.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:15
verses.text: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, even both of them <hi>are</hi> hateful to the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:16
verses.text: Why <hi>is there</hi> a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, since <hi>he has</hi> no heart <hi>for it</hi>?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:17
verses.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for the time of trouble.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:18
verses.text: A man lacking heart strikes hands; he pledges in the presence of his friend.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:19
verses.text: He who loves fighting loves transgression; he who makes his gate high seeks ruin.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:20
verses.text: He who has a perverse heart finds no good, and he who <hi>has</hi> a crooked tongue falls into mischief.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:21
verses.text: He who fathers a fool <hi>does it</hi> to his sorrow; the father of a fool has no joy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:22
verses.text: A merry heart does good <hi>like</hi> a medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:23
verses.text: A wicked <hi>man</hi> takes a bribe out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:24
verses.text: Wisdom <hi>is</hi> before him who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool <hi>are</hi> in the ends of the earth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:25
verses.text: A foolish son <hi>is</hi> a grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:26
verses.text: And <hi>it is</hi> not good to punish the just, nor to strike princes for uprightness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:27
verses.text: He who has knowledge uses few words; a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:28
verses.text: Even a fool, when he <hi>is</hi> silent, is counted wise, and he who shuts his lips <hi>is counted as</hi> a man of understanding.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:1
verses.text: He that separates himself seeks <hi>his own</hi> desire; he breaks out against all sound wisdom.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:2
verses.text: A fool has no delight in understanding, but only that his heart may lay itself bare.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:3
verses.text: When the wicked comes, scorn also comes, and with shame comes reproach.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:4
verses.text: The words of a man's mouth are like deep waters; the fountain of wisdom <hi>is like</hi> a flowing stream.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:5
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> not good to favor the person of the wicked, <hi>nor</hi> to overthrow the righteous in judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:6
verses.text: A fool's lips enter into argument, and his mouth calls for strokes.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:7
verses.text: A fool's mouth <hi>is</hi> his destruction, and his lips <hi>are</hi> the snare of his soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:8
verses.text: The words of a talebearer <hi>are</hi> as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:9
verses.text: Also he who is slack in his work is brother to a great destroyer.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:10
verses.text: The name of the LORD <hi>is</hi> a strong tower; the righteous man runs into it and is safe.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:11
verses.text: The rich man's wealth <hi>is</hi> his strong city, and as a high wall in his own mind.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:12
verses.text: Before shattering, the heart of man is proud, and before honor <hi>is</hi> humility.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:13
verses.text: If one answers a matter before he hears, it <hi>is</hi> folly and shame to him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:14
verses.text: The spirit of a man will nourish his sickness, but a wounded spirit who can bear?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:15
verses.text: The heart of the prudent gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:16
verses.text: A man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:17
verses.text: The first in his cause <hi>seems</hi> just, <hi>but</hi> his neighbor comes and searches him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:18
verses.text: The lot causes arguments to cease, and divides between the mighty.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:19
verses.text: An brother offended <hi>is like</hi> a strong city; and <hi>their</hi> disagreements <hi>are</hi> like the bars of a fortress.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:20
verses.text: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; he shall be satisfied with the product of his lips.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:21
verses.text: Death and life <hi>are</hi> in the power of the tongue, and those who love it shall eat the fruit of it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:22
verses.text: <hi> Whoever</hi> finds a wife finds good and gets favor from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:23
verses.text: The poor speaks humble requests, but the rich answers roughly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:24
verses.text: A man who has friends may be broken up, but there is a Lover who sticks closer than a brother.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:1
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> the poor who walks in his integrity than he who <hi>is</hi> perverse in his lips, and is a fool.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:2
verses.text: Also without knowledge the soul <hi>is</hi> not good, and he who hurries with his feet sins.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:3
verses.text: The foolishness of man perverts his way, and his heart frets against the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:4
verses.text: Wealth makes many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:5
verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and a breather of lies shall not escape.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:6
verses.text: Many will beg the favor of a ruler, and all <hi>are</hi> friends to a man who gives gifts.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:7
verses.text: All the brothers of the poor man hate him; how much more do his friends go far from him? He pursues <hi>them</hi> with words, yet they <hi>are</hi> lacking.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:8
verses.text: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul; he who keeps understanding shall find good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:9
verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and one speaking lies shall perish.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:10
verses.text: Luxury is not becoming for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:11
verses.text: The judgment of a man puts off his anger; and <hi>it is</hi> his glory to pass over a transgression.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:12
verses.text: The king's wrath <hi>is</hi> like the roaring of a lion; but his favor <hi>is</hi> like dew on the grass.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:13
verses.text: A foolish son <hi>is</hi> ruin to his father, and the quarreling of a wife <hi>is</hi> a never-ending dripping.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:14
verses.text: Houses and riches <hi>are</hi> the inheritance of fathers, and a prudent wife <hi>is</hi> from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:15
verses.text: Laziness throws one into a deep sleep, and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:16
verses.text: He who keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; he who despises His ways shall die.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:17
verses.text: He who has pity upon the poor lends to the LORD, and He will reward his dealing to him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:18
verses.text: Chasten your son while there is hope, and do not set your soul on making him die.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:19
verses.text: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment; for if you deliver <hi>him</hi> yet you must do it again.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:20
verses.text: Hear advice, and receive instruction, so that you may be wise in your latter end.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:21
verses.text: <hi> There are</hi> many purposes in a man's heart, but the counsel of the LORD shall stand.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:22
verses.text: The charm of a man <hi>is</hi> his kindness, and a poor man <hi>is</hi> better than a liar.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:23
verses.text: The fear of the LORD <hi>tends</hi> to life, and he rests satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:24
verses.text: A lazy one puts his hand in a dish, and he will not return it to his mouth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:25
verses.text: Strike a scorner, and the simple will beware; reprove one who has understanding, and he will understand knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:26
verses.text: He who assaults his father <hi>and</hi> chases away his mother <hi>is</hi> a son who causes shame and brings reproach.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:27
verses.text: My son, cease to hear the discipline, <hi>only</hi> to stray from the words of knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:28
verses.text: An ungodly witness scorns judgment, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:29
verses.text: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:1
verses.text: Wine <hi>is</hi> a mocker, strong drink <hi>is</hi> raging, and whoever goes astray by it <hi>is</hi> not wise.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:2
verses.text: The fear of a king <hi>is</hi> as the roaring of a lion; whoever stirs him up to anger sins against his own soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:3
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> an honor for a man to cease from strife, but every fool exposes himself.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:4
verses.text: The lazy one will not plow; after the autumn he shall beg in harvest and have nothing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:5
verses.text: Wisdom in the heart of man <hi>is like</hi> deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:6
verses.text: Most men will proclaim each his own goodness, but a faithful man who can find?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:7
verses.text: The just walks in his integrity; his sons <hi>are</hi> blessed after him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:8
verses.text: A king who sits in the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:9
verses.text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean; I am pure from my sin?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:10
verses.text: Different kinds of weights, different kinds of measures, both <hi>are</hi> hateful to the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:11
verses.text: Even a child is known by his own doings, whether his work <hi>is</hi> pure and whether <hi>it is</hi> right.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:12
verses.text: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the LORD has made both of them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:13
verses.text: Do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty; open your eyes and you shall be satisfied with bread.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:14
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> bad! Bad, says the buyer; but when <hi>it is</hi> left to him, then he boasts.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:15
verses.text: There is gold and a multitude of rubies; but the lips of knowledge <hi>are</hi> a rare jewel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:16
verses.text: Take the garment of him who is surety <hi>for</hi> a stranger; and take a pledge from him for strangers.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:17
verses.text: Bread of deceit <hi>is</hi> sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:18
verses.text: Purposes are established by counsel; and with good advice make war.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:19
verses.text: A gossip is a revealer of secrets; so do not mix with him who flatters with his lips.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:20
verses.text: Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in deep darkness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:21
verses.text: An inheritance gotten hastily in the beginning, even the end of it shall not be blessed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:22
verses.text: Do not say, I will repay evil; wait on the LORD, and He will save you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:23
verses.text: Different kinds of weights <hi>are</hi> hateful to the LORD, and a false balance <hi>is</hi> not good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:24
verses.text: Man's steps <hi>are</hi> of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:25
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> a snare <hi>to</hi> a man to say rashly, A holy thing, and afterward vows to ask <hi>about it</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:26
verses.text: A wise king scatters the wicked and brings the wheel over them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:27
verses.text: The spirit of man <hi>is</hi> the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:28
verses.text: Mercy and truth preserve the king; and his throne is upheld by mercy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:29
verses.text: The glory of young men <hi>is</hi> their strength; and the beauty of old men <hi>is</hi> the gray head.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:30
verses.text: The stripes of a wound cleanses away evil, and strokes the inward parts of the belly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:1
verses.text: The king's heart <hi>is</hi> in the hand of the LORD <hi>as</hi> the rivers of water; He turns it wherever He will.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:2
verses.text: Every way of a man <hi>is</hi> right in his own eyes, but the LORD ponders the hearts.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:3
verses.text: To do justice and judgment <hi>is</hi> more pleasing to the LORD than sacrifice.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:4
verses.text: A high look, a proud heart, <hi>and</hi> the plowing of the wicked, <hi>is</hi> sin.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:5
verses.text: The thoughts of the diligent <hi>tend</hi> only to plenty; but the thoughts of everyone <hi>who is</hi> hasty only to poverty.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:6
verses.text: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue <hi>is</hi> a vanity tossed to and fro by those who seek death.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:7
verses.text: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them, because they refuse to do judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:8
verses.text: The way of a guilty man <hi>is</hi> perverted; but the pure, his work <hi>is</hi> right.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:9
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than <hi>with</hi> a quarrelsome woman and to share a house.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:10
verses.text: The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:11
verses.text: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise; and when the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:12
verses.text: The righteous wisely considers the house of the wicked; <hi>but God</hi> overthrows the wicked for <hi>their</hi> wickedness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:13
verses.text: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:14
verses.text: A gift in secret quiets anger; and a bribe in the bosom quiets strong wrath.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:15
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> joy to the just to do judgment, but ruin <hi>shall be</hi> to the workers of iniquity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:16
verses.text: The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of departed spirits.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:17
verses.text: He who loves pleasure <hi>shall be</hi> a poor man; he who loves wine and oil shall not be rich.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:18
verses.text: The wicked <hi>shall be</hi> a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:19
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better to dwell in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry woman.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:20
verses.text: A desirable treasure and oil <hi>are</hi> in the home of the wise; but a foolish man swallows it up.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:21
verses.text: He who follows after righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness, and honor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:22
verses.text: A wise one scales the city of the mighty and brings down the strength of its hope.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:23
verses.text: Whoever keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:24
verses.text: Proud, haughty scorner <hi>is</hi> his name, he who deals in proud wrath.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:25
verses.text: The desire of the lazy man kills him, for his hands have refused to work.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:26
verses.text: He covets greedily all the day long; but the righteous gives and spares not.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:27
verses.text: The sacrifice of the wicked <hi>is</hi> hateful to God; how much more <hi>when</hi> he brings it with a wicked mind?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:28
verses.text: A false witness shall perish, but the man who hears speaks on and on.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:29
verses.text: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright establishes his way.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:30
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:31
verses.text: The horse <hi>is</hi> prepared for the day of battle; but safety <hi>is</hi> from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:1
verses.text: A <hi>good</hi> name <hi>is</hi> rather to be chosen than great riches; <hi>and</hi> loving favor rather than silver or gold.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:2
verses.text: The rich and poor meet together; the LORD <hi>is</hi> the maker of them all.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:3
verses.text: A prudent one foresees the evil and hides himself, but the simple pass on and are punished.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:4
verses.text: By humility <hi>and</hi> the fear of the LORD <hi>are</hi> riches and honor and life.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:5
verses.text: Thorns <hi>and</hi> snares <hi>are</hi> in the way of the perverse; he who keeps his soul shall be far from them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:6
verses.text: Train up a child in the way he should go; and when he is old, he will not depart from it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:7
verses.text: The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower <hi>is</hi> servant to the lender.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:8
verses.text: He who sows iniquity shall reap vanity; and the rod of his anger shall fail.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:9
verses.text: He who has a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he gives of his bread to the poor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:10
verses.text: Cast out the scorner, and fighting shall go out; yes, quarrels and shame shall cease.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:11
verses.text: He who loves pureness of heart, grace is on his lips; the king <hi>shall be</hi> his friend.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:12
verses.text: The eyes of the LORD keep knowledge, and He overthrows the words of the transgressor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:13
verses.text: The lazy one says, <hi>There is</hi> a lion outside; I shall be killed in the streets.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:14
verses.text: The mouth of strange women <hi>is</hi> a deep pit; those despised <hi>by</hi> the LORD shall fall there.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:15
verses.text: Foolishness <hi>is</hi> bound in the heart of a child; the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:16
verses.text: He who crushes the poor to multiply for himself, and he who gives to the rich, only <hi>to come</hi> to poverty.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:17
verses.text: Bow down your ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to My knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:18
verses.text: For <hi>it is</hi> a pleasant thing if you keep them within you; they shall all be fitted in your lips,

verses.name: Proverbs 22:19
verses.text: so that your trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to you this day, even to you.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:20
verses.text: Have I not written to you excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

verses.name: Proverbs 22:21
verses.text: that I might make you know the sureness of the words of truth; to return the words of truth to those who send to you?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:22
verses.text: Do not rob the poor, because he <hi>is</hi> poor; nor press down the afflicted in the gate;

verses.name: Proverbs 22:23
verses.text: for the LORD will plead their cause, and strip the soul of those who plunder them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:24
verses.text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and you shall not go up with a man of fury,

verses.name: Proverbs 22:25
verses.text: lest you learn his ways and get a snare to your soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:26
verses.text: Be not one of those who strike hands, of those who are sureties for debts.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:27
verses.text: If you have nothing to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:28
verses.text: Do not remove the old landmark which your fathers have set.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:29
verses.text: Do you see a man diligent in his business? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before unknown <hi>men</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:1
verses.text: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, look carefully at what <hi>is</hi> before you;

verses.name: Proverbs 23:2
verses.text: and put a knife to your throat, if you <hi>are</hi> a man given to appetite.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:3
verses.text: Do not desire his delicacies, for they <hi>are</hi> deceitful food.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:4
verses.text: Do not labor to be rich; cease from your own understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:5
verses.text: Will your eyes fly on it? And <hi>it</hi> is gone! For surely it makes wings for itself; it flies <hi>into</hi> the heavens like an eagle.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:6
verses.text: Do not eat the bread of <hi>him who has</hi> an evil eye, nor desire his dainty foods;

verses.name: Proverbs 23:7
verses.text: for as he thinks in his heart, so <hi>is</hi> he; Eat and drink, he says to you, but his heart <hi>is</hi> not with you.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:8
verses.text: Your bit <hi>which</hi> you have eaten, you shall vomit up, and spoil your pleasant words.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:9
verses.text: Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:10
verses.text: Do not remove the old landmarks, and do not enter into the fields of the fatherless;

verses.name: Proverbs 23:11
verses.text: for their Redeemer <hi>is</hi> mighty; He shall plead their cause with you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:12
verses.text: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to the words of knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:13
verses.text: Do not withhold correction from a boy, for <hi>if</hi> you beat him with the rod, he will not die.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:14
verses.text: You shall beat him with the rod, and shall deliver his soul from hell.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:15
verses.text: My son, if your heart is wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:16
verses.text: Yea, my heart shall rejoice when your lips speak right things.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:17
verses.text: Do not let your heart envy sinners; but <hi>be</hi> in the fear of the LORD all the day long.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:18
verses.text: For surely there is a hereafter, and your hope shall not be cut off.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:19
verses.text: My son, hear and be wise, and guide your heart in the way.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:20
verses.text: Do not be among those who drink much wine, among gluttons for flesh for themselves,

verses.name: Proverbs 23:21
verses.text: for the drunkard and the glutton lose all, and sleepiness shall clothe <hi>a man</hi> with rags.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:22
verses.text: Listen to your father who sired you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:23
verses.text: Buy the truth, and sell <hi>it</hi> not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:24
verses.text: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice; and he who fathers a wise <hi>child</hi> shall have joy from him.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:25
verses.text: Your father and your mother shall be glad, and she who bore you shall rejoice.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:26
verses.text: My son, give Me your heart, and let your eyes watch My ways.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:27
verses.text: For a harlot <hi>is</hi> a deep ditch, and a strange woman <hi>is</hi> a narrow pit.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:28
verses.text: She also lies in wait as <hi>for</hi> prey, and increases the treacherous among men.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:29
verses.text: Who <hi>has</hi> woe? Who has sorrow? Who <hi>has</hi> fighting? Who <hi>has</hi> babbling? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes?

verses.name: Proverbs 23:30
verses.text: Those who stay long at the wine, those who go to seek mixed wine.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:31
verses.text: Do not look upon the wine when it is red, <hi>when</hi> it gives its color in the cup, <hi>when</hi> it goes down smoothly

verses.name: Proverbs 23:32
verses.text: At the last it bites like an asp and stings like an adder.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:33
verses.text: Your eyes shall look upon strange women and your heart shall speak perverse things.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:34
verses.text: Yes, you shall be as one who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as one who lies upon the top of a mast,

verses.name: Proverbs 23:35
verses.text: <hi> saying</hi>, They struck me; I was not sick; they beat me, <hi>but</hi> I did not know it. When I awaken, I will add <hi>more</hi>. I will seek it again.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:1
verses.text: Do not be jealous of evil men, nor desire to be with them.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:2
verses.text: For their heart studies ruin, and their lips talk of mischief.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:3
verses.text: Through wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:4
verses.text: and by knowledge the rooms shall be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:5
verses.text: A wise man <hi>is</hi> strong; yes, a man of knowledge increases strength.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:6
verses.text: For by wise counsel you shall make your war; and in a multitude of wise men <hi>there is</hi> safety.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:7
verses.text: Wisdom <hi>is</hi> too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the gate.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:8
verses.text: He who plots to do evil shall be called a master of wicked thoughts.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:9
verses.text: The thought of foolishness <hi>is</hi> sin; and the scorner <hi>is</hi> hateful to men.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:10
verses.text: <hi> If</hi> you faint in the day of trial, your strength <hi>is</hi> small.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:11
verses.text: Deliver those being taken to death, and those stumbling to be killed, unless you hold back.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:12
verses.text: if you say, Behold, we did not know; does not He who searches the heart consider it? And the Keeper of your soul, does He know? And He repays to a man according to his works?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:13
verses.text: My son, eat honey, because <hi>it is</hi> good; and the honeycomb, <hi>is</hi> sweet to your palate;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:14
verses.text: so <hi>shall</hi> the knowledge of wisdom <hi>be</hi> to your soul; when you have found it, then there shall be a reward, and your hope shall not be cut off.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:15
verses.text: Wicked one, do not lie in ambush at the dwelling of the righteous; do not spoil his resting place;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:16
verses.text: for a just one falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked shall fall into evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:17
verses.text: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:18
verses.text: lest the LORD see, and it displease Him, and He turn away His wrath from him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:19
verses.text: Do not fret yourself because of evil ones, nor be jealous of the wicked;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:20
verses.text: for there shall be not be a hereafter to the evil; the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:21
verses.text: My son, fear the LORD and the king; <hi>and</hi> do not fellowship with those who are given to change;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:22
verses.text: for their trouble shall rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin of them both?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:23
verses.text: These also <hi>are</hi> for the wise: To have respect of persons in judgment <hi>is</hi> not good.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:24
verses.text: He who says to the wicked, You <hi>are</hi> righteous; the people shall curse him <hi>and</hi> nations shall abhor him.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:25
verses.text: But to those who rebuke <hi>him</hi>, it shall be a delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:26
verses.text: He shall kiss the lips that return right words.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:27
verses.text: Prepare your work outside, and make it fit for yourself in the field; and afterwards build your house.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:28
verses.text: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, nor deceive with your lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:29
verses.text: Do not `say, I will do so to him as he has done to me; I will give to the man according to his work.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:30
verses.text: I went by the field of the lazy man, and by the vineyard of the man without understanding;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:31
verses.text: and, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, <hi>and</hi> nettles had covered the face of it, and its stone wall was broken down.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:32
verses.text: Then I saw; I set my heart on it; I looked and I received instruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:33
verses.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:34
verses.text: then your poverty comes stalking, and your want like an a man <hi>armed with</hi> a shield.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:1
verses.text: These <hi>are</hi> also proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:2
verses.text: The glory of God <hi>is</hi> to hide a thing; but the honor of kings <hi>is</hi> to search out a matter.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:3
verses.text: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, but the heart of kings <hi>is</hi> without searching.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:4
verses.text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the refiner.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:5
verses.text: Take away the wicked <hi>from</hi> before the king, and his throne shall be founded in righteousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:6
verses.text: Do not put yourself forth in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of the great;

verses.name: Proverbs 25:7
verses.text: for <hi>it is</hi> better that it should be said to you, Come up here, than that you should be put lower in the presence of a noble whom your eyes have seen.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:8
verses.text: Do not go forth quickly to fight, lest <hi>you know not</hi> what to do in the end of it, when your neighbor has put you to shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:9
verses.text: Debate your cause with your neighbor; and do not uncover a secret to another,

verses.name: Proverbs 25:10
verses.text: lest he who hears <hi>it</hi> put you to shame, and your evil report turn not away.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:11
verses.text: A word fitly spoken <hi>is like</hi> apples of gold in pictures of silver.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:12
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> a ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, <hi>so is</hi> a wise reprover upon a hearing ear.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:13
verses.text: Like cold snow in the time of harvest, <hi>so is</hi> a faithful messenger to his senders; <hi>for</hi> he makes return <hi>to</hi> his master's soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:14
verses.text: A man boasting himself in a false gift <hi>is like</hi> clouds and wind, but no rain.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:15
verses.text: In <hi>being</hi> slow to anger a ruler is won over, and a soft tongue breaks the bone.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:16
verses.text: Have you found honey? Eat <hi>only</hi> as much as is enough for you, lest you be filled with it and vomit it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:17
verses.text: Withdraw your foot from your neighbor's house, lest he be weary of you and hate you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:18
verses.text: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor <hi>is</hi> a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:19
verses.text: Trust in an unfaithful man in time of trouble <hi>is like</hi> a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:20
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> he who takes away a garment in cold weather, <hi>as</hi> vinegar upon niter, <hi>so is</hi> he who sings songs to a heavy heart.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:21
verses.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,

verses.name: Proverbs 25:22
verses.text: for you shall heap coals <hi>of fire</hi> upon his head, and the LORD shall reward you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:23
verses.text: The north wind drives away rain; so <hi>does</hi> an angry face a backbiting tongue.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:24
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than with a quarreling woman and to share a house.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:25
verses.text: <hi> Like</hi> cold waters to a thirsty soul, <hi>so is</hi> good news from a far country.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:26
verses.text: A righteous man falling down before the wicked <hi>is like</hi> a troubled fountain and a rotten spring.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:27
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> not good to eat much honey; so <hi>for men</hi> to search their own glory <hi>is not</hi> glory.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:28
verses.text: He who <hi>has</hi> no rule over his own spirit <hi>is like a</hi> broken down city without a wall.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:1
verses.text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor <hi>is</hi> not becoming for a fool.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:2
verses.text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse without cause shall not come.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:3
verses.text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:4
verses.text: Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, lest you also be like him.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:5
verses.text: Answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that he may not be wise in his own eyes.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:6
verses.text: He who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off the feet <hi>and</hi> drinks down damage.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:7
verses.text: The legs of the lame <hi>are</hi> not equal; so <hi>is</hi> a parable in the mouth of fools.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:8
verses.text: As he who binds a stone in a sling, so <hi>is</hi> he who gives honor to a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:9
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so <hi>is</hi> a parable in the mouth of fools.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:10
verses.text: Great <hi>is</hi> the Former of all, but he who hires a fool <hi>is like</hi> one who hires one passing by.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:11
verses.text: As a dog returns to its vomit, <hi>so</hi> a fool returns to his folly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:12
verses.text: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? <hi>There is</hi> more hope for a fool than for him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:13
verses.text: The lazy one says, <hi>There is</hi> a lion in the way; a lion <hi>is</hi> in the streets.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:14
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> the door turns upon its hinges, <hi>so does</hi> the lazy man turn upon his bed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:15
verses.text: The lazy man hides his hand in <hi>his</hi> bosom; it grieves him to bring it again to his mouth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:16
verses.text: The sluggard <hi>is</hi> wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can give a reason.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:17
verses.text: He who passes by enraging himself over strife not his own <hi>is like</hi> one who takes a dog by the ears,  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:18
verses.text: <hi> or</hi> like a madman who throws firebrands, arrows, and death.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:19
verses.text: so <hi>is</hi> the man who deceives his neighbor and says, Am I not joking.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:20
verses.text: Where there is no wood, the fire goes out; and where <hi>there is</hi> no talebearer, the fighting ceases.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:21
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> coals to burning coals, and wood to fire, so <hi>is</hi> a quarrelsome man to kindle fighting.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:22
verses.text: The words of a talebearer <hi>are</hi> as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:23
verses.text: Burning lips and a wicked heart <hi>are like</hi> a broken piece of pottery with silver waste.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:24
verses.text: He who hates pretends with his lips and stores up deceit within him.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:25
verses.text: When he makes his voice gracious, do not believe him; for seven hateful things <hi>are</hi> in his heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:26
verses.text: <hi> He whose</hi> hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the congregation.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:27
verses.text: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it; and he who rolls a stone, it will return on him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:28
verses.text: A lying tongue hates <hi>those</hi> afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:1
verses.text: Do not boast yourself of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:2
verses.text: Let another man praise you, and not your mouth; a stranger, and not your lips.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:3
verses.text: A stone <hi>is</hi> heavy, and sand <hi>is</hi> heavy; but a fool's wrath <hi>is</hi> heavier than them both.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:4
verses.text: Wrath <hi>is</hi> cruel, and anger <hi>is</hi> overwhelming; but who <hi>is</hi> able to stand before envy?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:5
verses.text: Open rebuke <hi>is</hi> better than secret love.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:6
verses.text: Faithful <hi>are</hi> the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy <hi>are</hi> deceitful.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:7
verses.text: The full soul despises a honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing <hi>is</hi> sweet.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:8
verses.text: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so <hi>is</hi> a man who wanders from his place.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:9
verses.text: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart; so does the sweetness of one's friend by advice from the heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:10
verses.text: Your own friend, and your father's friend, do not forsake them; nor go to your brother's house in the day of your trouble; better <hi>is</hi> a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:11
verses.text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer him who shames me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:12
verses.text: A sensible one foresees the evil <hi>and</hi> hides himself, but the simple pass on <hi>and</hi> are punished.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:13
verses.text: Take his robe that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for a strange woman.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:14
verses.text: He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:15
verses.text: A never-ending dropping in a very rainy day and a quarrelsome woman are alike.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:16
verses.text: Whoever hides her hides the wind, and his right <hi>hand</hi> encounters <hi>slippery</hi> oil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:17
verses.text: Iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the face of his friend.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:18
verses.text: Whoever keeps the fig tree shall eat its fruit; so he who waits on his master shall be honored.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:19
verses.text: As in water face <hi>answers</hi> to face, so the heart of man <hi>answers</hi> to man.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:20
verses.text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:21
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> the refining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, so <hi>is</hi> a man to his praise.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:22
verses.text: Though you should pound a fool in a bowl with a bar in the midst of wheat, his foolishness will not depart from him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:23
verses.text: Know well the face of your flocks; set your heart on your herds.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:24
verses.text: For riches <hi>are</hi> not forever; nor the crown from generation to generation?

verses.name: Proverbs 27:25
verses.text: When the hay is removed, and the tender grass is seen, and mountain-plants are gathered,

verses.name: Proverbs 27:26
verses.text: the lambs <hi>are</hi> for your clothing, and the goats <hi>are</hi> the price of the field.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:27
verses.text: And <hi>you shall have</hi> goats' milk enough for your food, for the food of your household, and a living for your young women.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:1
verses.text: The wicked flee <hi>when</hi> no man pursues; but the righteous are bold as a lion.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:2
verses.text: Because of the transgression of a land, many <hi>are</hi> its rulers; but <hi>it is</hi> prolonged by a man of discernment who knows <hi>right</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:3
