verses.text: A poor man who crushes the poor <hi>is like</hi> a sweeping rain which leaves no food.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:4
verses.text: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law plead against them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:5
verses.text: Evil men do not understand judgment; but those who seek the LORD understand all <hi>things</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:6
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> the poor who walks in his uprightness than he who <hi>is</hi> perverse <hi>in his</hi> ways, though he <hi>is</hi> rich.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:7
verses.text: Whoever keeps the law <hi>is</hi> a wise son, but a companion of gluttons shames his father.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:8
verses.text: He who increases his wealth by interest and unjust gain, <hi>he shall</hi> gather it for him who will pity the poor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:9
verses.text: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer <hi>is</hi> a hateful thing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:10
verses.text: Whoever causes the righteous man to go astray in an evil way, he himself shall fall into his own pit; but the upright shall inherit good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:11
verses.text: The rich man <hi>is</hi> wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding searches him out.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:12
verses.text: When the righteous rejoice, <hi>there is</hi> great glory; but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:13
verses.text: He who covers his sins shall not be blessed; but whoever confesses and leaves <hi>them</hi> shall have mercy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:14
verses.text: Blessed <hi>is</hi> the man dreading <hi>God</hi>, but he who hardens his heart shall fall into mischief.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:15
verses.text: <hi> Like</hi> a roaring lion and a ranging bear, <hi>so is</hi> a wicked ruler over the helpless people.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:16
verses.text: A ruler lacking understanding even adds oppressions; he who hates unjust gain shall prolong <hi>his</hi> days.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:17
verses.text: A man who is pressed down with the blood of a soul shall flee to the pit; do not let them uphold him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:18
verses.text: Whoever walks uprightly shall be saved; but he who is perverse <hi>in his</hi> ways shall fall at once.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:19
verses.text: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he pursuing vanities shall have poverty enough.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:20
verses.text: A faithful man shall overflow with blessings, but he who makes haste to be rich shall not be innocent.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:21
verses.text: To have respect of persons <hi>is</hi> not good; yea, for a piece of bread a man will transgress.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:22
verses.text: He who hastens to be rich <hi>has</hi> an evil eye, and does not know that poverty will come upon him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:23
verses.text: He who rebukes a man shall afterwards find <hi>more</hi> favor than he who flatters <hi>with</hi> the tongue.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:24
verses.text: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, <hi>It is</hi> no sin he <hi>shall be</hi> a companion to a destroyer.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:25
verses.text: He who is of a proud heart stirs up fighting; but he who puts his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:26
verses.text: He who trusts in his own heart is a fool; but whoever walks wisely, he shall be delivered.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:27
verses.text: He who gives to the poor shall not lack, but he who hides his eyes shall have many a curse.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:28
verses.text: When the wicked rise, a man hides himself, but when they perish, the righteous increase.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:1
verses.text: A man who hardens <hi>his</hi> neck <hi>when</hi> reproved shall be suddenly broken, and there will be no healing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:2
verses.text: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people mourn.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:3
verses.text: Whoever loves wisdom rejoices his father; but a companion of harlots wastes wealth.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:4
verses.text: The king establishes the land by judgment; but he <hi>taking</hi> bribes tears it down.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:5
verses.text: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:6
verses.text: In the sin of an evil man <hi>there is</hi> a snare; but the righteous sings and rejoices.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:7
verses.text: The righteous knows the plea of the poor; the wicked cares not to know it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:8
verses.text: Scornful men bring a city into a snare, but the wise turn away wrath.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:9
verses.text: <hi> If</hi> a wise man contends with a foolish man, whether he rages or laughs, <hi>there is</hi> no rest.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:10
verses.text: Men of blood hate the upright; but the just seek his soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:11
verses.text: A fool speaks all his mind; but a wise one keeps it in until afterwards.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:12
verses.text: If a ruler listens to lies, all his servants <hi>are</hi> wicked.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:13
verses.text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:14
verses.text: A king who truly judges the weak, his throne shall be established forever.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:15
verses.text: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a boy sent off causes shame to his mother.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:16
verses.text: When the wicked are multiplied, sin increases; but the righteous shall see their fall.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:17
verses.text: Correct your son, and he shall give you rest; yea, he shall give delight to your soul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:18
verses.text: Where <hi>there is</hi> no wisdom, the people perish; but he who keeps the law, he <hi>is</hi> blessed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:19
verses.text: A servant will not be corrected by words, for though he understands, he will not answer.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:20
verses.text: Do you see a man hasty in his words? <hi>There is</hi> more hope for a fool than for him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:21
verses.text: He pampering his servant from youth, <hi>that one</hi> in his after days shall <hi>his</hi> successor.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:22
verses.text: An angry man stirs up fighting, and a furious man abounds in sin.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:23
verses.text: A man's pride shall bring him low; but honor shall uphold the humble in spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:24
verses.text: He who shares with a thief hates his own soul; he hears an oath and does not tell.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:25
verses.text: The fear of man brings a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the LORD shall be safe.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:26
verses.text: Many seek the ruler's favor; but each man's judgment <hi>comes</hi> from the LORD.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:27
verses.text: An unjust man <hi>is</hi> a hateful thing to the just; and <hi>he who is</hi> upright in the way <hi>is</hi> hateful to the wicked.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:1
verses.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the prophecy: The man spoke to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal, saying,

verses.name: Proverbs 30:2
verses.text: Surely I <hi>am more</hi> like an animal than any man, and do not have the understanding of a man.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:3
verses.text: I have not learned wisdom, nor the knowledge of the holy.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:4
verses.text: Who has gone up <hi>to</hi> Heaven and has come down? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has bound the waters in <hi>His</hi> garments? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What <hi>is</hi> His name, and what <hi>is</hi> His Son's name? Surely you know.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:5
verses.text: Every word of God <hi>is</hi> pure; He <hi>is</hi> a shield to those who put their trust in Him.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:6
verses.text: Do not add to His words, lest He reprove you and you be found a liar.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:7
verses.text: I have asked two things from You; do not deny them before I die;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:8
verses.text: remove far from me vanity and a lying word; give me neither poverty or riches; tear for me my portion of bread,

verses.name: Proverbs 30:9
verses.text: lest I be full and deceive, and say, Who <hi>is</hi> the LORD? Or lest I be poor, and steal, and violate the name of my God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:10
verses.text: Do not accuse a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be found guilty.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:11
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> a generation that curses their father, and does not bless their mother.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:12
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> a generation <hi>that are</hi> pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their own filth.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:13
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:14
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaw teeth like knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from <hi>among</hi> men.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:15
verses.text: The leech <hi>has</hi> two daughters, <hi>crying</hi>, Give, give! Three things are never satisfied, yea, four things never say, Enough!

verses.name: Proverbs 30:16
verses.text: The grave; and the barren womb, the earth not filled <hi>with</hi> water, and the fire, have not said, Enough.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:17
verses.text: The eye <hi>that</hi> mocks at <hi>his</hi> father and despises to obey <hi>his</hi> mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:18
verses.text: Three <hi>things are</hi> too wonderful for me, yea, four which I do not know:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:19
verses.text: the way of an eagle in the air; the way of a snake on a rock; the way of a ship in the middle of the sea; and the way of a man with a maiden.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:20
verses.text: Such <hi>is</hi> the way of an adulterous woman; she eats, and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:21
verses.text: Under three <hi>things</hi> the earth quakes, and under four it is not able to bear up:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:22
verses.text: for a servant when he reigns; and a fool when he is filled with food;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:23
verses.text: for a hateful woman when she is married; and a servant girl that is heir to her mistress.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:24
verses.text: Four <hi>things are</hi> little on the earth, but they <hi>are</hi> exceedingly wise:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:25
verses.text: the ants <hi>are</hi> a people not strong, yet they prepare their food in the summer;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:26
verses.text: the rock-badgers <hi>are</hi> not a mighty people, yet they make their houses in the rock;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:27
verses.text: the locusts have no king, yet they go forth by bands, all of them;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:28
verses.text: you can take the lizard with the hands, yet it <hi>is</hi> in king's palaces.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:29
verses.text: There <hi>are</hi> three <hi>things</hi> which go well in a march, yea, four that go well in walking:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:30
verses.text: a lion <hi>is</hi> mighty among beasts and does not turn away for any;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:31
verses.text: one girded in the loins; and a he-goat; and a king <hi>when his</hi> army <hi>is</hi> with him.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:32
verses.text: If you have done foolishly in lifting yourself up, or if you have thought evil, <hi>lay your</hi> hand on your mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:33
verses.text: Surely the churning of milk brings forth butter, and the wringing of the nose brings forth blood; so the forcing of wrath brings forth fighting.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 31:1
verses.text: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy which his mother taught him.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:2
verses.text: What, my son? And what, the son of my womb? And what, the son of my vows?

verses.name: Proverbs 31:3
verses.text: Do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:4
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> not for kings, O Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes <hi>to lust</hi> for strong drink;

verses.name: Proverbs 31:5
verses.text: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:6
verses.text: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to those who are of heavy hearts.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:7
verses.text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:8
verses.text: Open your mouth for the dumb, for the cause of all the sons <hi>of those</hi> passing away.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:9
verses.text: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 31:10
verses.text: Who can find a woman of virtue? For her value <hi>is</hi> far above rubies.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:11
verses.text: The heart of her husband trusts safely in her, so that he shall have no need of plunder.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:12
verses.text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:13
verses.text: She seeks wool and flax, and works willingly <hi>with</hi> her hands.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:14
verses.text: She is like the merchants' ships; she brings her food from afar.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:15
verses.text: She also rises while <hi>it is</hi> still night, and gives food to her household, and a share to her young women.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:16
verses.text: She considers a field, and buys it; with the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:17
verses.text: She binds her loins with strength, and makes her arms strong.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:18
verses.text: She sees that her merchandise <hi>is</hi> good; her lamp does not go out by night.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:19
verses.text: She lays her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:20
verses.text: She stretches out her hand to the poor; yea, she reaches forth her hands to the needy.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:21
verses.text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; for all her household <hi>are</hi> clothed <hi>with</hi> scarlet.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:22
verses.text: She makes herself coverings; her clothing <hi>is</hi> silk and purple.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:23
verses.text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:24
verses.text: She makes fine linen and sells <hi>it</hi>, and delivers girdles to the merchants.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:25
verses.text: Strength and honor <hi>are</hi> her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:26
verses.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue <hi>is</hi> the law of kindness.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:27
verses.text: She looks well to the ways of her household, and does not eat the bread of idleness.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:28
verses.text: Her sons rise up and call her blessed; her husband <hi>also</hi>, and he praises her.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:29
verses.text: Many daughters have done well, but you excel them all.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:30
verses.text: Favor <hi>is</hi> deceitful, and beauty <hi>is</hi> vain, <hi>but</hi> a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:31
verses.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:1
verses.text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:2
verses.text: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities! all <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:3
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> the profit to a man in all his labor which he labors under the sun?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:4
verses.text: A generation passes away, and a generation comes; but the earth remains forever.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:5
verses.text: The sun also arises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it arose.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:6
verses.text: The wind goes toward the south, and it turns around to the north; it whirls around continually; and the wind returns on its circuits.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:7
verses.text: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea <hi>is</hi> not full; to the place from where the rivers come, there they return again.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:8
verses.text: All things <hi>are</hi> full of labor; man cannot utter it; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:9
verses.text: That which has been <hi>is</hi> that which shall be; and that which has been done <hi>is</hi> that which shall be done; and <hi>there is</hi> nothing new under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:10
verses.text: Is there a thing <hi>of</hi> which it may be said, See, this <hi>is</hi> new? It has already been in days of old, which were before us.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:11
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> no memory of former <hi>things</hi>, and also of after <hi>things</hi> when he shall be; for neither shall be a remembrance of them with those who will be at the afterwards.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:12
verses.text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:13
verses.text: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all which is done under the heavens. <hi>It is</hi> a sad task God has given to the sons of men to be humbled by it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:14
verses.text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all <hi>is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:15
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> crooked cannot be made straight; and <hi>that</hi> lacking cannot be numbered.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:16
verses.text: I spoke within my own heart, saying, Lo, I have become great and have gathered more wisdom than all that have been before me in Jerusalem; yea, my heart has seen much of wisdom and knowledge.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:17
verses.text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly; I know that this also <hi>is</hi> vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:18
verses.text: For in much wisdom <hi>is</hi> much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:1
verses.text: I said in my heart, Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore consider and behold goodness; this also <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:2
verses.text: I said of laughter, <hi>It is</hi> madness; and of mirth, What does it do?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:3
verses.text: I sought in my heart to drag my flesh with wine, yet leading my heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, until I might see where the good for the sons of men might be, what they should do under the heavens all the days of their life.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:4
verses.text: I made my works great; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:5
verses.text: I made gardens and orchards for myself, And I planted trees in them, of all fruit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:6
verses.text: I made pools of water for myself, to water the forest shooting forth trees.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:7
verses.text: I bought slaves and slave women, and sons of the house were mine; also livestock, a herd and a great flock were mine, above all that were before me in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:8
verses.text: I also gathered silver and gold to myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got men singers and women singers for myself, and the delights of the sons of men, a wife and very many wives.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:9
verses.text: I was great and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom remained with me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:10
verses.text: And whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them; I did not withhold my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labor, and this was my part of all my labor.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:11
verses.text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had done, and on the labor that I had labored to do; and, behold, all <hi>is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit; and <hi>there is</hi> no profit under the sun.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:12
verses.text: And I turned to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what <hi>can</hi> the man <hi>do</hi> who comes after the king, when they have already done it?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:13
verses.text: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:14
verses.text: The wise man's eyes <hi>are</hi> in his head; but the fool walks in darkness; and I also knew that one event happens to all of them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:15
verses.text: Then I said in my heart, As it happens to the fool, <hi>so</hi> it happens even to me; and why was I then more wise? And I said in my heart that this also <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:16
verses.text: For <hi>there is</hi> no memory of the wise <hi>more than</hi> of the fool forever, since that which is now shall all be forgotten in the days to come. And how does the wise die above the fool!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:17
verses.text: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is done under the sun <hi>is</hi> sad to me; for all <hi>is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:18
verses.text: Yes, I hated all my labor which I had done under the sun; that I must leave it to the man who shall be after me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:19
verses.text: And who knows <hi>whether</hi> he shall be wise or a fool? Yet he shall have rule over all my labor in which I have labored, and acted wisely under the sun. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:20
verses.text: And I turned to cause my heart to despair over all the labor which I did under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:21
verses.text: When there is a man whose labor is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and with success; yet to a man who has not labored in it, he shall leave it <hi>for</hi> his share. This also is vanity and a great evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:22
verses.text: For what has man from all his labor, and from the troubling of his heart, in which he has labored under the sun?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:23
verses.text: For all his days <hi>are</hi> sorrows, and his labor sadness; yea, his heart does not take rest in the night. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:24
verses.text: Is it not good that he should eat and drink and make his soul see good in his labor? This I also saw, that it <hi>was</hi> from the hand of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:25
verses.text: For who can eat, or who can enjoy, apart from me?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:26
verses.text: For <hi>God</hi> gives wisdom, and knowledge, and joy to a man who <hi>is</hi> good in His sight. But to the sinner He gives labor, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to <hi>him who is</hi> good before God. This also <hi>is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:1
verses.text: To every thing <hi>there is</hi> a season, and a time for every purpose under the heavens:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:2
verses.text: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pull up what <hi>is</hi> planted;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:3
verses.text: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:4
verses.text: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:5
verses.text: a time to throw away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:6
verses.text: a time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:7
verses.text: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:8
verses.text: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:9
verses.text: What profit does he have who works in that in which he labors?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:10
verses.text: I have seen the task which God has given to the sons of men to be humbled by it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:11
verses.text: He has made everything beautiful in His time; also He has set eternity in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God makes from the beginning to the end.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:12
verses.text: I know that <hi>there is</hi> no good in them, but to rejoice and to do good in his life.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:13
verses.text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor, it <hi>is</hi> the gift of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:14
verses.text: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God does <hi>it</hi> so that they fear before Him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:15
verses.text: That which has been is now; and that which <hi>is</hi> to be has already been; and God requires that which is past.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:16
verses.text: And again I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness <hi>was</hi> there; and the place of righteousness, that wickedness <hi>was</hi> there.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:17
verses.text: I said in my heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked; for <hi>there is</hi> a time there for every purpose and for every work.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:18
verses.text: I said in my heart concerning the matter of sons of men, that God might reveal them, and that they might see that they themselves <hi>are</hi> beasts.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:19
verses.text: For that which happens <hi>to</hi> the sons of men also happens to beasts even one thing <hi>happens</hi> to them. As this <hi>one</hi> dies, so that <hi>one</hi> dies; yea, they all <hi>have</hi> one breath; so that a man has no advantage over a beast; for all <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:20
verses.text: All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust again.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:21
verses.text: Who knows the spirit of man <hi>that</hi> goes upward, and the spirit of the beast <hi>that</hi> goes downward?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:22
verses.text: Therefore I have seen that <hi>there is</hi> nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that <hi>is</hi> his portion; for who can bring him to see what shall be after him?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:1
verses.text: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And behold the tears of the oppressed ones, and hey had no comforter! And on the side of those who oppressed them there <hi>was</hi> power, but they had no comforter.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:2
verses.text: And I commended the dead who already have died, more than the living who <hi>are</hi> living now.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:3
verses.text: Yea, better than both <hi>is he</hi> who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:4
verses.text: Again, I considered all labor, and every right work, that for this a man is envied by his neighbor. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:5
verses.text: The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:6
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> a hand filled with rest than two fists <hi>with</hi> travail and vexation of spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:7
verses.text: And I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:8
verses.text: There is one <hi>alone</hi>, and <hi>there is</hi> not a second; yea, he has neither son nor brother; yet there is no end to all his labor; and his eyes are not satisfied with riches; and <hi>he says</hi>, For whom do I labor and take good from my soul? This <hi>is</hi> also vanity. Yes, it <hi>is</hi> an evil business.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:9
verses.text: Two <hi>are</hi> better than one; because they have a good reward for their labor.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:10
verses.text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him <hi>who is</hi> alone when he falls, for he does not have another to help him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:11
verses.text: Again, if two lie <hi>together</hi>, then they have warmth; but how can one be warm <hi>alone</hi>?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:12
verses.text: And if one overthrows him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:13
verses.text: A poor and a wise child <hi>is</hi> better than an old and foolish king, who will not be warned any more.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:14
verses.text: For out of prison he comes to reign; although in his kingdom he was born poor.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:15
verses.text: I saw all the living who walk under the sun, with the second child who shall stand up in his place.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:16
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> no end of all the people, of all who have been before them; they also who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also <hi>is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:1
verses.text: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools. For they do not know that they are doing evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:2
verses.text: Do not be rash <hi>with</hi> your mouth, and do not let your heart be hasty to say a word before God. For God <hi>is</hi> in Heaven, and you <hi>are</hi> on earth; therefore let your words be few.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:3
verses.text: For a dream comes through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice by the multitude of words.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:4
verses.text: When you vow a vow to God, do not wait to pay it. For He has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you have vowed.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:5
verses.text: <hi> it is</hi> better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:6
verses.text: Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin; do not say before the angel that it <hi>was</hi> an error. Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:7
verses.text: For in the multitude of dreams, both words and vanities abound; but fear God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:8
verses.text: If you see the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel at the matter. For He <hi>who is</hi> higher than the highest watches; and there are some higher than they.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:9
verses.text: And the advantage of a land, it is for all; <hi>even</hi> a king has a field being tilled.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:10
verses.text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves plenty does not gain. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:11
verses.text: When the good thing increases, those who eat it increase; then what profit <hi>is it</hi> to its owners, except to see <hi>it</hi> with their eyes?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:12
verses.text: The sleep of a laboring man <hi>is</hi> sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:13
verses.text: There is a sore evil <hi>which</hi> I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for their owners to their hurt.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:14
verses.text: But those riches perish by evil use. And he brings forth a son, and nothing <hi>is</hi> in his hand.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:15
verses.text: As he came forth from his mother's womb naked, he shall return to go as he came. And from his labor he may not carry anything that may go in his hand.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:16
verses.text: And this also <hi>is</hi> a sore evil, <hi>that</hi> in all, as he came, so shall he go; and what profit does he have who has labored for the wind?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:17
verses.text: Also all his days he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and wrath <hi>with</hi> his sickness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:18
verses.text: Behold that which I have seen. <hi>it is</hi> good and right for one to eat and to drink, and to see good in all his labor that he labors under the sun all the days of his life, which God gives him; for it <hi>is</hi> his portion.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:19
verses.text: Also every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor this <hi>is</hi> the gift of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:20
verses.text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life, because God answers <hi>him</hi> in the joy of his heart.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:1
verses.text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it <hi>is</hi> great among men:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:2
verses.text: a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to eat of it, but a stranger eats it. This <hi>is</hi> vanity, and it <hi>is</hi> an evil disease.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:3
verses.text: If a man fathers a hundred, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not filled with good, and also is for him no burial; I say, a miscarriage <hi>is</hi> better than he.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:4
verses.text: For he comes in with vanity and goes out in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:5
verses.text: Also he has not seen the sun, nor known <hi>anything</hi>. This one has more rest than the other.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:6
verses.text: Yea, though he live twice a thousand years, yet he has seen no good. Do not all go to one place?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:7
verses.text: All the labor of man <hi>is</hi> for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:8
verses.text: For what <hi>has</hi> the wise more than the fool? What <hi>gain has</hi> the poor who knows <hi>how</hi> to walk before the living?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:9
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:10
verses.text: That which has been <hi>is</hi> named already, and it is known that he <hi>is</hi> man. And he is not able to contend with Him who is mightier than he.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:11
verses.text: For there are many things that increase vanity, <hi>and</hi> what <hi>is</hi> man the better?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:12
verses.text: For who knows what <hi>is</hi> good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends as a shadow? For who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:1
verses.text: A good name <hi>is</hi> better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:2
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that <hi>is</hi> the end of all men; and the living will lay <hi>it</hi> to his heart.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:3
verses.text: Sorrow <hi>is</hi> better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made better.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:4
verses.text: The heart of the wise <hi>is</hi> in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools <hi>is</hi> in the house of laughter.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:5
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:6
verses.text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so <hi>is</hi> the laughter of the fool; this also <hi>is</hi> vanity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:7
verses.text: Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a bribe destroys the heart.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:8
verses.text: Better <hi>is</hi> the end of a thing than the beginning of it; the patient in spirit <hi>is</hi> better than the proud in spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:9
verses.text: Do not be hasty in your spirit to be angry; for anger rests in the bosom of fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:10
verses.text: Do not say, Why was <hi>it</hi> that the former days were better than these? For you do not ask wisely in regard to this.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:11
verses.text: Wisdom <hi>is</hi> good with an inheritance; but it is gain to those who see the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:12
verses.text: For wisdom <hi>is</hi> a defense, and money <hi>is</hi> a defense; but the excellency of knowledge <hi>is</hi> that wisdom gives life to those who have it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:13
verses.text: Consider the work of God; for who can make straight what He has made crooked?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:14
verses.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity take note <hi>that</hi> God also has set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:15
verses.text: All <hi>things</hi> I have seen in the days of my vanity; there is a just one who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked one who prolongs <hi>life</hi> in his wickedness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:16
verses.text: Do not be righteous overmuch, neither make yourself overwise; why destroy yourself?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:17
verses.text: Do not be very wicked, and do not be a fool; why should you die before your time?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:18
verses.text: <hi> It is</hi> good that you should take hold of this; yea, also from this do not withdraw your hand; for he who fears God shall come forth from all of them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:19
verses.text: Wisdom makes the wise stronger than ten mighty ones who are in the city.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:20
verses.text: For <hi>there is</hi> not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:21
verses.text: Also do not listen to all words that are spoken; lest you hear your servant curse you.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:22
verses.text: For also your own heart knows that you yourself have also cursed others many times.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:23
verses.text: All this I have proved by wisdom; I said, I will be wise; but it <hi>was</hi> far from me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:24
verses.text: That which is far off and exceedingly deep, who can find it out?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:25
verses.text: I set my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason <hi>of things</hi>, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:26
verses.text: and I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart <hi>is</hi> snares and nets, and her hands <hi>like</hi> bands. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:27
verses.text: Behold, this I have found, says the Preacher, <hi>counting</hi> one by one, to find out the sum,

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:28
verses.text: which my soul still sought, but I find not: one man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all those I have not found.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:29
verses.text: Lo, this only I have found, that God has made man upright, but they have sought out many inventions.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:1
verses.text: Who <hi>is</hi> as the wise? And who knows the meaning of a thing? A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:2
verses.text: I <hi>say</hi>, keep the king's word, and <hi>that</hi> because of the oath of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:3
verses.text: Do not be hasty to leave his presence. Do not take a stand in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:4
verses.text: Because the word of a king <hi>is</hi> that which has power; and who may say to him, What are you doing?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:5
verses.text: Whoever keeps the command shall feel no evil thing; and a wise man's heart knows both time and judgment.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:6
verses.text: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man <hi>is</hi> great on him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:7
verses.text: For he does not know what shall be; for who can tell him when it shall be?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:8
verses.text: <hi> There is</hi> no man who has power over the spirit to keep the spirit; nor power in the day of death; and <hi>there is</hi> no discharge in <hi>that</hi> war; nor shall wickedness deliver its owners.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:9
verses.text: All this I have seen, and I gave my heart to every work that is done under the sun. <hi>there is</hi> a time in which one man rules over another to his own hurt.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:10
verses.text: And so I saw the wicked buried, and they came and went from the holy place. And they were forgotten in the city, <hi>these</hi> things that they had done. This <hi>is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:11
verses.text: Because sentence <hi>against</hi> an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:12
verses.text: Though a sinner does evil a hundred <hi>times</hi>, and his <hi>days</hi> be made longer, yet surely I know that it shall be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:13
verses.text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, nor shall he make <hi>his</hi> days longer like a shadow; because he does not fear before God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:14
verses.text: There is a vanity which is done on the earth: There are just ones to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked ones to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:15
verses.text: Then I praised gladness, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat and to drink and to be glad; for that shall go with him of his labor for the days of his life which God gives him under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:16
verses.text: When I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth; for neither day nor night do men see sleep with their eyes.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:17
verses.text: Then I looked at all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; because though a man labors to seek <hi>it</hi> out, yet he shall not find it. Yea, further, though a wise one speaks of knowing, yet he shall not be able to find <hi>it</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:1
verses.text: For all this I took to heart, even to make all this clear, that the righteous and the wise and their works <hi>are</hi> in the hand of God. No man knows either love or hatred <hi>by</hi> all <hi>that is</hi> before them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:2
verses.text: All <hi>happens</hi> alike to all; <hi>there is</hi> one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him who sacrifices, and to him who does not sacrifice. As <hi>is</hi> the good, so is the sinner. He who swears is as <hi>he</hi> who fears an oath.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:3
verses.text: This <hi>is</hi> an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that <hi>there is</hi> one event to all. Yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness <hi>is</hi> in their heart while they live, and after that <hi>they go</hi> to the dead.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:4
verses.text: For whoever is chosen, to all those living, there is hope; for a living dog <hi>is</hi> better than a dead lion.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:5
verses.text: For the living know that they shall die; but the dead do not know anything, nor do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:6
verses.text: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; nor do they any longer have a part forever in all that is done under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:7
verses.text: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God now is pleased with your works.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:8
verses.text: Let your garments be always white; and let your head lack no ointment.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:9
verses.text: Look <hi>on</hi> life with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which He has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity. For that <hi>is</hi> your share in <hi>this</hi> life, and in your labor which you labor under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:10
verses.text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do <hi>it</hi> with all your might; for <hi>there is</hi> no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave where you go.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:11
verses.text: I returned and saw under the sun that the race <hi>is</hi> not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happens to them all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:12
verses.text: For man also does not know his time; as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so <hi>are</hi> the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:13
verses.text: This wisdom I have seen also under the sun, and it <hi>seemed</hi> great to me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:14
verses.text: <hi> There was</hi> a little city, and few men in it; and a great king came against it and besieged it, and built huge bulwarks against it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:15
verses.text: And a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that poor man.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:16
verses.text: And I said, Wisdom <hi>is</hi> better than strength; but the poor man's wisdom <hi>is</hi> despised, and his words are not heard.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:17
verses.text: The words of the wise <hi>are</hi> heard in quiet more than the cry of him who rules among fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:18
verses.text: Wisdom <hi>is</hi> better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:1
verses.text: As dead flies cause the perfumer's ointment to stink <hi>and</hi> ferment; <hi>so</hi> a little folly <hi>is more</hi> rare than wisdom <hi>and</hi> than honor.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:2
verses.text: A man's heart <hi>is</hi> at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:3
verses.text: Yes also, in the way a fool walks, his heart fails; and he says to all <hi>that</hi> he <hi>is</hi> a fool.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:4
verses.text: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, do not leave your place; for yielding quiets great sinners.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:5
verses.text: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, sins which comes from the ruler's face;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:6
verses.text: foolishness is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:7
verses.text: I have seen servants on horses and princes walking as servants on the earth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:8
verses.text: He who digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoever breaks a hedge, a snake shall bite him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:9
verses.text: Whoever removes stones shall be hurt with them. He who splits wood shall be endangered by it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:10
verses.text: If the iron is blunt, and he does not whet the edge, then he must put more strength to <hi>it</hi>. But wisdom <hi>is</hi> profitable to direct.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:11
verses.text: Surely the snake will bite without enchantment; and a babbler <hi>is</hi> no better.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:12
verses.text: The words of a wise mouth <hi>are</hi> gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:13
verses.text: The beginning of the words of his mouth <hi>is</hi> foolishness; and the end of his talk <hi>is</hi> wicked madness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:14
verses.text: A fool also makes many words; a man knows not what they shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:15
verses.text: The labor of fools wearies him, because he does not know <hi>how</hi> to go to the city.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:16
verses.text: Woe to you, O land, when your king <hi>is</hi> a child and your leaders eat in the morning.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:17
verses.text: Blessed <hi>are</hi> you, O land, when your king <hi>is</hi> the son of nobles, and your leaders eat in <hi>due</hi> time, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:18
verses.text: By slothfulness the building decays; and through lowering of the hands the house leaks.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:19
verses.text: Bread <hi>is</hi> made for laughter, and wine makes merry; but silver answers all <hi>things</hi>.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:20
verses.text: Do not curse a king, no, not in your thought; and do not curse the rich in your bedroom; for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:1
verses.text: Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:2
verses.text: Give a share to seven, and also to eight; for you know not what evil shall be on the earth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:3
verses.text: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty on the earth; and if the tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall be.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:4
verses.text: He who watches the wind shall not sow; and he who pays attention to the clouds shall not reap.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:5
verses.text: As you do not know what <hi>is</hi> the way of the spirit, as how the bones <hi>grow</hi> in the pregnant woman's womb; even so you do not know the works of God who makes all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:6
verses.text: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not withhold your hand; for you do not know what shall be blessed, either this or that, or whether they both <hi>shall be</hi> fruitful in the same way.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:7
verses.text: Also the light <hi>is</hi> sweet, and a pleasant thing <hi>it is</hi> for the eyes to behold the sun;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:8
verses.text: but if a man lives many years, <hi>and</hi> rejoices in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:9
verses.text: Rejoice, in your youth, young man; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these <hi>things</hi> God will bring you into judgment.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:10
verses.text: Therefore remove vexation from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for childhood and prime of life <hi>are</hi> vanity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:1
verses.text: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, while the evil days do not come, nor the years draw near, when you shall say, I have no pleasure in them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:2
verses.text: So long as the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are darkened, or the clouds return after rain,

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:3
verses.text: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men, are bowed, and the grinders cease because there are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:4
verses.text: and the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and you shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music are silenced;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:5
verses.text: also they are afraid of the high place, and terrors along the way, and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:6
verses.text: or ever the silver cord is not loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:7
verses.text: then the dust shall return to the earth as it was, and the spirit shall return to God who gave it.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:8
verses.text: Vanity of vanities, says the preacher; all <hi>is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:9
verses.text: And more than that, the preacher <hi>was</hi> wise; he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he listened, and looked, and set in order many proverbs.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:10
verses.text: The preacher sought to find out pleasing words; and words of truth written by the upright.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:11
verses.text: The words of the wise <hi>are</hi> like goads; yes, their collected words are like nails driven home; they <hi>are</hi> given from one Shepherd.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:12
verses.text: And further, by these, my son, be warned: The making of many books has no end, and much study <hi>is</hi> a weariness of the flesh.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:13
verses.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter. Fear God, and keep His commandments. For this <hi>is</hi> the whole <hi>duty</hi> of man.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:14
verses.text: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether <hi>it is</hi> good, or whether evil.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:1
verses.text: The song of songs, which <hi>is</hi> Solomon's.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:2
verses.text: Let Him kiss me with the kisses of His mouth; for Your loves <hi>are</hi> better than wine.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:3
verses.text: For Your ointments have a lovely fragrance; Your name is <hi>as</hi> oil poured out; therefore the virgins love You.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:4
verses.text: Draw me, we will run after You, The King has brought me into his chambers; we will be glad and rejoice in You, we will remember Your love more than wine; the upright love You.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:5
verses.text: I <hi>am</hi> black, but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:6
verses.text: Do not look on me, that I <hi>am</hi> black, that the sun has looked on me. My mother's sons were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; <hi>but</hi> my vineyard I have not kept.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:7
verses.text: Tell me, <hi>You</hi> whom my soul loves, where do You feed, where do You lie down at noon? For why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of Your companions?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:8
verses.text: If you know not, most beautiful among women, go in the footsteps of the flock; and feed your kids beside the shepherds' tents.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:9
verses.text: O My love, I have compared you to My mares among Pharaoh's chariots.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:10
verses.text: Your cheeks <hi>are</hi> beautiful with ornaments, your neck with chains.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:11
verses.text: We will make you borders of gold with studs of silver.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:12
verses.text: While the King is in His circle, my spikenard gives its smell.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:13
verses.text: A bundle of myrrh <hi>is</hi> my Beloved to me. <hi>He</hi> shall lie all night between my breasts.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:14
verses.text: My Beloved <hi>is</hi> to me <hi>like</hi> a cluster of henna in the vineyards of Engedi.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:15
verses.text: Behold, you <hi>are</hi> beautiful, my love; behold, you <hi>are</hi> beautiful; you <hi>have</hi> doves' eyes.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:16
verses.text: Behold, you <hi>are</hi> beautiful, my Beloved, yea, pleasant. Also our bed <hi>is</hi> green.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:17
verses.text: The beams of our house <hi>are</hi> cedar, <hi>and</hi> our rafters are of fir.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:1
verses.text: I <hi>am</hi> the rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:2
verses.text: As the lily among thorns, so <hi>is</hi> My love among the daughters.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:3
verses.text: As the apple among the trees of the wood, so <hi>is</hi> my Beloved among the sons. I sat down under His shadow with great delight, and His fruit <hi>was</hi> sweet to my taste.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:4
verses.text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and His banner over me <hi>was</hi> love.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:5
verses.text: Feed me with raisin cakes, comfort me with apples, for I <hi>am</hi> sick <hi>with</hi> love.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:6
verses.text: His left hand <hi>is</hi> under my head, and His right hand embraces me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:7
verses.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, and by the does of the field, do not stir up or awake <hi>my</hi> Love until He please.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:8
verses.text: The voice of my Beloved! Behold, He comes leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:9
verses.text: My Beloved is like a roe or a young hart. Behold, <hi>He</hi> stands behind our wall, He looks forth at the windows, peering from the lattice.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:10
verses.text: My Beloved spoke, and said to me, Rise up, My love, My beautiful one, and come away.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:11
verses.text: For lo, the winter is past, the rain is over; it goes to itself.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:12
verses.text: the flowers appear on the earth; the time of singing has come, and the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:13
verses.text: the fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines <hi>with</hi> the tender grape give a <hi>good</hi> smell. Arise, My love, My beautiful one, and come away.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:14
verses.text: O My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let Me see your face, let Me hear your voice; for your voice <hi>is</hi> sweet, and your face <hi>is</hi> beautiful.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:15
verses.text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vines; for our vines <hi>have</hi> tender grapes.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:16
verses.text: My Beloved <hi>is</hi> mine, and I <hi>am</hi> His; He feeds among the lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:17
verses.text: Until when does the day blow, and the shadows flee away? Turn, my Beloved, and be like a gazelle, or a young deer, the stag, on the mountains of Bether.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:1
verses.text: By night on my bed I sought Him whom my soul loved; I sought <hi>Him</hi>, but I did not find Him.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:2
verses.text: I will rise now and go about the city, in the streets and in the broad ways; I will seek <hi>Him</hi> whom my soul loves. I sought Him, but I did not find Him.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:3
verses.text: The watchmen going about the city found me. <hi>I said</hi>, Have you seen Him whom my soul loves?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:4
verses.text: But a little while after I passed from them, I found <hi>Him</hi> whom my soul loves. I held Him and would not let Him go, until I had brought Him into my mother's house, and into the room of her who conceived me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:5
verses.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, and by the does of the field, do not stir up nor awake <hi>my</hi> love until it pleases.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:6
verses.text: Who <hi>is</hi> this coming up out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, from all the merchant's powders?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:7
verses.text: Behold his bed, Solomon's! Sixty mighty men <hi>are</hi> around it, of Israel's mighty men.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:8
verses.text: They all hold swords, instructed in war; each man has his sword on his thigh because of fear in the night.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:9
verses.text: King Solomon made himself a litter-bed of Lebanon's trees.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:10
verses.text: He made its poles <hi>of</hi> silver, its back gold, its seat of purple, its middle was paved <hi>with</hi> love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:11
verses.text: Go forth, O daughters of Zion, and behold King Solomon with the crown <hi>with</hi> which his mother crowned him on his wedding day, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:1
verses.text: Behold, you <hi>are</hi> beautiful, My love. Behold, you <hi>are</hi> beautiful; your eyes <hi>are</hi> like doves' from behind your veil; your hair <hi>is</hi> like a flock of goats that appear from Mount Gilead.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:2
verses.text: Your teeth <hi>are</hi> like a flock of shorn <hi>sheep</hi>, which came up from the washing; they all are bearing twins and not one <hi>is</hi> barren among them.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:3
verses.text: Your lips <hi>are</hi> like a cord of scarlet, and your speech <hi>is</hi> becoming; your temples <hi>are</hi> like a piece of pomegranate behind your veil.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:4
verses.text: Your neck <hi>is</hi> like the tower of David built for an armory, on which there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:5
verses.text: Your two breasts <hi>are</hi> like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:6
verses.text: Until when the day blows, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:7
verses.text: You <hi>are</hi> all fair, My love; no blemish <hi>is</hi> in you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:8
verses.text: Come with Me from Lebanon, <hi>My</hi> spouse; with Me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:9
verses.text: You have ravished My heart, My sister, <hi>My</hi> spouse; you have ravished My heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:10
verses.text: How fair is your love, My sister, <hi>My</hi> spouse! How <hi>much</hi> better <hi>are</hi> your loves than wine, and the smell of your ointments than all spices!

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:11
verses.text: Your lips, <hi>My</hi> spouse, drop like the honeycomb; honey and milk <hi>are</hi> under your tongue; and the smell of your garments <hi>is</hi> like the smell of Lebanon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:12
verses.text: A locked garden <hi>is</hi> My sister, <hi>My</hi> spouse; a rock heap locked up, a fountain sealed.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:13
verses.text: Your plants <hi>are</hi> an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; with henna <hi>and</hi> spikenard,

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:14
verses.text: spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices;  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:15
verses.text: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:16
verses.text: Awake, O north <hi>wind</hi>; and come, south <hi>wind</hi>; blow on my garden, so <hi>that</hi> the spices of it may flow out. Let my Beloved come into His garden and eat His pleasant fruits.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:1
verses.text: I have come into My garden, My sister, <hi>My</hi> spouse; I have gathered My myrrh with My spice; I have eaten My honeycomb with My honey; I have drunk My wine with My milk. Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O Beloved.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:2
verses.text: I sleep, but my heart is awake. <hi>It is</hi> the sound of my Beloved that knocks, <hi>saying</hi>, Open to Me, My sister, My love, My dove, My undefiled; for My head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:3
verses.text: I have put off My coat; How shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:4
verses.text: My Beloved put in His hand by the hole <hi>of the door</hi>, and my heart was moved for Him.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:5
verses.text: I rose up to open to my Beloved; and my hands dripped <hi>with</hi> myrrh, and my fingers flowing <hi>with</hi> myrrh on the handles of the bolt.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:6
verses.text: I opened to my Beloved, but my Beloved had left. He passed on. My soul went out when He spoke; I sought Him, but I could not find Him. I called Him, but He did not answer me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:7
verses.text: The watchmen who went about the city found me <hi>and</hi> struck me; they wounded me. The keepers of the wall lifted my veil from me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:8
verses.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my Beloved, what do you tell Him? That I <hi>am</hi> sick <hi>with</hi> love.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:9
verses.text: What <hi>is</hi> your Beloved more than <hi>another</hi> beloved, most beautiful among women? What <hi>is</hi> your Beloved more than <hi>another</hi> beloved, that you adjure us so?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:10
verses.text: My Beloved <hi>is</hi> bright and ruddy, standing out among ten thousand.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:11
verses.text: His head <hi>is like</hi> refined gold; His locks <hi>are</hi> bushy, black as a raven.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:12
verses.text: His eyes <hi>are</hi> as doves' <hi>eyes</hi> on the rivers of waters, washed with milk, sitting on a setting.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:13
verses.text: His cheeks <hi>are</hi> like a bed of spices, a raised bed of aromatic herbs. His lips <hi>are as</hi> lilies dropping flowing myrrh.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:14
verses.text: His hands <hi>are like</hi> rings of gold filled with jewels; His body an ivory plate overlaid with sapphires.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:15
verses.text: His legs <hi>are like</hi> pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold; His face <hi>is like</hi> Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:16
verses.text: His mouth <hi>is</hi> most sweet; yes, He <hi>is</hi> altogether lovely. This <hi>is</hi> my Beloved, and this <hi>is</hi> my Friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:1
verses.text: Where has your Beloved gone, most beautiful among women? Where has your Beloved turned? For we seek Him along with you.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:2
verses.text: My Beloved has gone down to His garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens and to gather lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:3
verses.text: I <hi>am</hi> my Beloved's, and my Beloved <hi>is</hi> mine; He feeds among the lilies.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:4
verses.text: O my love, you <hi>are</hi> as beautiful as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as inspiring as an army with banners.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:5
verses.text: Turn away your eyes from Me, for they have overcome Me; your hair <hi>is</hi> like a flock of goats that appears from Gilead.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:6
verses.text: Your teeth <hi>are</hi> like a flock of ewes which go up from the washing; they all <hi>are</hi> bearing twins, and a barren one <hi>is</hi> not among them.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:7
verses.text: Your temples behind your veil <hi>are</hi> like a piece of pomegranate.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:8
verses.text: There <hi>are</hi> sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and virgins without number.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:9
verses.text: But My dove, My undefiled is one <hi>alone</hi>. She <hi>is</hi> the <hi>only</hi> one of her mother. She <hi>is</hi> the choice of her who bore her. The daughters saw <hi>her</hi> and blessed her; the queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:10
verses.text: Who <hi>is</hi> she who looks forth like the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, awesome <hi>armies</hi> with banners?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:11
verses.text: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the greenery of the valley, to see whether the vine flowered <hi>and</hi> the pomegranates budded.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:12
verses.text: I did not know, <hi>but</hi> my soul set me <hi>on</hi> the chariots of my princely people.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:13
verses.text: Return, return, O Shulamite! Return, return, that we may look on you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the dance of two camps.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:1
verses.text: How beautiful <hi>are</hi> your feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! The curves of your thighs <hi>are</hi> like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:2
verses.text: Your navel <hi>is like</hi> a round goblet, which never lacks mixed wine; your belly <hi>is like</hi> a heap of wheat set about with lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:3
verses.text: Your two breasts <hi>are</hi> like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:4
verses.text: Your neck <hi>is like</hi> a tower of ivory; your eyes <hi>like</hi> the fish-pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Beth-rabbim; your nose <hi>is like</hi> the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:5
verses.text: Your head on you <hi>is like</hi> Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple cloth; the King <hi>is</hi> held captive in its tresses.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:6
verses.text: How beautiful and how pleasant you <hi>are</hi>, O love, for delights!

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:7
verses.text: Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts <hi>are</hi> like clusters <hi>of grapes</hi>.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:8
verses.text: I said, I will go up in the palm tree, I will take hold of its stalk. And please let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the smell of your nose like apples;

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:9
verses.text: and the roof of your mouth like the best wine for my Beloved, that goes <hi>down</hi> smoothly for My Beloved, flowing softly <hi>over</hi> the lips of sleeping ones.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:10
verses.text: I <hi>am</hi> my Beloved's, and His desire <hi>is</hi> toward me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:11
verses.text: Come, my Beloved, let us go out into the field; let us stay in the villages.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:12
verses.text: Let us rise up early to the vineyards; let us see <hi>if</hi> the vine flowers, whether the tender grape appears, and the pomegranates bud forth; there I will give You my loves.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:13
verses.text: The love-apples give a scent, and over our doors <hi>are</hi> all pleasant <hi>fruits</hi>, new and old, which I have laid up for You, O my Beloved.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:1
