verses.text: O stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers <hi>did</hi>, so you do.

verses.name: Acts 7:52
verses.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of the Just One, of whom you have now been the betrayers and murderers;

verses.name: Acts 7:53
verses.text: who received the Law through disposition of angels, and did not keep <hi>it.</hi>  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 7:54
verses.text: And hearing these things, they were cut to their hearts. And they gnashed on him with <hi>their</hi> teeth.

verses.name: Acts 7:55
verses.text: But being full of <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit, looking up intently into Heaven, he saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

verses.name: Acts 7:56
verses.text: And <hi>he</hi> said, Behold, I see Heaven opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

verses.name: Acts 7:57
verses.text: And crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and ran on him with one accord.

verses.name: Acts 7:58
verses.text: And throwing <hi>him</hi> outside the city, they stoned <hi>him</hi>. And the witnesses laid their clothes down at the feet of a young man named Saul.

verses.name: Acts 7:59
verses.text: And they stoned Stephen, who was calling on <hi>God</hi> and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

verses.name: Acts 7:60
verses.text: And kneeling down, he cried with a loud voice, Lord, do not lay this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:1
verses.text: And Saul was consenting to his death. And in that day there was a great persecution on the church at Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 8:2
verses.text: And devout men buried Stephen and made a great mourning over him.

verses.name: Acts 8:3
verses.text: But Saul ravaged the church, entering into every house. And dragging men and women, he delivered <hi>them</hi> up to prison.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:4
verses.text: Then, indeed, the ones who had been scattered passed through, preaching the gospel, the Word.

verses.name: Acts 8:5
verses.text: And Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed Christ to them.

verses.name: Acts 8:6
verses.text: And the people with one accord gave heed to those things which Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the many miracles which he did.

verses.name: Acts 8:7
verses.text: For out of those having unclean spirits, many came out, crying with loud voice. And many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.

verses.name: Acts 8:8
verses.text: And there was great joy in that city.

verses.name: Acts 8:9
verses.text: But a certain man called Simon had long been conjuring in the city, and amazing the nation of Samaria, claiming himself to be some great one.

verses.name: Acts 8:10
verses.text: All gave heed to <hi>him</hi>, from the least to the greatest, saying, This one is the great power of God.

verses.name: Acts 8:11
verses.text: And they were paying attention to him, because for a long time he had amazed them <hi>with</hi> conjuring.

verses.name: Acts 8:12
verses.text: But when they believed Philip preaching the gospel, the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

verses.name: Acts 8:13
verses.text: Then Simon himself believed also, and being baptized, he continued with Philip. And seeing miracles and mighty works happening, he was amazed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:14
verses.text: And the apostles in Jerusalem hearing that Samaria had received the Word of God, they sent Peter and John to them;

verses.name: Acts 8:15
verses.text: who when they had come down, prayed for them that they might receive <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 8:16
verses.text: For as yet He had not fallen on any of them, they were baptized only in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 8:17
verses.text: Then they laid <hi>their</hi> hands on them, and they received <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 8:18
verses.text: And when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money,

verses.name: Acts 8:19
verses.text: saying, Give me this power also, that on whomever I lay hands, he may receive <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 8:20
verses.text: But Peter said to him, May your silver perish with you, because you have thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

verses.name: Acts 8:21
verses.text: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right in the sight of God.

verses.name: Acts 8:22
verses.text: Therefore repent of this wickedness of yours, and pray God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.

verses.name: Acts 8:23
verses.text: For I see that you are in <hi>the</hi> gall of bitterness and <hi>in</hi> the bond of iniquity.

verses.name: Acts 8:24
verses.text: And answering Simon said, You pray to the Lord for me that none of these things which you have spoken may come on me.

verses.name: Acts 8:25
verses.text: Then, indeed, having earnestly testified and having spoken the Word of the Lord also having preached the gospel <hi>to</hi> many villages of the Samaritans, they returned to Jerusalem.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 8:26
verses.text: And the angel of <hi>the</hi> Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Arise and go toward the south, on the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza, which is a deserted <hi>place</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 8:27
verses.text: And he arose and went. And behold, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship,

verses.name: Acts 8:28
verses.text: was returning. And sitting in his chariot he read Isaiah the prophet.

verses.name: Acts 8:29
verses.text: Then the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join yourself to this chariot.

verses.name: Acts 8:30
verses.text: And Philip ran there to <hi>him</hi> and heard him read the prophet Isaiah, and said, Do you indeed understand what you are reading?

verses.name: Acts 8:31
verses.text: And he said, How can I unless some man should guide me? And he asked Philip to come up and sit with him.

verses.name: Acts 8:32
verses.text: And the content of the Scripture which he read was this: "He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so He opened not His mouth.

verses.name: Acts 8:33
verses.text: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away, and who shall declare His generation? For His life is taken from the earth."

verses.name: Acts 8:34
verses.text: And the eunuch answered Philip and said, I beg you, of whom does the prophet speak this? Of himself or of some other man?

verses.name: Acts 8:35
verses.text: Then Philip opened his mouth and began at the same Scripture and preached the gospel of Jesus to him.

verses.name: Acts 8:36
verses.text: And as they passed along the way, they came on some water. And the eunuch said, See, here is water, what hinders me <hi>from</hi> being baptized?

verses.name: Acts 8:37
verses.text: Philip said, If you believe with all your heart, it is lawful. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

verses.name: Acts 8:38
verses.text: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch. And he baptized him.

verses.name: Acts 8:39
verses.text: And when they had come up out of the water, <hi>the</hi> Spirit of <hi>the</hi> Lord caught Philip away, so that the eunuch saw him no more. And he went on his way rejoicing.

verses.name: Acts 8:40
verses.text: But Philip was found at Azotus. And passing through, he preached the gospel in all the cities until he came to Caesarea.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:1
verses.text: And Saul, still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest

verses.name: Acts 9:2
verses.text: and asked letters from him to Damascus to the synagogues; so that if he found any of the Way, whether they were men or women, he might bring <hi>them</hi> bound to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 9:3
verses.text: But in going, it happened as he drew near to Damascus, even suddenly a light from the heaven shone around him.

verses.name: Acts 9:4
verses.text: And he fell to the earth and heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?

verses.name: Acts 9:5
verses.text: And he said, Who are you, lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom you persecute. <hi>It is</hi> hard for you to kick against the goads.

verses.name: Acts 9:6
verses.text: And trembling and astonished, he said, Lord, what will You have me to do? And the Lord <hi>said</hi> to him, Arise and go into the city, and you shall be told what you must do.

verses.name: Acts 9:7
verses.text: And the men who journeyed with him stood speechless, indeed hearing a voice but seeing no one.

verses.name: Acts 9:8
verses.text: And Saul was lifted up from the earth, his eyes were opened, but he saw no one. But they led him by the hand and brought <hi>him</hi> into Damascus.

verses.name: Acts 9:9
verses.text: And he was three days not seeing, and did not eat or drink.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:10
verses.text: And there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias! And he said, Behold me, Lord.

verses.name: Acts 9:11
verses.text: And the Lord <hi>said</hi> to him, Arise and go into the street which is called Straight and inquire in <hi>the</hi> house of Judas for <hi>one</hi> called Saul of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying,

verses.name: Acts 9:12
verses.text: and has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and putting <hi>his</hi> hand on him so that he might receive his sight.

verses.name: Acts 9:13
verses.text: And Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many of this man, how many evil things he has done to Your saints at Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 9:14
verses.text: And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on Your Name.

verses.name: Acts 9:15
verses.text: But the Lord said to him, Go! For this one is a chosen vessel to Me, to bear My name before nations and kings and the sons of Israel.

verses.name: Acts 9:16
verses.text: For I will show him what great things he must suffer for My name's sake.

verses.name: Acts 9:17
verses.text: And Ananias went and entered into the house. And putting his hands on him, <hi>he</hi> said, Brother Saul, the Lord, Jesus, who appeared to you in the way in which you came, has sent me to you that you might see and be filled with <hi> the</hi> Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 9:18
verses.text: And instantly scales as it were fell from his eyes, and he instantly saw again. And rising up, he was baptized.

verses.name: Acts 9:19
verses.text: And taking food, <hi>he</hi> was strengthened. And Saul was certain days with the disciples in Damascus.

verses.name: Acts 9:20
verses.text: And immediately he proclaimed Christ in the synagogues, that He is the Son of God.

verses.name: Acts 9:21
verses.text: But all who heard <hi>him</hi> were amazed and said, Is this not he who destroyed those who called on this name in Jerusalem and came here for that reason, that he might bring them bound to the chief priests?

verses.name: Acts 9:22
verses.text: But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this One is the Christ.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:23
verses.text: And after many days had been fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him.

verses.name: Acts 9:24
verses.text: But their plot was known to Saul. And they watched the gates day and night in order to kill him.

verses.name: Acts 9:25
verses.text: Then the disciples took <hi>him</hi> by night and let him down through the wall in a basket.

verses.name: Acts 9:26
verses.text: And arriving in Jerusalem, Saul attempted to join himself to the disciples. But they were all afraid of him, and did not believe that he was a disciple.

verses.name: Acts 9:27
verses.text: But Barnabas took him and brought <hi>him</hi> to the apostles and told them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that He had spoken to him, and how he had spoken boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 9:28
verses.text: And he was with them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 9:29
verses.text: And he spoke boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and argued with the Hellenists. But they seized him in order to kill him.

verses.name: Acts 9:30
verses.text: But knowing, the brothers brought him down to Caesarea and sent him forth to Tarsus.

verses.name: Acts 9:31
verses.text: Then, indeed, the churches had rest throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria, and having been built up. And having gone on in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, they <hi>were</hi> increased.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:32
verses.text: And it happened, passing through all, Peter also came down to the saints who lived at Lydda.

verses.name: Acts 9:33
verses.text: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had lain eight years on a mattress, paralyzed.

verses.name: Acts 9:34
verses.text: And Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you; rise up and spread for yourself! And he arose immediately.

verses.name: Acts 9:35
verses.text: And all who lived at Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 9:36
verses.text: And in Joppa was a certain disciple named Tabitha (which translated is called Dorcas). She was full of good works and kind deeds which she did.

verses.name: Acts 9:37
verses.text: And it happened in those days, becoming sick, she died. And washing her, they laid <hi>her</hi> in an upper room.

verses.name: Acts 9:38
verses.text: And, because Lydda was near Joppa, hearing that Peter is in it, the disciples sent two men to him, begging <hi>him</hi> not to delay to come to them.

verses.name: Acts 9:39
verses.text: And rising up, Peter went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. And all the widows stood beside him, weeping and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made <hi>while</hi> she was with them.

verses.name: Acts 9:40
verses.text: And putting them all out, Peter knelt down and prayed. And turning to the body he said, Tabitha, arise! And she opened her eyes. And when she saw Peter, she sat up.

verses.name: Acts 9:41
verses.text: And he gave her <hi>his</hi> hand and lifted her up. And when he had called the saints and widows, he presented her alive.

verses.name: Acts 9:42
verses.text: And it was known throughout all Joppa. And many believed in the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 9:43
verses.text: And it was many days that he remained in Joppa, with one Simon, a tanner.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:1
verses.text: And a certain man named Cornelius was in Caesarea, a centurion of the Italian cohort,

verses.name: Acts 10:2
verses.text: <hi> one</hi> devout and fearing God, with all his household, both doing many merciful deeds to the people, and praying continually to God.

verses.name: Acts 10:3
verses.text: About the ninth hour of the day he saw plainly in a vision an angel of God coming to him and saying to him, Cornelius!

verses.name: Acts 10:4
verses.text: And he was gazing at him, and becoming terrified, he said, What is it, lord? And he said to him, Your prayers and your merciful deeds have come up for a memorial before God.

verses.name: Acts 10:5
verses.text: And now send men to Joppa and call for Simon, whose last name is Peter.

verses.name: Acts 10:6
verses.text: He is staying with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by <hi>the</hi> seaside. He will tell you what you must do.

verses.name: Acts 10:7
verses.text: And when the angel who spoke to Cornelius departed, he called two of his servants and a devout soldier from those who waited on him continually.

verses.name: Acts 10:8
verses.text: And explaining all things to them, he sent them to Joppa.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:9
verses.text: On the next day, as these went on <hi>the</hi> road, and drawing near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about <hi>the</hi> sixth hour.

verses.name: Acts 10:10
verses.text: And he became very hungry and desired to eat. But while they made ready, an ecstasy fell on him.

verses.name: Acts 10:11
verses.text: And he saw the heaven opened and a certain vessel like a sheet coming down to him, being bound at the four corners and let down to the earth;

verses.name: Acts 10:12
verses.text: in which were all the four-footed animals of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the reptiles, and the birds of the heaven.

verses.name: Acts 10:13
verses.text: And a voice came to him, saying, Rise, Peter! Kill and eat!

verses.name: Acts 10:14
verses.text: But Peter said, Not so, Lord, for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.

verses.name: Acts 10:15
verses.text: And the voice <hi>spoke</hi> to him again the second <hi>time</hi>, What God has made clean, you do not call common.

verses.name: Acts 10:16
verses.text: This happened three <hi>times</hi>, and the vessel was received up again into the heaven.

verses.name: Acts 10:17
verses.text: And while Peter doubted within himself what the vision which he had seen might be, even behold, the men who were sent from Cornelius had asked for Simon's house and stood on the porch.

verses.name: Acts 10:18
verses.text: And they called and asked if Simon whose last name is Peter was staying there.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:19
verses.text: And <hi>while</hi> Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said to him, Behold, three men are looking for you.

verses.name: Acts 10:20
verses.text: Therefore arise and go down and go with them without doubting, for I have sent them.

verses.name: Acts 10:21
verses.text: And going down to the men, those sent to him from Cornelius, Peter said, Behold, I am <hi>the one</hi> you are seeking. For what reason have you come?

verses.name: Acts 10:22
verses.text: And they said, Cornelius the centurion, a just man and <hi>one</hi> who fears God, and one of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by a holy angel to send for you to come to his house and to hear words from you.

verses.name: Acts 10:23
verses.text: Then he called them in and lodged <hi>them</hi>. And on the next day Peter went away with them, and certain brothers from Joppa went with him.

verses.name: Acts 10:24
verses.text: And the next day they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.

verses.name: Acts 10:25
verses.text: And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him and fell down at <hi>his</hi> feet <hi>and</hi> worshiped.

verses.name: Acts 10:26
verses.text: But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up! I also am a man myself.

verses.name: Acts 10:27
verses.text: And as he talked with him, he went in and found many who had come together.

verses.name: Acts 10:28
verses.text: And he said to them, You know that it is an unlawful thing for a man, a Jew to keep company with or to come near to one of another nation. But God has shown me not to call any man common or unclean.

verses.name: Acts 10:29
verses.text: Therefore I came without complaint, being sent for. I ask, then, for what reason have you sent for me.

verses.name: Acts 10:30
verses.text: And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour. And at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing.

verses.name: Acts 10:31
verses.text: And he said, Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your merciful deeds have been remembered before God.

verses.name: Acts 10:32
verses.text: Therefore send to Joppa and call here Simon whose last name is Peter, he is staying in <hi>the</hi> house of Simon, a tanner by the seaside; who, when he comes, shall speak to you.

verses.name: Acts 10:33
verses.text: Therefore I immediately sent to you, and you have done well <hi>to</hi> come. Now therefore we are all here present before God to hear all things that are commanded you by God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:34
verses.text: Then Peter opened <hi>his</hi> mouth and said, Truly I see that God is no respecter of persons;

verses.name: Acts 10:35
verses.text: but in every nation he who fears Him and works righteousness is accepted with Him.

verses.name: Acts 10:36
verses.text: You know the word which <hi>God</hi> sent to the sons of Israel, preaching the gospel of peace by Jesus Christ (He is Lord of all!);

verses.name: Acts 10:37
verses.text: that word which was published throughout all Judea, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John proclaimed;

verses.name: Acts 10:38
verses.text: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit and with power, and He went about doing good, and healing all those who were oppressed by the Devil, for God was with Him.

verses.name: Acts 10:39
verses.text: And we are witnesses of all things which He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed <hi>Him</hi> and hanged <hi>Him</hi> on a tree;

verses.name: Acts 10:40
verses.text: but God raised Him up the third day and showed Him openly,

verses.name: Acts 10:41
verses.text: not to all the people, but to witnesses hand-picked before by God, <hi>even</hi> to us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from <hi>the</hi> dead.

verses.name: Acts 10:42
verses.text: And He commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify that it is He who was ordained of God <hi>to be</hi> the Judge of <hi>the</hi> living and <hi>the</hi> dead.

verses.name: Acts 10:43
verses.text: All the prophets give witness to Him, <hi>that</hi> through His name whoever believes in Him <hi>shall</hi> receive remission of sins.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 10:44
verses.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those hearing the Word.

verses.name: Acts 10:45
verses.text: And those of the circumcision, who believed (as many as came with Peter), were astonished because the gift of the Holy Spirit was poured out on the nations also.

verses.name: Acts 10:46
verses.text: For they heard them speak with tongues and magnify God. Then Peter answered,

verses.name: Acts 10:47
verses.text: Can anyone forbid water that these, who have received the Holy Ghost as well as we, should not be baptized?

verses.name: Acts 10:48
verses.text: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they begged him to stay certain days.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:1
verses.text: And the apostles and brothers who were in Judea heard that the nations had also received the Word of God.

verses.name: Acts 11:2
verses.text: And when Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision contended with him,

verses.name: Acts 11:3
verses.text: saying, You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them.

verses.name: Acts 11:4
verses.text: But Peter related <hi>the matter</hi> from the beginning and explained <hi>it</hi> by order to them, saying,

verses.name: Acts 11:5
verses.text: I was in <hi>the</hi> city of Joppa praying. And in an ecstasy I saw a vision, a certain vessel like a sheet coming down, let down from the sky by four corners. And it came even to me.

verses.name: Acts 11:6
verses.text: When I had fastened my eyes on <hi>it</hi>, I looked and saw four-footed animals of the earth, and wild beasts, and reptiles, and birds of the heaven.

verses.name: Acts 11:7
verses.text: And I heard a voice saying to me, Arise, Peter! Kill and eat!

verses.name: Acts 11:8
verses.text: But I said, Not so, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has at any time entered into my mouth.

verses.name: Acts 11:9
verses.text: But the voice answered me again from the heaven, What God has made clean, you do not call common.

verses.name: Acts 11:10
verses.text: And this was done three <hi>times</hi>, and all were drawn up again into the heaven.

verses.name: Acts 11:11
verses.text: And behold, immediately three men stood at house in which I was, sent from Caesarea to me.

verses.name: Acts 11:12
verses.text: And the Spirit told me to go with them, not discriminating. And these six brothers <hi>went</hi> with me, and we entered the man's house.

verses.name: Acts 11:13
verses.text: And he declared to us how he had seen an angel in his house, who stood and said to him, Send men to Joppa and call for Simon whose last name is Peter,

verses.name: Acts 11:14
verses.text: who will tell you words by which you and all your house shall be saved.

verses.name: Acts 11:15
verses.text: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, as on us at <hi>the</hi> beginning.

verses.name: Acts 11:16
verses.text: And I remembered the Word of the Lord, how He said, John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Acts 11:17
verses.text: Therefore because God gave them the same gift to us who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to prevent God?

verses.name: Acts 11:18
verses.text: When they heard these things, they were silent and glorified God, saying, Then God has also granted repentance to life to the nations.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:19
verses.text: Then, indeed, they who were scattered abroad by the persecution that rose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, preaching the Word to no one except the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 11:20
verses.text: And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene; who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the gospel of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 11:21
verses.text: And <hi>the</hi> hand of <hi>the</hi> Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 11:22
verses.text: And the Word was heard in the ears of the church in Jerusalem. And they sent out Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch;

verses.name: Acts 11:23
verses.text: who was glad when he had come and had seen the grace of God. And he exhorted all with purpose of heart to remain near to the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 11:24
verses.text: For he was a good man and full of <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit and faith. And many people were added to the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 11:25
verses.text: And Barnabas went out to Tarsus to seek Saul.

verses.name: Acts 11:26
verses.text: And finding him, it was a whole year <hi>they</hi> were gathered to them in the church and taught a considerable crowd. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 11:27
verses.text: And in these days prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch.

verses.name: Acts 11:28
verses.text: And one of them named Agabus stood up and signified by the Spirit that there should be great famine over the world (which also happened in the <hi>days</hi> of Claudius Caesar).

verses.name: Acts 11:29
verses.text: And the disciples, as any were prospered, determined each of them to send for ministry to those brothers who lived in Judea,

verses.name: Acts 11:30
verses.text: which they also did, sending to the elders by <hi>the</hi> hand of Barnabas and Saul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:1
verses.text: And at that time Herod the king threw on <hi>his</hi> hands to oppress some of those of the church.

verses.name: Acts 12:2
verses.text: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.

verses.name: Acts 12:3
verses.text: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he went further to seize Peter also. (And they were days of Unleavened <hi>Bread</hi>.)

verses.name: Acts 12:4
verses.text: And capturing <hi>him</hi>, he put <hi>him</hi> in prison, and delivered <hi>him</hi> to four sets of four soldiers to keep him; intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:5
verses.text: Then, indeed, Peter was kept in prison. But earnest prayer was made to God for him by the church.

verses.name: Acts 12:6
verses.text: And when Herod was about to bring him out, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Also guards were keeping the prison before the door.

verses.name: Acts 12:7
verses.text: And behold! An angel of <hi>the</hi> Lord stood by, and a light shone in the building. And striking Peter's side, he raised him up, saying, Rise up quickly! And his chains fell off his hands.

verses.name: Acts 12:8
verses.text: And the angel said to him, Gird yourself and put on your sandals. And he did so. And he says to him, Throw your robe around you and follow me.

verses.name: Acts 12:9
verses.text: And he went out and followed him. And he did not know that this happening through the angel was true, but thought he saw a vision.

verses.name: Acts 12:10
verses.text: When they were past the first and second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city, which opened to them of its own accord. And they went out and passed on through one street. And immediately the angel departed from him.

verses.name: Acts 12:11
verses.text: And having come to himself, Peter said, Now I know surely that <hi>the</hi> Lord has sent His angel and has delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and <hi>from</hi> all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 12:12
verses.text: And thinking <hi>about it</hi>, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose last name was Mark; where many had gathered together to pray.

verses.name: Acts 12:13
verses.text: And as Peter knocked <hi>at</hi> the door of the porch, a girl named Rhoda came to listen.

verses.name: Acts 12:14
verses.text: And when she knew Peter's voice, she did not open the porch because of gladness, but running in she reported Peter <hi>was</hi> standing before the porch.

verses.name: Acts 12:15
verses.text: And they said to her, You are mad. But she kept on saying that it was so. And they said, It is his angel.

verses.name: Acts 12:16
verses.text: But Peter continued knocking, and when they had opened and saw him, they were amazed.

verses.name: Acts 12:17
verses.text: But, waving to them with his hand to be quiet, he declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go tell these things to James and to the brothers. And he departed and went into another place.

verses.name: Acts 12:18
verses.text: And day coming, there was not a little stir among the soldiers, saying, What, then, became of Peter.

verses.name: Acts 12:19
verses.text: And searching for him, and not finding <hi>him</hi>, examining the guards, Herod commanded them to be led away to death. And he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 12:20
verses.text: And Herod was in bitter hostility with the men of Tyre and Sidon. But they came to him with one accord and, having made Blastus (who had charge of the king's bedroom) their friend, desired peace, because their country was fed by the king's <hi>country</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 12:21
verses.text: And on a certain day, Herod sat on his throne, dressed in royal clothing, and made a speech to them.

verses.name: Acts 12:22
verses.text: And the people gave a shout, <hi>saying, It is</hi> the voice of a god and not of a man!

verses.name: Acts 12:23
verses.text: And immediately the angel of <hi>the</hi> Lord struck him, because he did not give God the glory. And he was eaten by worms and gave up the spirit.

verses.name: Acts 12:24
verses.text: But the Word of God grew and increased.

verses.name: Acts 12:25
verses.text: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem when they had fulfilled the ministry, having taken with <hi>them</hi> John, whose last name was Mark.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:1
verses.text: And in Antioch some among the existing church were prophets and teachers. (such as Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch) and Saul.

verses.name: Acts 13:2
verses.text: <hi> As</hi> they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, So, then, separate Barnabas and Saul to Me for the work to which I have called them.

verses.name: Acts 13:3
verses.text: Then having fasted and prayed and laid hands on them, they let <hi>them</hi> go.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:4
verses.text: Then these indeed sent out by the Holy Spirit went down to Seleucia. And from there they sailed to Cyprus.

verses.name: Acts 13:5
verses.text: And when they were at Salamis, they announced the Word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they also had John as an assistant.

verses.name: Acts 13:6
verses.text: And when they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain conjurer, a false prophet, a Jew whose name <hi>was</hi> Bar-jesus;

verses.name: Acts 13:7
verses.text: who was with the proconsul of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man. He called for Barnabas and Saul and asked to hear the Word of God.

verses.name: Acts 13:8
verses.text: But Elymas the conjurer (for so his name is, if translated) withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

verses.name: Acts 13:9
verses.text: Then Saul (who <hi>is</hi> also Paul), filled with <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit, set his eyes on him

verses.name: Acts 13:10
verses.text: and said, O son of the Devil, full of all deceit and all craftiness, enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop perverting the right ways of <hi>the</hi> Lord?

verses.name: Acts 13:11
verses.text: And now, behold, <hi>the</hi> hand of the Lord <hi>is</hi> on you. And you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a while. And immediately a mist and a darkness fell on him, and he went about seeking <hi>some to</hi> lead him by the hand.

verses.name: Acts 13:12
verses.text: Then, seeing the thing happening, the proconsul believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 13:13
verses.text: And Paul and those around <hi>him</hi> sailed from Paphos and came to Perga of Pamphylia. And John left them and returned to Jerusalem.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:14
verses.text: But going through from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia and went into the synagogue on the sabbath day and sat down.

verses.name: Acts 13:15
verses.text: And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Men, brothers, if you have any word of comfort for the people, speak.

verses.name: Acts 13:16
verses.text: And rising up and signaling with his hand, Paul said, Men, Israelites, and those fearing God, listen.

verses.name: Acts 13:17
verses.text: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people in their residency in <hi>the</hi> land <hi>of</hi> Egypt, and He brought them out of it with a high arm.

verses.name: Acts 13:18
verses.text: And about the time of forty years He tenderly bore them in the wilderness.

verses.name: Acts 13:19
verses.text: And when He had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave their land to them as an inheritance.

verses.name: Acts 13:20
verses.text: And after that He gave <hi>them</hi> judges for about four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet.

verses.name: Acts 13:21
verses.text: And afterward they asked <hi>for</hi> a king. And God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man of <hi>the</hi> tribe of Benjamin, <hi>for</hi> forty years.

verses.name: Acts 13:22
verses.text: And when He had removed him, He raised up David to them to be their king; to whom He also witnessed and said, I have found David the <hi>son</hi> of Jesse <hi>to be</hi> a man after My own heart, who shall fulfill all My will.

verses.name: Acts 13:23
verses.text: Of this <hi>man's</hi> seed God has raised to Israel, according to <hi>His</hi> promise, a Savior, Jesus;

verses.name: Acts 13:24
verses.text: John having before proclaimed the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel, before His coming.

verses.name: Acts 13:25
verses.text: And as John fulfilled his course, he said, Who do you think that I am? I am not <hi>He</hi>. But behold, One comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to loose.

verses.name: Acts 13:26
verses.text: Men, brothers, sons of <hi>the</hi> race of Abraham, and whoever among you fears God, the word of this salvation is sent to you.

verses.name: Acts 13:27
verses.text: For those living in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not having known this One, and the voices of the prophets being read throughout every sabbath, condemning <hi>Him</hi>, they fulfilled <hi>the Scriptures</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 13:28
verses.text: And finding not one cause of death <hi>in Him</hi>, they begged Pilate to do away with Him.

verses.name: Acts 13:29
verses.text: And when they had fulfilled all that was written concerning Him, taking <hi>Him</hi> down from the tree, they laid <hi>Him</hi> in a tomb.

verses.name: Acts 13:30
verses.text: But God raised Him from <hi>the</hi> dead,

verses.name: Acts 13:31
verses.text: who appeared for many days by those who came up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are His witnesses to the people.

verses.name: Acts 13:32
verses.text: And we preach the gospel to you, the promise made to the fathers,

verses.name: Acts 13:33
verses.text: this God has fulfilled to us their children, raising up Jesus, as also it is written in the second Psalm, "You are My Son, this day I have begotten You."

verses.name: Acts 13:34
verses.text: And that He raised Him up from <hi>the</hi> dead, no more to return to corruption, He spoke in this way: "I will give you the holy promises of David."

verses.name: Acts 13:35
verses.text: Therefore he also says in another <hi>psalm</hi>, "You shall not allow Your Holy One to see corruption."

verses.name: Acts 13:36
verses.text: For after he had served <hi>his</hi> own generation by the will of God, David fell asleep and was added to his fathers and saw corruption.

verses.name: Acts 13:37
verses.text: But <hi>He</hi> whom God raised again saw no corruption.

verses.name: Acts 13:38
verses.text: Therefore be it known to you, men, brothers, that through this One the forgiveness of sins is announced to you.

verses.name: Acts 13:39
verses.text: And by Him all who believe are justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

verses.name: Acts 13:40
verses.text: Therefore beware lest that come on you which is spoken of in the prophets:

verses.name: Acts 13:41
verses.text: "Behold, you despisers, and marvel, and perish; for I work a work in your days, a work which you shall in no way believe, though a man declare <hi>it</hi> to you."  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 13:42
verses.text: And the Jews having gone out of the synagogue, the nations begged that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath.

verses.name: Acts 13:43
verses.text: And the synagogue being broken up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.

verses.name: Acts 13:44
verses.text: And on the coming sabbath day almost all the city came together to hear the Word of God.

verses.name: Acts 13:45
verses.text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy and contradicted those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.

verses.name: Acts 13:46
verses.text: But speaking boldly, Paul and Barnabas said, It was necessary <hi>for</hi> the word of God to be spoken to you first. But since indeed you put it far from you and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the nations.

verses.name: Acts 13:47
verses.text: For so the Lord has commanded us, <hi>saying</hi>, "I have set You to be a light of the nations, for salvation to the end of the earth."

verses.name: Acts 13:48
verses.text: And hearing, the nations rejoiced and glorified the Word of the Lord. And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

verses.name: Acts 13:49
verses.text: And the Word of the Lord was carried throughout all the country.

verses.name: Acts 13:50
verses.text: But the Jews stirred up the devout and honorable women, and the chief ones of the city, and raised a persecution against Paul and Barnabas. And they threw them out of their borders.

verses.name: Acts 13:51
verses.text: But shaking the dust of their feet off on them, they came into Iconium.

verses.name: Acts 13:52
verses.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:1
verses.text: And it happened in Iconium, they both went together into the synagogue of the Jews, and spoke so as a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.

verses.name: Acts 14:2
verses.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the nations and made them evil-hearted against the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 14:3
verses.text: Therefore they stayed a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who bore witness to the word of His grace, giving miracles and wonders to be done by their hands.

verses.name: Acts 14:4
verses.text: But the multitude of the city was divided. And part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 14:5
verses.text: And when there was an assault made by both the nations and the Jews, with their rulers, in order to insult and to stone them,

verses.name: Acts 14:6
verses.text: they were aware of <hi>it</hi> and fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and to the country around them.

verses.name: Acts 14:7
verses.text: And there they were preaching the gospel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:8
verses.text: And a certain man was sitting in Lystra, without strength in the feet, being lame from his mother's womb, who never had walked.

verses.name: Acts 14:9
verses.text: This one heard Paul speaking; <hi>and Paul</hi>, looking intently at him, and seeing that he had faith to be healed,

verses.name: Acts 14:10
verses.text: said with a loud voice, Stand up on your feet! And he leaped and walked.

verses.name: Acts 14:11
verses.text: And seeing what Paul did, the crowd lifted up their voice, saying in Lycaonian, The gods have come down to us, becoming like men.

verses.name: Acts 14:12
verses.text: And they called Barnabas Jupiter, and Paul Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.

verses.name: Acts 14:13
verses.text: And the priest of Jupiter, being before their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, wishing to sacrifice with the crowds.

verses.name: Acts 14:14
verses.text: But hearing <hi>this</hi>, the apostles Barnabas and Paul tore their clothes and ran in among the people, crying out

verses.name: Acts 14:15
verses.text: and saying, Men, why do you do these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preaching the gospel to you to turn <hi>you</hi> from these vanities to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all things in them;

verses.name: Acts 14:16
verses.text: who in past generations allowed all nations to walk in their <hi>own</hi> ways.

verses.name: Acts 14:17
verses.text: And yet He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good, giving rain and fruitful season to us from heaven, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

verses.name: Acts 14:18
verses.text: And saying these things, they scarcely stopped the people from sacrificing to them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 14:19
verses.text: And Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, who, having persuaded the people, and having stoned Paul, they drew <hi>him</hi> out of the city, supposing him to have died.

verses.name: Acts 14:20
verses.text: But the disciples surrounding him, he rose up and came into the city. And the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.

verses.name: Acts 14:21
verses.text: And preaching the gospel to that city, and having made many disciples, they returned to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch,

verses.name: Acts 14:22
verses.text: confirming the souls of the disciples, calling on them to continue in the faith and that through much tribulation we must enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 14:23
verses.text: And having hand-picked elders for them in every church, and had prayed with fastings, they commended them to the Lord into whom they believed.

verses.name: Acts 14:24
verses.text: And passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

verses.name: Acts 14:25
verses.text: And speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

verses.name: Acts 14:26
verses.text: And from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.

verses.name: Acts 14:27
verses.text: And having arrived, and gathering the church they related all that God had done with them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the nations.

verses.name: Acts 14:28
verses.text: And they stayed there not a little time with the disciples.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:1
verses.text: And certain ones who came down from Judea taught the brothers, <hi>saying</hi>, Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.

verses.name: Acts 15:2
verses.text: Therefore dissension and not a little disputation occurring by Paul and Barnabas, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and certain others of them to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.

verses.name: Acts 15:3
verses.text: And indeed being set forward by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the nations. And they caused great joy to all the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 15:4
verses.text: And arriving in Jerusalem, they were received by the church, and <hi>by</hi> the apostles and elders. And <hi>they</hi> declared all things that God had done with them.

verses.name: Acts 15:5
verses.text: But some of those from the sect of the Pharisees, having believed, rose up, saying, It was necessary to circumcise them and to command <hi>them</hi> to keep the law of Moses.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:6
verses.text: And the apostles and elders were assembled to see about this matter.

verses.name: Acts 15:7
verses.text: And after much disputing, Peter rose up and said to them, Men, brothers, you recognize that from ancient days God chose among us <hi>that</hi> through my mouth the nations <hi>should</hi> hear the word of the gospel, and believe.

verses.name: Acts 15:8
verses.text: And God, who knows the hearts, bore them witness, giving them the Holy Spirit even as to us.

verses.name: Acts 15:9
verses.text: And He put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

verses.name: Acts 15:10
verses.text: Now therefore why do you tempt God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples, a yoke which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

verses.name: Acts 15:11
verses.text: But we believe that through the grace of <hi>the</hi> Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, according to which manner they also believed.

verses.name: Acts 15:12
verses.text: And all the multitude kept silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul declaring what miracles and wonders God had worked among the nations through them.

verses.name: Acts 15:13
verses.text: And after they were silent, James answered, saying, Men, brothers, listen to me.

verses.name: Acts 15:14
verses.text: Even as Simon has declared <hi>how</hi> God <hi>at</hi> the first visited the nations to take out of them a people for His name.

verses.name: Acts 15:15
verses.text: And the words of the prophets agree to this; as it is written,

verses.name: Acts 15:16
verses.text: "After this I will return and will build again the tabernacle of David <hi>which</hi> has fallen down; and I will build again its ruins, and I will set it up,

verses.name: Acts 15:17
verses.text: so those men who are left might seek after the Lord, and all the nations on whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who does all these things."

verses.name: Acts 15:18
verses.text: All His works are known to God from eternity.

verses.name: Acts 15:19
verses.text: Therefore my judgment is that we do not trouble those who have turned to God from among the nations,

verses.name: Acts 15:20
verses.text: but that we write to them that they should abstain from pollutions of idols, and <hi>from</hi> fornication, and <hi>from</hi> things strangled, and from blood.

verses.name: Acts 15:21
verses.text: For Moses from ages past has those in every city proclaiming him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:22
verses.text: Then it pleased the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men from them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; Judas, whose last name was Barsabas; and Silas, chief men among the brothers.

verses.name: Acts 15:23
verses.text: And they wrote these things by their hand: The apostles and elders and brothers <hi>send</hi> greeting to the brothers, from <hi>the</hi> nations in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.

verses.name: Acts 15:24
verses.text: Because we have heard that certain ones who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying, Be circumcised and keep the law! (to whom we gave no such command);

verses.name: Acts 15:25
verses.text: it seemed <hi>good</hi> to us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

verses.name: Acts 15:26
verses.text: men who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Acts 15:27
verses.text: Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, who will also announce <hi>to you</hi> the same things by word.

verses.name: Acts 15:28
verses.text: For it seemed <hi>good</hi> to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay on you no greater burden than these necessary things:

verses.name: Acts 15:29
verses.text: that you abstain from meats offered to idols, and <hi>from</hi> blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication; from which, if you keep yourselves, you shall do well. Be prospered.

verses.name: Acts 15:30
verses.text: Then indeed they being let go, they came to Antioch. And gathering the multitude, <hi>they</hi> delivered the letter.

verses.name: Acts 15:31
verses.text: And when they had read <hi>it</hi>, they rejoiced at the comfort.

verses.name: Acts 15:32
verses.text: And Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, exhorted the brothers with many words and confirmed <hi>them</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 15:33
verses.text: And remaining for a time, they were let go in peace from the brothers to the apostles.

verses.name: Acts 15:34
verses.text: But it pleased Silas to remain there.

verses.name: Acts 15:35
verses.text: Also Paul and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the gospel, the Word of the Lord, with many others also.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 15:36
verses.text: And some days afterward, Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brothers in every city where we have announced the Word of the Lord, how they are doing.

verses.name: Acts 15:37
verses.text: And Barnabas determined to take with <hi>them</hi> John, he being called Mark.

verses.name: Acts 15:38
verses.text: But Paul thought it well not to take that one with <hi>them</hi>, he having withdrawn form them from Pamphylia, and did not go with them to the work.

verses.name: Acts 15:39
verses.text: Then there was sharp feeling, as to separate them from each other. And taking Mark, Barnabas sailed to Cyprus.

verses.name: Acts 15:40
verses.text: But choosing Silas, Paul went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God,

verses.name: Acts 15:41
verses.text: passing through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches strong.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:1
verses.text: And he came to Derbe and Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple named Timothy was there, <hi>the</hi> son of a woman who was a Jewess and who believed. But <hi>his</hi> father <hi>was</hi> a Greek.

verses.name: Acts 16:2
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> was well reported of by the brothers at Lystra and Iconium.

verses.name: Acts 16:3
verses.text: Paul wanted him to go with him, and taking <hi>him he</hi> circumcised him, because of the Jews who were in those places; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

verses.name: Acts 16:4
verses.text: And as they passed through the cities, they delivered to them the commandments to keep, the ones that were ordained by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 16:5
verses.text: Then indeed the churches were established in the faith and increased in number daily.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:6
verses.text: And coming through the Phrygian and the Galatian region; and by the Holy Spirit being forbidden to speak the Word in Asia;

verses.name: Acts 16:7
verses.text: having come to Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia. But the Spirit did not allow them.

verses.name: Acts 16:8
verses.text: Then passing by Mysia, they came down into Troas.

verses.name: Acts 16:9
verses.text: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night. A certain man of Macedonia stood, begging him, saying, Come over into Macedonia and help us!

verses.name: Acts 16:10
verses.text: And after he saw the vision, we immediately tried to go into Macedonia, gathering that the Lord had called us in order to preach the gospel <hi>to</hi> them.

verses.name: Acts 16:11
verses.text: Then having set sail from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next <hi>day</hi> to Neapolis;

verses.name: Acts 16:12
verses.text: and from there to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, a colony. And we continued spending time in that city some days.

verses.name: Acts 16:13
verses.text: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was usually made. And we sat down and spoke to the women who came together <hi>there</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 16:14
verses.text: And a certain woman named Lydia heard us, a seller of purple of the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God; whose heart the Lord opened, so that she attended to the things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.name: Acts 16:15
verses.text: And when she was baptized, she and her household, she begged us, saying, If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay. And she constrained us.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:16
verses.text: And as we went to prayer, it happened that a certain girl possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by divining.

verses.name: Acts 16:17
verses.text: The same followed Paul and us and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the Most High God, who are announcing to us the way of salvation.

verses.name: Acts 16:18
verses.text: And she did this many days. But being distressed, and turning to the <hi>demonic</hi> spirit, Paul said, I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her! And it came out in that hour.

verses.name: Acts 16:19
verses.text: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gain went out, having seized Paul and Silas, they dragged <hi>them</hi> to the market before the rulers.

verses.name: Acts 16:20
verses.text: And bringing them near to the judges, they said, These men, being Jews, are exceedingly troubling our city.

verses.name: Acts 16:21
verses.text: And they teach customs which are not lawful for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.

verses.name: Acts 16:22
verses.text: And the crowd rose up against them. And tearing off their clothes, the judges ordered <hi>them</hi> to be flogged.

verses.name: Acts 16:23
verses.text: And after laying on them many stripes, they threw <hi>them</hi> into prison, commanding the jailor to keep them safely;

verses.name: Acts 16:24
verses.text: who, having received such a command, thrust them into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:25
verses.text: And toward midnight Paul and Silas prayed and praised to God in a hymn. And the prisoners listened to them.

verses.name: Acts 16:26
verses.text: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. And immediately all the doors were opened and all the bonds were loosened.

verses.name: Acts 16:27
verses.text: And being awakened, and seeing the doors of the prison being open, drawing a sword, the jailer was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.

verses.name: Acts 16:28
verses.text: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, Do yourself no harm, for we are all here.

verses.name: Acts 16:29
verses.text: Then asking for a light he rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

verses.name: Acts 16:30
verses.text: And leading them outside, he said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

verses.name: Acts 16:31
verses.text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and you shall be saved, and your household.

verses.name: Acts 16:32
verses.text: And they spoke the Word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his household.

verses.name: Acts 16:33
verses.text: And taking them in that hour of the night, he washed from <hi>their</hi> stripes. And he was baptized, he and all his, immediately.

verses.name: Acts 16:34
verses.text: And bringing them up to the house, he set a table before <hi>them</hi> and rejoiced, believing in God with all his household.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 16:35
verses.text: And day coming, the judges sent the floggers, saying, Let those men go.

verses.name: Acts 16:36
verses.text: And the jailer spoke these words to Paul: The judges have sent to let you go. Now therefore depart, and go in peace.

verses.name: Acts 16:37
verses.text: But Paul said to them, Having beaten us publicly, men who are Romans and uncondemned, they threw <hi>us</hi> into prison. And now do they put us out secretly? No indeed! But coming themselves, let them bring us out.

verses.name: Acts 16:38
verses.text: And the floggers reported these words to the judges. And hearing that they were Romans, they were afraid.

verses.name: Acts 16:39
verses.text: And coming they begged <hi>them</hi>. And bringing <hi>them</hi> out, <hi>they</hi> asked <hi>them</hi> to depart out of the city.

verses.name: Acts 16:40
verses.text: And going out from the prison, <hi>they</hi> entered into <hi>the house of</hi> Lydia. And seeing the brothers, they comforted them and departed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:1
verses.text: And traveling through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 17:2
verses.text: And according to Paul's custom, he went in to them and reasoned with them out of the Scriptures on three sabbaths,

verses.name: Acts 17:3
verses.text: opening and setting forth that Christ must have suffered, and to have risen again from <hi>the</hi> dead; and that this Jesus whom I preach to you is Christ.

verses.name: Acts 17:4
verses.text: And some of them believed and joined themselves to Paul and Silas, both a great multitude of the worshiping Greeks, and not a few of the chief women.

verses.name: Acts 17:5
verses.text: But the disobeying Jews becoming jealous, and having taken aside some wicked men of the market-loafers, and gathering a crowd, they set all the city in an uproar. And coming on the house of Jason, <hi>they</hi> sought to bring them out to the mob.

verses.name: Acts 17:6
verses.text: And not finding them, they drew Jason and certain brothers before the city judges, crying, These who have turned the world upside down have come here too,

verses.name: Acts 17:7
verses.text: whom Jason has received. And these all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 17:8
verses.text: And hearing these things, they troubled the crowd and the city judge.

verses.name: Acts 17:9
verses.text: And taking security from Jason and from the rest, they let them go.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:10
verses.text: And the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea. They, when they arrived, went into the synagogue of the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 17:11
verses.text: And these were more noble than those of Thessalonica, in that <hi>they received</hi> the Word with all readiness of mind and searched the Scriptures daily <hi>to see</hi> if those things <hi>were so</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 17:12
verses.text: Therefore many of them believed, and quite a few of honorable Greek women and men.

verses.name: Acts 17:13
verses.text: But when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that the Word of God was preached by Paul at Berea, they came there also and stirred up the people.

verses.name: Acts 17:14
verses.text: And then immediately the brothers sent Paul away to go towards the sea, but both Silas and Timothy stayed there.

verses.name: Acts 17:15
verses.text: And those conducting Paul brought him to Athens. And receiving a command to Silas and Timothy to come to him with all speed, they departed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:16
verses.text: But awaiting them in Athens, Paul's spirit was pained within him, seeing city full of idols.

verses.name: Acts 17:17
verses.text: Then indeed he addressed the Jews in the synagogue, and those worshiping, and daily in the market, to those happening to be <hi>there</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 17:18
verses.text: And certain philosophers from the Epicureans and from the Stoics met him. And some said, What will this babbler say? And others said, He seems to be an announcer of foreign demons (because he preached Jesus and the resurrection to them).

verses.name: Acts 17:19
verses.text: And taking hold of him, they led <hi>him</hi> to the Areopagus, saying, Are we able to know what <hi>is</hi> this new doctrine of which you speak?

verses.name: Acts 17:20
verses.text: For you bring certain strange things to our ears, therefore we are minded to know what these things mean.

verses.name: Acts 17:21
verses.text: (For all the Athenians and strangers who were <hi>there</hi> spent their time in nothing else except to tell or to hear something newer.)  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:22
verses.text: And standing in <hi>the</hi> middle of the Areopagus, Paul said, Men, Athenians, I see that you <hi>are</hi> fearful of gods in everything.

verses.name: Acts 17:23
verses.text: For <hi>as I</hi> passed by and saw the things you worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Not knowing then whom you worship, I make Him known to you.

verses.name: Acts 17:24
verses.text: The God who made the world and all things in it, since He is Lord of Heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands.

verses.name: Acts 17:25
verses.text: Nor is served with men's hands, <hi>as though</hi> He needed anything, <hi>since</hi> He gives life and breath and all things to all.

verses.name: Acts 17:26
verses.text: And He has made all nations of men of one blood to dwell on all the face of the earth, ordaining fore-appointed seasons and boundaries of their dwelling,

verses.name: Acts 17:27
verses.text: to seek the Lord, if perhaps they might feel after Him and find Him, though indeed <hi>He</hi> is not far from each one of us.

verses.name: Acts 17:28
verses.text: For in Him we live and move and have our being, as also certain of your own poets have said, For we are also His offspring.

verses.name: Acts 17:29
verses.text: Then being offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like gold or silver or stone, engraved by art and man's imagination.

verses.name: Acts 17:30
verses.text: Truly, then, God overlooking the times of ignorance, now He strictly commands all men everywhere to repent,

verses.name: Acts 17:31
verses.text: because He has appointed a day in which He is going to judge the world in righteousness by a Man whom He appointed, having given proof to all <hi>by</hi> raising Him from <hi>the</hi> dead.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 17:32
verses.text: And hearing <hi>of</hi> a resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead, some indeed mocked; and others said, We will hear you again concerning this.

verses.name: Acts 17:33
verses.text: And so Paul departed from among them.

verses.name: Acts 17:34
verses.text: But certain men joined themselves to him and believed; among whom <hi>were</hi> Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:1
verses.text: And after these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

verses.name: Acts 18:2
verses.text: And finding a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy <hi>with</hi> his wife Priscilla (because Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome) Paul came to them.

verses.name: Acts 18:3
verses.text: And because <hi>he</hi> was of the same trade, he stayed and worked with them; for they were tentmakers by occupation.

verses.name: Acts 18:4
verses.text: And he reasoned in the synagogue on every sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.

verses.name: Acts 18:5
verses.text: And when Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit and testified to the Jews <hi>that</hi> Jesus <hi>is</hi> the Christ.

verses.name: Acts 18:6
verses.text: And they resisting and blaspheming, shaking <hi>his</hi> garment, he said to them, Your blood <hi>is</hi> on your own heads. I <hi>am</hi> pure from <hi>it</hi>. From now on I will go to the nations.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:7
verses.text: And he departed from there and entered into <hi>the</hi> house of one named Justus, <hi>one</hi> worshiping God, whose house was next to the synagogue.

verses.name: Acts 18:8
verses.text: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house. And hearing this, many of the Corinthians believed and were baptized.

verses.name: Acts 18:9
verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Paul in <hi>the</hi> night by a vision, Do not be afraid, but speak, and be not silent.

verses.name: Acts 18:10
verses.text: For I am with you, and no one shall set on you to hurt you, for I have many people in this city.

verses.name: Acts 18:11
verses.text: And he continued <hi>there</hi> a year and six months, teaching the Word of God among them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:12
verses.text: But Gallio <hi>being</hi> pro-consul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rushed against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat,

verses.name: Acts 18:13
verses.text: saying, This one persuades men to worship God contrary to the Law.

verses.name: Acts 18:14
verses.text: And Paul being about to open <hi>his</hi> mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If indeed then, it was anything wrong or wicked criminality, O Jews, according to reason I would endure you.

verses.name: Acts 18:15
verses.text: But if it is a question of a word and names, and <hi>of</hi> your law, you look <hi>to it</hi>. For I do not wish to be a judge of such things.

verses.name: Acts 18:16
verses.text: And he drove them from the judgment seat.

verses.name: Acts 18:17
verses.text: And all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat <hi>him</hi> before the judgment seat. And Gallio did not care for any of these things.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:18
verses.text: And Paul having remained many days more, taking leave of the brothers, he sailed from there into Syria. And Priscilla and Aquila were with him. And Paul had shorn his head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow.

verses.name: Acts 18:19
verses.text: And he came to Ephesus and left them there. But he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 18:20
verses.text: And they asking <hi>him</hi> to stay a longer time with them, he did not consent

verses.name: Acts 18:21
verses.text: but took leave of them, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that is coming in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you, God willing. And he sailed from Ephesus.

verses.name: Acts 18:22
verses.text: And when he had landed at Caesarea and had gone up to greet the church, he went down to Antioch.

verses.name: Acts 18:23
verses.text: And after he had spent some time <hi>there</hi>, he departed and went over the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:24
verses.text: And a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.

verses.name: Acts 18:25
verses.text: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord. And <hi>being</hi> fervent in the spirit, he spoke and taught the things of the Lord diligently, knowing only the baptism of John.

verses.name: Acts 18:26
verses.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. And Aquila and Priscilla heard him, and they took him and expounded to him the way of God more perfectly.

verses.name: Acts 18:27
verses.text: And intending to pass into Achaia, being encouraged, the brothers wrote to the disciples to welcome him; who, having arrived, very much helped those who had believed through grace.

verses.name: Acts 18:28
verses.text: For he mightily confuted the Jews publicly, proving by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:1
verses.text: And it happened in the <hi>time</hi> Apollos was at Corinth, Paul <hi>was</hi> passing through the higher parts to Ephesus. And finding certain disciples,

verses.name: Acts 19:2
verses.text: he said to them, Have you received <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit since you believed? And they said to him, We did not so much as hear whether <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit is.

verses.name: Acts 19:3
verses.text: And he said to them, Then to what were you baptized? And they said, To John's baptism.

verses.name: Acts 19:4
verses.text: And Paul said, John truly baptized <hi>with</hi> the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe into Him coming after him, that is, into Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Acts 19:5
verses.text: And hearing, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 19:6
verses.text: And as Paul laid <hi>his</hi> hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.

verses.name: Acts 19:7
verses.text: And all of the men were about twelve.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:8
verses.text: And going into the synagogue, he spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 19:9
verses.text: But when some were hardened and did not believe, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

verses.name: Acts 19:10
verses.text: And this happened over two years, so that all those living in Asia heard the Word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

verses.name: Acts 19:11
verses.text: And God did works of power through the hands of Paul,

verses.name: Acts 19:12
verses.text: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons from his skin being brought onto the sick, the diseases were released, and the evil spirits went out of them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:13
verses.text: And certain from the strolling Jews, exorcists, undertook to name the name of the Lord Jesus over those having evil spirits, saying, We adjure you <hi>by</hi> Jesus whom Paul preaches.

verses.name: Acts 19:14
verses.text: And there were seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did so.

verses.name: Acts 19:15
verses.text: But answering the evil spirit said, Jesus I know, and I comprehend Paul, but who are you?

verses.name: Acts 19:16
verses.text: And the man in whom the evil spirit resided leaped on them, and overcoming them he was strong against them, so that they fled out of the house naked and wounded.

verses.name: Acts 19:17
verses.text: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks who lived at Ephesus, and fear fell on all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

verses.name: Acts 19:18
verses.text: And many who believed came and confessed and showed their deeds.

verses.name: Acts 19:19
verses.text: Also many of those practicing the curious arts, bringing together the books, burned <hi>them</hi> before all. And they counted the prices of them and found <hi>it to be</hi> fifty thousand <hi>pieces</hi> of silver.

verses.name: Acts 19:20
verses.text: So the Word of God grew mightily and prevailed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:21
verses.text: After these things were ended, passing through Macedonia and Achaia, Paul purposed in the spirit to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have come there, I must also see Rome.

verses.name: Acts 19:22
verses.text: And sending into Macedonia two who ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus, he stayed in Asia for a time.

verses.name: Acts 19:23
verses.text: And about that time there was no little a stir about the Way.

verses.name: Acts 19:24
verses.text: For a certain silversmith named Demetrius was making silver temples of Artemis, providing not a little trade <hi>for</hi> the craftsmen.

verses.name: Acts 19:25
verses.text: And assembling the workmen about such things, he said, Men, you know that from this trade is our wealth.

verses.name: Acts 19:26
verses.text: And you see and hear that, not only at Ephesus, but almost all Asia, this Paul having persuaded, he has perverted a huge crowd, saying that those which are made with hands are no gods.

verses.name: Acts 19:27
verses.text: And not only is this dangerous to us, our share coming into dispute, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted for nothing, and her magnificence is also about to be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.

verses.name: Acts 19:28
verses.text: And hearing, and becoming full of anger, they cried out, saying, Great <hi>is</hi> Artemis of <hi>the</hi> Ephesians.

verses.name: Acts 19:29
verses.text: And all the city was filled with confusion. And they rushed with one accord to the theater, keeping a firm grip on Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, traveling companions of Paul.

verses.name: Acts 19:30
verses.text: And Paul intending to go in to the mob, the disciples did not allow him.

verses.name: Acts 19:31
verses.text: And some of the chief men of Asia, being his friends, sent to him, begging <hi>him</hi> not to give himself into the theater.

verses.name: Acts 19:32
verses.text: Then indeed others cried out, some other things; for the assembly was confused, and most of them did not know why they had come together.

verses.name: Acts 19:33
verses.text: And they dragged Alexander forward out of the crowd, the Jews thrusting him forward. And waving <hi>his</hi> hand Alexander desired to defend himself to the mob.

verses.name: Acts 19:34
verses.text: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice cried out for two hours' <hi>time</hi>, Great <hi>is</hi> Artemis of <hi>the</hi> Ephesians!

verses.name: Acts 19:35
verses.text: And quieting the crowd, the town clerk said, Men, Ephesians! What one of you does not know that the city of the Ephesians is a worshiper of the great goddess Artemis, and of That Fallen from the Sky?

verses.name: Acts 19:36
verses.text: Since these things cannot be spoken against, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rashly.

verses.name: Acts 19:37
verses.text: For you have brought these men, who are neither robbers of churches nor blasphemers of your goddess.

verses.name: Acts 19:38
verses.text: Therefore if Demetrius and those craftsmen with him truly have a matter against anyone, the court days are <hi>kept</hi>, and there are proconsuls. Let them plead against one another.

verses.name: Acts 19:39
verses.text: But if you ask anything concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

verses.name: Acts 19:40
verses.text: For we are in danger to be accused of revolt concerning today; there being no cause by which we may give an account of this crowding together.

verses.name: Acts 19:41
verses.text: And saying these things, he dismissed the assembly.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:1
verses.text: And after the uproar had ceased, calling the disciples and greeting <hi>them</hi>, Paul left to go into Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:2
verses.text: And passing through those parts, and exhorting them with much speech, he came into Greece.

verses.name: Acts 20:3
verses.text: And spending three months <hi>there</hi>, there <hi>being</hi> a plot against him by the Jews, being about to sail into Syria, he proposed to return through Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:4
verses.text: And Sopater of Berea accompanied him into Asia, and Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus as far as Asia.

verses.name: Acts 20:5
verses.text: Going before, these waited for us at Troas.

verses.name: Acts 20:6
verses.text: And after the days of Unleavened <hi>Bread</hi>, we sailed away from Philippi and came to them at Troas <hi>in</hi> five days, where we stayed seven days.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:7
verses.text: And on the first of the week, the disciples having been assembled to break bread, being about to depart on the morrow, Paul reasoned to them. And he continued his speech until midnight.

verses.name: Acts 20:8
verses.text: And there were many lights in the upper room where they were assembled.

verses.name: Acts 20:9
