verses.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus <hi>was</hi> sitting on the window sill, Paul reasoning for a longer time, being overborne by sleep, he fell down from the third floor, and was taken up dead.

verses.name: Acts 20:10
verses.text: And Paul went down and fell on him, and embracing <hi>him</hi> said, Do not be terrified, for his soul is in him.

verses.name: Acts 20:11
verses.text: And going up, and breaking bread, and tasting, and conversing over a long <hi>time</hi>, until daybreak, he went out thus.

verses.name: Acts 20:12
verses.text: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:13
verses.text: And going ahead onto the ship, we sailed to Assos, there intending to take in Paul; for so he had appointed, intending himself to go on foot.

verses.name: Acts 20:14
verses.text: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in and came to Mitylene.

verses.name: Acts 20:15
verses.text: And we sailed from there and came the next <hi>day</hi> across from Chios. And the next <hi>day</hi> we arrived at Samos, and we stayed at Trogyllium. And the next <hi>day</hi> we came to Miletus.

verses.name: Acts 20:16
verses.text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not lose time in Asia; for, if it were possible for him, he hastened to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:17
verses.text: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called the elders of the church.

verses.name: Acts 20:18
verses.text: And when they had come to him, he said to them, You know how I was with you at all times, from <hi>the</hi> first day I arrived in Asia,

verses.name: Acts 20:19
verses.text: serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and many tears and temptations happening to me through the plots of the Jews;

verses.name: Acts 20:20
verses.text: <hi> and</hi> how I kept back nothing that was profitable, but have shown you and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,

verses.name: Acts 20:21
verses.text: testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Acts 20:22
verses.text: And now, behold, I am going bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall happen to me there,

verses.name: Acts 20:23
verses.text: except that the Holy Spirit witnesses in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.

verses.name: Acts 20:24
verses.text: But none of these things move me, neither do I count my life dear to myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus <hi>Christ</hi>, to testify fully the gospel of the grace of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:25
verses.text: And now, behold, I know that you all will see my face no more, among whom I went proclaiming the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:26
verses.text: Therefore I testify to you on this day that I <hi>am</hi> pure from the blood of all.

verses.name: Acts 20:27
verses.text: For I did not keep back from declaring to you all the counsel of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:28
verses.text: Therefore take heed to yourselves, and to all the flock over which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to feed the church of God which He has purchased with <hi>His</hi> own blood.

verses.name: Acts 20:29
verses.text: For I know this, that after my departure grievous wolves shall enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

verses.name: Acts 20:30
verses.text: Also men shall arise from your own selves, speaking perverse things in order to draw disciples away after them.

verses.name: Acts 20:31
verses.text: Therefore watch and remember that <hi>for the time</hi> of three years I did not cease to warn everyone night and day with tears.

verses.name: Acts 20:32
verses.text: And now, brothers, I commend you to God, and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

verses.name: Acts 20:33
verses.text: I have coveted no man's silver or gold or apparel.

verses.name: Acts 20:34
verses.text: Yea, you yourselves know that these hands have ministered to my needs, and to those who were with me.

verses.name: Acts 20:35
verses.text: I have shown you all things, that working in this way we ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:36
verses.text: And saying these things, kneeling, he prayed with them all.

verses.name: Acts 20:37
verses.text: And there was much weeping of all, and falling on the neck of Paul, they ardently kissed him,

verses.name: Acts 20:38
verses.text: grieving most of all over the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they went with him to the ship.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:1
verses.text: And it happened when it was time to sail, we having been torn away from them, running direct we came to Cos; and on the next <hi>day</hi> to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

verses.name: Acts 21:2
verses.text: And finding a ship sailing over to Phoenicia, going on board, we set sail.

verses.name: Acts 21:3
verses.text: And sighting Cyprus, and leaving it on the left, we sailed into Syria, and came down to Tyre. For the ship was to unload its cargo there.

verses.name: Acts 21:4
verses.text: And finding disciples, we stayed there seven days; who said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:5
verses.text: But when it was <hi>time to</hi> finish the days, going out, we traveled on. <hi>And they</hi> with all <hi>the</hi> women and children went with us as far as outside the city. And we kneeled down on the shore and prayed.

verses.name: Acts 21:6
verses.text: And giving parting greetings to one another, we went up into the ship; and they returned to their own things.

verses.name: Acts 21:7
verses.text: And finishing the voyage from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais. And greeting the brothers, we stayed with them one day.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:8
verses.text: And the next <hi>day</hi> those around <hi>him</hi> going out, Paul came to Caesarea. And entering the house of Philip the evangelist, <hi>he</hi> being of the seven, we stayed with him.

verses.name: Acts 21:9
verses.text: And there were four virgin daughters to this one, who prophesied.

verses.name: Acts 21:10
verses.text: And as we stayed more days, a certain prophet from Judea named Agabus came down.

verses.name: Acts 21:11
verses.text: And coming to us, and taking Paul's belt, and binding his hands and feet, he said, The Holy Spirit says these <hi>things</hi>: So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man whose belt this is, and will deliver <hi>him</hi> into the hands of <hi>the</hi> nations.

verses.name: Acts 21:12
verses.text: And when we heard these things, both we and those of <hi>the</hi> place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:13
verses.text: Then Paul answered, What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 21:14
verses.text: And he not being persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be <hi>done</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:15
verses.text: And after those days, making ready, we went up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:16
verses.text: Also <hi>some</hi> of the disciples from Caesarea went with us, bringing Mnason, a certain Cypriot, an old disciple with whom we were to lodge.

verses.name: Acts 21:17
verses.text: And we being in Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

verses.name: Acts 21:18
verses.text: And on the next <hi>day</hi> Paul went with us to James. And all the elders were present.

verses.name: Acts 21:19
verses.text: And having greeted them, he related one by one what things God had done among the nations by his ministry.

verses.name: Acts 21:20
verses.text: And hearing, they glorified the Lord, and said to him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who believe, and they are all zealous of the law.

verses.name: Acts 21:21
verses.text: And they are informed concerning you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the nations to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise <hi>their</hi> children, nor to walk after the customs.

verses.name: Acts 21:22
verses.text: What is it therefore? At all events a multitude will come together, for they will hear that you have come.

verses.name: Acts 21:23
verses.text: Therefore do this, what we say to you: We have four men who have a vow on themselves;

verses.name: Acts 21:24
verses.text: taking them, be purified with them, and be at expense for them, so that they may shave <hi>their</hi> heads. And all may know that what they have been told about you is nothing, but you yourself also walk orderly and keep the Law.

verses.name: Acts 21:25
verses.text: And as to the nations who believe, we joined in writing, judging them to observe no such things, except only that they keep themselves from both idol sacrifice, and blood, and a thing strangled, and <hi>from</hi> fornication.

verses.name: Acts 21:26
verses.text: Then taking the men on the next day, being purified with them, Paul went into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of the purification, until an offering should be offered for each of them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:27
verses.text: And when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews who were from Asia, having seen him in the temple, stirred up all the crowd and laid hands on him,

verses.name: Acts 21:28
verses.text: crying out, Men, Israelites, help! This is the man who teaches all everywhere against the people and the Law and this place. And even he brought Greeks into the temple and has polluted this holy place.

verses.name: Acts 21:29
verses.text: (For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city before, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

verses.name: Acts 21:30
verses.text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together. And laying hands on Paul, they drew him outside of the temple. And immediately the doors were shut.

verses.name: Acts 21:31
verses.text: And as they <hi>were</hi> seeking to kill him, the news came to the chiliarch of the cohort, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.name: Acts 21:32
verses.text: <hi> He</hi> immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. And seeing the chiliarch and the soldiers, they quit beating Paul.

verses.name: Acts 21:33
verses.text: Then going near, the chiliarch laid hold on him, and commanded <hi>him</hi> to be bound with two chains. And <hi>he</hi> demanded who he was and what he had done.

verses.name: Acts 21:34
verses.text: And others cried something else in the crowd, and not being able to know the certainty on account of the uproar, he commanded him to be carried into the fortress.

verses.name: Acts 21:35
verses.text: And when he came on the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers, because of the violence of the crowd.

verses.name: Acts 21:36
verses.text: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him!

verses.name: Acts 21:37
verses.text: And as Paul was about to be led into the fortress, he said to the chiliarch, Is it lawful for me to say a thing to you? And he said, Do you know Greek?

verses.name: Acts 21:38
verses.text: Then are you not the Egyptian who before these days caused a riot, and led four thousand men of the assassins out into the wilderness?

verses.name: Acts 21:39
verses.text: But Paul said, I am a man, a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen <hi>of</hi> no small city. And I beseech you, allow me to speak to the people.

verses.name: Acts 21:40
verses.text: And he allowing him, standing on the stairs, Paul signaled with <hi>his</hi> hand to the people. And much silence taking place, he spoke in the Hebrew dialect, saying:  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:1
verses.text: Men, brothers and fathers! Hear my defense now to you.

verses.name: Acts 22:2
verses.text: And hearing that he spoke to them in the Hebrew dialect, they all the more kept silence. And he said,  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:3
verses.text: I am truly a man, a Jew born in Tarsus in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the exactness of the law of the fathers, being a zealous one of God, as you all are today.

verses.name: Acts 22:4
verses.text: <hi> I</hi> persecuted this Way as far as death, binding and delivering both men and women into prisons;

verses.name: Acts 22:5
verses.text: as also the high priest bears witness to me, and all the elderhood. And receiving letters from <hi>them</hi> to the brothers, I traveled into Damascus indeed to lead those being bound to Jerusalem, in order that they might be punished.

verses.name: Acts 22:6
verses.text: And it happened to me, traveling and drawing near to Damascus: suddenly, about midday, a great light out of the heaven shone around me.

verses.name: Acts 22:7
verses.text: And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?

verses.name: Acts 22:8
verses.text: And I answered, Who are you, lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.

verses.name: Acts 22:9
verses.text: And they who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid. But they did not hear the voice of Him who spoke to me.

verses.name: Acts 22:10
verses.text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Arise and go into Damascus. And there it shall be told you all things which are appointed for you to do.

verses.name: Acts 22:11
verses.text: And I did not see, because of the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

verses.name: Acts 22:12
verses.text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, testified to by all the Jews who lived <hi>there</hi>,

verses.name: Acts 22:13
verses.text: coming to me and standing by, said to me, Brother Saul, look up! And the same hour I looked up on him.

verses.name: Acts 22:14
verses.text: And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen you to know His will and to see the Just One, and to hear a voice out of His mouth.

verses.name: Acts 22:15
verses.text: For you shall be His witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.

verses.name: Acts 22:16
verses.text: And now what do you intend? Arise and be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 22:17
verses.text: And it happened to me, I returning to Jerusalem and praying in the temple, I became in an ecstasy.

verses.name: Acts 22:18
verses.text: And I saw Him say to me, Hurry and go quickly out of Jerusalem, for they will not receive your testimony concerning Me.

verses.name: Acts 22:19
verses.text: And I said, Lord, they know that I was imprisoning and beating those who believed on You throughout the synagogues.

verses.name: Acts 22:20
verses.text: And when the blood of Your martyr Stephen was poured out, I also was standing by and consenting to his death, and holding the garments of those who killed him.

verses.name: Acts 22:21
verses.text: And He said to me, Go, for I will send you far away to the nations.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:22
verses.text: And they listened to him until this word, and <hi>then</hi> they lifted up their voice, saying, Take such a one from the earth! For it is not fitting that he should live.

verses.name: Acts 22:23
verses.text: And as they shouted and tore <hi>their</hi> garments, and threw dust into the air,

verses.name: Acts 22:24
verses.text: the chiliarch commanded him to be brought into the fortress, saying for him to be examined by scourging, so that he might know why they cried out so against him.

verses.name: Acts 22:25
verses.text: And as they stretched him with thongs, Paul said to the centurion who stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman and uncondemned?

verses.name: Acts 22:26
verses.text: And hearing, coming near the centurion reported to the chiliarch, saying, Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman.

verses.name: Acts 22:27
verses.text: And coming up the chiliarch said to him, Tell me, are you a Roman? And He said, Yes.

verses.name: Acts 22:28
verses.text: And the chiliarch answered, With a great sum I bought this citizenship. And Paul said, But I was even born <hi>free</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 22:29
verses.text: Then immediately, those being about to examine him stood away from him. And the chiliarch also was afraid, fully knowing that he was a Roman, and that he had bound him.

verses.name: Acts 22:30
verses.text: On the next day, he desiring to know with certainty why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from <hi>his</hi> bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their sanhedrin to appear. And bringing Paul down, <hi>he</hi> set <hi>him</hi> among them.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:1
verses.text: And looking earnestly on the sanhedrin, Paul said, Men, brothers, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

verses.name: Acts 23:2
verses.text: And the high priest Ananias commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

verses.name: Acts 23:3
verses.text: Then Paul said to him, God shall strike you, whitened wall! For do you sit judging me according to the Law, and against law command me to be stricken?

verses.name: Acts 23:4
verses.text: And they who stood by him said, Do you revile God's high priest?

verses.name: Acts 23:5
verses.text: Then Paul said, I did not know, brothers, that he was the high priest; for it is written, "You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people."  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:6
verses.text: But when Paul saw that the one part were Sadducees and the other part Pharisees, he cried out in the sanhedrin, Men! Brothers! I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee! I am being judged because of the hope and resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead.

verses.name: Acts 23:7
verses.text: And when he had said this, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees; and the multitude was divided.

verses.name: Acts 23:8
verses.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess both.

verses.name: Acts 23:9
verses.text: And there arose a great cry. And the scribes <hi>who were</hi> on the Pharisees' side arose and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

verses.name: Acts 23:10
verses.text: And dissension arising, the chiliarch, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and to take him from among them by force, and to bring <hi>him</hi> into the fortress.

verses.name: Acts 23:11
verses.text: And the following night the Lord stood by him and said, Be of good cheer, Paul, for as you have testified of Me in Jerusalem, so you also must bear witness at Rome.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:12
verses.text: And when <hi>it</hi> became day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:13
verses.text: And they who made this conspiracy were more than forty.

verses.name: Acts 23:14
verses.text: And they came to the chief priests and elders and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse that we will eat nothing until we have killed Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:15
verses.text: Now therefore you, with the sanhedrin, inform the chiliarch that he bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you would inquire something more perfectly regarding him. And we are ready to put him to death before he comes near.

verses.name: Acts 23:16
verses.text: And hearing of the ambush, Paul's sister's son, having come near, and entering into the fortress, he reported to Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:17
verses.text: And calling one of the centurions, Paul said, Bring this young man to the chiliarch, for he has a certain thing to tell him.

verses.name: Acts 23:18
verses.text: So he took him and brought <hi>him</hi> to the chiliarch and said, Paul the prisoner called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to say to you.

verses.name: Acts 23:19
verses.text: And laying hold of his hand, and drawing aside privately, the chiliarch asked <hi>him</hi>, What is <hi>it</hi> that you have to tell me?

verses.name: Acts 23:20
verses.text: And he said, The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the sanhedrin tomorrow, as though they would inquire something more exactly about him.

verses.name: Acts 23:21
verses.text: But do not yield to them, for there are more than forty men of them lying in wait for him, who have bound themselves with an oath that they will neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. And now they are ready, looking for a promise from you.

verses.name: Acts 23:22
verses.text: So the chiliarch sent away the young man commanding, Tell no one that you have shown these things to me.

verses.name: Acts 23:23
verses.text: And he called two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night.

verses.name: Acts 23:24
verses.text: And provide animals, so that they may set Paul on them and bring <hi>him</hi> to Felix the governor.

verses.name: Acts 23:25
verses.text: And he wrote a letter in this way:

verses.name: Acts 23:26
verses.text: Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix, greetings.

verses.name: Acts 23:27
verses.text: This man was taken by the Jews and would have been killed by them. Then I came with an army and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.name: Acts 23:28
verses.text: And being minded to know the charge for which they accused him, I brought him down to their sanhedrin;

verses.name: Acts 23:29
verses.text: whom I found be accused of questions of their law, and having no charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Acts 23:30
verses.text: And it being revealed to me that a plot against the man was about to be <hi>executed</hi> by the Jews, I immediately sent him to you, commanding his accusers also to say before you what <hi>they had</hi> against him. Farewell.

verses.name: Acts 23:31
verses.text: Then, indeed, taking up Paul, as it was commanded them, the soldiers brought <hi>him</hi> by night to Antipatris.

verses.name: Acts 23:32
verses.text: And on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him and returned to the fortress.

verses.name: Acts 23:33
verses.text: And when they had come to Caesarea and had delivered the letter to the governor, <hi>they</hi> presented Paul before him also.

verses.name: Acts 23:34
verses.text: And when the governor had read <hi>the letter</hi>, he asked what province he was from. And when he understood that <hi>he was</hi> from Cilicia,

verses.name: Acts 23:35
verses.text: he said, I will hear you when your accusers have also come. And <hi>he</hi> commanded him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:1
verses.text: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders and <hi>with</hi> a certain orator, Tertullus, who made a statement to the governor against Paul.

verses.name: Acts 24:2
verses.text: And being called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying,

verses.name: Acts 24:3
verses.text: Since we enjoy great quietness by you, and very worthy deeds are done to this nation due to your forethought, in everything and everywhere, most noble Felix, we accept with all thankfulness.

verses.name: Acts 24:4
verses.text: But that I not hinder you further, I beseech you to hear us briefly in your fairness.

verses.name: Acts 24:5
verses.text: For we have found this man pestilent, and moving rebellion among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

verses.name: Acts 24:6
verses.text: who also attempted to profane the temple, whom we took and would have judged according to our law.

verses.name: Acts 24:7
verses.text: But the chiliarch Lysias came with much force, taking <hi>him</hi> away out of our hands,

verses.name: Acts 24:8
verses.text: commanding his accusers to come to you. By examining him, you yourself may know about all these things of which we accuse him.

verses.name: Acts 24:9
verses.text: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:10
verses.text: But the governor motioning to him to speak, Paul answered; Understanding you as being a judge of this nation many years, I cheerfully defend myself <hi>as to</hi> the things concerning myself.

verses.name: Acts 24:11
verses.text: You can know that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

verses.name: Acts 24:12
verses.text: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, nor making a gathering of a crowd; not even in the synagogues, nor throughout the city.

verses.name: Acts 24:13
verses.text: Nor can they prove the things of which they now accuse me.

verses.name: Acts 24:14
verses.text: But I confess this to you, that after the Way which they call heresy, so I worship the God of my fathers, believing all things that are written in the Law and in the Prophets.

verses.name: Acts 24:15
verses.text: And I have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead, both of the just and unjust.

verses.name: Acts 24:16
verses.text: And in this I exercise myself, always to have a blameless conscience toward God and men.

verses.name: Acts 24:17
verses.text: And after many years I came to bring alms and offerings to my nation.

verses.name: Acts 24:18
verses.text: Among which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with tumult.

verses.name: Acts 24:19
verses.text: These ought to be present before you and to accuse me, if they have anything against me.

verses.name: Acts 24:20
verses.text: Or else let these themselves say if they have found anything unjust in me while I stood before the sanhedrin,

verses.name: Acts 24:21
verses.text: unless it may be for this one voice that I cried out standing among them, that concerning a resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead I am being judged by you today.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:22
verses.text: And having heard these things, Felix put them off, knowing more accurately of the Way, saying, When Lysias the chiliarch has come down, I will examine the things concerning you.

verses.name: Acts 24:23
verses.text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul and to let <hi>him</hi> have liberty, and not to forbid anyone of his own to minister or come to him.

verses.name: Acts 24:24
verses.text: Then after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

verses.name: Acts 24:25
verses.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and the Judgment to come, Felix trembled and answered, Go for this time, but taking time later, I will call for you.

verses.name: Acts 24:26
verses.text: He also hoped that silver would be given him by Paul, that he might free him. Therefore <hi>he</hi> also frequently sent for him <hi>and</hi> talked with him.

verses.name: Acts 24:27
verses.text: But after two years Felix welcomed a successor, Porcius Festus. And wishing to show a favor to the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:1
verses.text: Then entering the province, after three days Festus went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 25:2
verses.text: And the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him

verses.name: Acts 25:3
verses.text: asking a favor against him that he would send for him to Jerusalem, making a plot to kill him on way.

verses.name: Acts 25:4
verses.text: Then indeed Festus answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea; he himself would depart shortly.

verses.name: Acts 25:5
verses.text: Then he said, those having power among you may go down with <hi>me</hi>. If there is a thing amiss in this man, let them accuse him.

verses.name: Acts 25:6
verses.text: And staying among them more than ten days, going down to Caesarea, on the next day sitting on the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.

verses.name: Acts 25:7
verses.text: And he having come, the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stood around and brought many charges against Paul, which they could not prove.

verses.name: Acts 25:8
verses.text: Defending himself, <hi>Paul</hi> said, Neither against the Law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I offended in anything.

verses.name: Acts 25:9
verses.text: But Festus, wanting to please the Jews, answered Paul and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem and be judged there before me about these things?

verses.name: Acts 25:10
verses.text: But Paul said, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you very well know.

verses.name: Acts 25:11
verses.text: For if I am an offender or have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing of which these accuse me, no one can deliver me to them. I appeal to Caesar.

verses.name: Acts 25:12
verses.text: Then conferring with the sanhedrin, Festus answered, You have appealed to Caesar? To Caesar you shall go.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:13
verses.text: And after some days king Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.

verses.name: Acts 25:14
verses.text: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause to the king, saying, A certain man has been left in bonds by Felix,

verses.name: Acts 25:15
verses.text: about whom, when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed <hi>me</hi>, desiring judgment against him.

verses.name: Acts 25:16
verses.text: To them I answered, It is not the custom of the Romans to deliver any man to destruction before he being accused may have the accusers face to face, and have had freedom to answer for himself concerning the accusation.

verses.name: Acts 25:17
verses.text: Therefore, when they had come here, without any delay I sat on the judgment seat the next <hi>day</hi> and commanded the man to be brought,

verses.name: Acts 25:18
verses.text: about whom, standing up, the accusers brought against him no charge of which I suspected,

verses.name: Acts 25:19
verses.text: but they had certain questions about <hi>their</hi> own demon-worship, and about a certain Jesus dying, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

verses.name: Acts 25:20
verses.text: And because I was perplexed about this question, I asked whether he would go to Jerusalem and be judged there about these matters.

verses.name: Acts 25:21
verses.text: But Paul having appealed to be reserved to the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be held until I might send him to Caesar.

verses.name: Acts 25:22
verses.text: And Agrippa said to Festus, I also would like to hear the man myself. And he said, Tomorrow you shall hear him.

verses.name: Acts 25:23
verses.text: And on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp and had entered into the auditorium with both the chiliarchs and principal men of the city, also Festus commanding, Paul was brought out.

verses.name: Acts 25:24
verses.text: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all those men present with us, you see this one about whom all the multitude of the Jews pleaded with me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.name: Acts 25:25
verses.text: But I had perceived nothing he had committed worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I determined to send him,

verses.name: Acts 25:26
verses.text: about whom I have no certain thing to write of him to <hi>my</hi> lord. Therefore I brought him before you, and especially before you, O king Agrippa, so that, after examination is made, I might have something to write.

verses.name: Acts 25:27
verses.text: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not to signify the charges against him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:1
verses.text: And Agrippa said to Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then stretching out his hand, Paul made a defense:

verses.name: Acts 26:2
verses.text: Concerning all of which I am accused by Jews, king Agrippa, I think myself happy being about to make defense before you today,

verses.name: Acts 26:3
verses.text: you being especially expert in all customs and questions among the Jews. Therefore I beseech you to hear me patiently.

verses.name: Acts 26:4
verses.text: Truly, then, all the Jews know my manner of life from my youth, which was at first among my own nation at Jerusalem,

verses.name: Acts 26:5
verses.text: who knew me from the first, if they would testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

verses.name: Acts 26:6
verses.text: And now I stand and am judged for <hi>the</hi> hope of the promise made to our fathers by God,

verses.name: Acts 26:7
verses.text: to which <hi>promise</hi> our twelve tribes hope to attain, serving God fervently night and day. For the sake of this hope, king Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 26:8
verses.text: Why is it thought a thing incredible with you that God raises <hi>the</hi> dead?

verses.name: Acts 26:9
verses.text: I truly thought within myself that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth,

verses.name: Acts 26:10
verses.text: which I also did in Jerusalem. And I shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests. And they being put to death, I cast a vote.

verses.name: Acts 26:11
verses.text: And I punished them often in every synagogue; I compelled <hi>them</hi> to blaspheme; and <hi>being</hi> exceedingly furious against them, I persecuted them even to the outside cities.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:12
verses.text: In which pursuit also traveling to Damascus with authority and power of decision from the chief priests,

verses.name: Acts 26:13
verses.text: at midday, along the highway, O king, I and those with me saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun; shining around me.

verses.name: Acts 26:14
verses.text: And all of us falling to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me and saying in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? <hi>It is</hi> hard for you to kick against the goads.

verses.name: Acts 26:15
verses.text: And I said, Who are you, lord? And He said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.

verses.name: Acts 26:16
verses.text: But rise and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of what you saw, and in what I shall appear to you;

verses.name: Acts 26:17
verses.text: delivering you from the people and the nations, to whom I now send you

verses.name: Acts 26:18
verses.text: in order to open their eyes so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the authority of Satan to God, so that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.

verses.name: Acts 26:19
verses.text: After this, king Agrippa, I did not disobey the heavenly vision.

verses.name: Acts 26:20
verses.text: But to those first in Damascus, and Jerusalem, and to all the country of Judea, and to the nations, I made known <hi>the command</hi> to repent and to turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance

verses.name: Acts 26:21
verses.text: Because of these things, having caught <hi>me</hi> in the temple, The Jews tried to kill <hi>me</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 26:22
verses.text: Then having obtained help from God, I stand until this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses said was going to happen;

verses.name: Acts 26:23
verses.text: that Christ should suffer, <hi>that</hi> by a resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead, He would be the first, going to proclaim light to the people and to the nations.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:24
verses.text: And he defending himself <hi>with</hi> these things, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you rave! Your many letters turn <hi>you</hi> to insanity.

verses.name: Acts 26:25
verses.text: But he said, Not to insanity, most noble Festus, but I speak words of truth and sanity.

verses.name: Acts 26:26
verses.text: For the king understands about these things, to whom I speak, even being bold of speech. For I am persuaded that not any of these things are hidden <hi>from</hi> him, nothing. For the doing of this was not in a corner.

verses.name: Acts 26:27
verses.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.

verses.name: Acts 26:28
verses.text: And Agrippa said to Paul, Do you persuade me to be a Christian in <hi>but</hi> a little?

verses.name: Acts 26:29
verses.text: And Paul said, I would pray to God, both in a little and in much, that not only you, but also all hearing me today to become as I also am, except for these bonds.

verses.name: Acts 26:30
verses.text: And he having spoken this, the king and the governor and Bernice and those who sat with them rose up.

verses.name: Acts 26:31
verses.text: And withdrawing, they spoke with one another, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Acts 26:32
verses.text: And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been set at liberty if he had not appealed to Caesar.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:1
verses.text: And when it was determined that we should sail to Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to <hi>one</hi> named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' cohort.

verses.name: Acts 27:2
verses.text: And boarding a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail alongside Asian places, we set sail, Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.name: Acts 27:3
verses.text: And on the next <hi>day</hi> we were landed at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul courteously and gave <hi>him</hi> liberty to go to his friends to receive care.

verses.name: Acts 27:4
verses.text: And setting sail from there, we sailed close to Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

verses.name: Acts 27:5
verses.text: And sailing over the sea against Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra of Lycia.

verses.name: Acts 27:6
verses.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing to Italy, and he put us on it.

verses.name: Acts 27:7
verses.text: And sailing slowly many days and with difficulty, coming abreast of Cnidus; the wind not allowing us; we sailed close to Crete, across from Salmone.

verses.name: Acts 27:8
verses.text: And coasting along with difficulty, we came to a place named Fair Havens, near which was a city, Lasea.

verses.name: Acts 27:9
verses.text: And much time having been used up, and the voyage already being dangerous, because the Fast was now already past, Paul warned <hi>them</hi>,

verses.name: Acts 27:10
verses.text: saying, Men, I perceive that this voyage is about to be with much harm and loss, and not only much cargo and of the ship, but also of our souls.

verses.name: Acts 27:11
verses.text: But the centurion was rather persuaded by the helmsman and the shipmaster, than by the things spoken by Paul.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:12
verses.text: And the port not being fit to winter in, the most of them advised to set sail from there, if by any means they might be able to get to Phoenix to winter; <hi>which is</hi> a port of Crete, looking toward <hi>the</hi> southwest and northwest.

verses.name: Acts 27:13
verses.text: And a south wind blowing softly, thinking to have obtained <hi>their</hi> purpose, lifting <hi>anchor</hi>, they sailed along close beside Crete.

verses.name: Acts 27:14
verses.text: But not long after, a stormy wind called Euroclydon beat down <hi>on</hi> it.

verses.name: Acts 27:15
verses.text: And the ship being seized, and not being able to beat against the wind, giving way we were borne along.

verses.name: Acts 27:16
verses.text: And running under an islet being called Clauda, we hardly were able to become masters of the boat;

verses.name: Acts 27:17
verses.text: which taking, they used helps, undergirding the ship. And fearing lest they should fall into the sandbanks of Syrtis, lowering the tackle, so they were borne along.

verses.name: Acts 27:18
verses.text: And being exceedingly storm-tossed with a tempest, they made a casting on the next <hi>day</hi>;

verses.name: Acts 27:19
verses.text: And on the third <hi>day</hi> we threw out the ship's tackle with our hands.

verses.name: Acts 27:20
verses.text: And neither sun nor stars appearing in many days, and no small tempest pressing hard, now all hope that we would be saved was taken away.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:21
verses.text: But there being much fasting, then standing up in their midst, Paul said, O men, being obedient to me <hi>you</hi> ought not to have set sail from Crete, and to have come by this harm and loss.

verses.name: Acts 27:22
verses.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer, for there will be no casting away of life among you, only of the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:23
verses.text: For tonight an angel of God stood beside me, whose I am and whom I serve,

verses.name: Acts 27:24
verses.text: saying, Fear not, Paul! You must stand before Caesar. And behold! God has given you all those who sail with you.

verses.name: Acts 27:25
verses.text: Therefore, men, be of good cheer, for I believe God, that it will be so, according to the way it was told me.

verses.name: Acts 27:26
verses.text: But we must fall on a certain island.

verses.name: Acts 27:27
verses.text: But when <hi>the</hi> fourteenth night came, we being carried about in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors thought that they drew near some country.

verses.name: Acts 27:28
verses.text: And sounding they found it twenty fathoms; and moving a little further, and sounding again, they found <hi>it</hi> fifteen fathoms.

verses.name: Acts 27:29
verses.text: And fearing that we would fall on rocks, and casting four anchors out of <hi>the</hi> stern, they wished day to come.

verses.name: Acts 27:30
verses.text: But the sailors seeking to flee out of the ship, and lowering the boat into the sea, pretending to be about to cast out anchors from <hi>the</hi> prow,

verses.name: Acts 27:31
verses.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Unless these remain in the ship, you cannot be saved.

verses.name: Acts 27:32
verses.text: Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat, and let her fall.

verses.name: Acts 27:33
verses.text: And until day was about to come, Paul begged all to take food, saying, This <hi>is</hi> the fourteenth day that you continued waiting without food, having taken nothing.

verses.name: Acts 27:34
verses.text: Therefore I beg you to take <hi>some</hi> food, for this is for your deliverance. For not a hair of your head shall perish.

verses.name: Acts 27:35
verses.text: And saying these things, and taking bread, he gave thanks to God before all, and breaking, he began to eat.

verses.name: Acts 27:36
verses.text: And all becoming cheered, they also took food.

verses.name: Acts 27:37
verses.text: And we were, all the souls in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six.

verses.name: Acts 27:38
verses.text: And being filled <hi>with</hi> food, they lightened the ship, throwing the wheat into the sea.

verses.name: Acts 27:39
verses.text: And when day came, they did not recognize the land. But they discovered a certain bay with a beach, into which they were minded, if they were able, to drive the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:40
verses.text: And casting off the anchors, they left <hi>them</hi> in the sea; at the same time they loosened the rudder bands and hoisted up the foresail to the wind and held to the shore.

verses.name: Acts 27:41
verses.text: And coming on a place between two seas, they drove the vessel. And indeed the prow sticking fast, <hi>it</hi> remained unmovable. But the stern was broken with the violence of the waves.

verses.name: Acts 27:42
verses.text: And the mind of the soldiers was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out and escape.

verses.name: Acts 27:43
verses.text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, kept them from <hi>their</hi> purpose and commanded those who could swim, to throw <hi>themselves</hi> overboard, to go out on the land.

verses.name: Acts 27:44
verses.text: And the rest <hi>went</hi>, some on boards and others on some of the things from the ship. And so it happened that all were saved on the land.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:1
verses.text: And being saved, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

verses.name: Acts 28:2
verses.text: And the foreigners showed us not the common kindness. For they kindled a fire and welcomed all of us, because of the rain coming on, and because of the cold.

verses.name: Acts 28:3
verses.text: And Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laying <hi>them</hi> on the fire, a viper came out of the heat and fastened on his hand.

verses.name: Acts 28:4
verses.text: And when the foreigners saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, being saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed to live.

verses.name: Acts 28:5
verses.text: Then indeed he shook off the creature into the fire, suffering no harm.

verses.name: Acts 28:6
verses.text: But they expected him to be about to become inflamed, or to fall down dead suddenly, But over much <hi>time</hi> expecting and seeing nothing amiss happening to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.

verses.name: Acts 28:7
verses.text: In the <hi>quarters</hi> about that place were lands to the chief of the island, whose name was Publius. Welcoming us, <hi>he</hi> lodged us courteously three days.

verses.name: Acts 28:8
verses.text: And it happened the father of Publius was lying down, suffering fevers and dysentery; to whom Paul entered in, and praying and laying on his hands, he healed him.

verses.name: Acts 28:9
verses.text: Then this taking place, the rest who were having infirmities in the island also came, and were healed.

verses.name: Acts 28:10
verses.text: <hi> They</hi> also honored us with many honors. And on <hi>our</hi> setting sail, they laid on the things of <hi>our</hi> needs.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:11
verses.text: And after three months we sailed in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, an Alexandrian with an ensign, The Twin Brothers.

verses.name: Acts 28:12
verses.text: And landing at Syracuse, we stayed three days.

verses.name: Acts 28:13
verses.text: Going around from there we arrived at Rhegium. And after one day a south wind coming on, we came to Puteoli on the second,

verses.name: Acts 28:14
verses.text: where finding brothers, we were asked to stay seven days. And so we went toward Rome.

verses.name: Acts 28:15
verses.text: And the brothers from there hearing of us, <hi>they</hi> came to meet us as far as <hi>the</hi> market-place of Appius, and Three Taverns. Seeing them, thanking God, Paul took courage.

verses.name: Acts 28:16
verses.text: And when we came into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the camp commander. But Paul was allowed to dwell by himself, with a soldier guarding him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:17
verses.text: And after three days it happened that Paul called together those being chief of the Jews. And they coming together, he said to them, Men, brothers, I did nothing against the people or customs of our fathers. I was delivered a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans

verses.name: Acts 28:18
verses.text: who, examining me, were of a mind to let <hi>me</hi> go because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.name: Acts 28:19
verses.text: But the Jews speaking against <hi>it</hi>, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar; not as having anything to accuse my nation.

verses.name: Acts 28:20
verses.text: For this cause, then, I called for you, to see and to speak with <hi>you</hi>. For I have this chain around me for the hope of Israel.

verses.name: Acts 28:21
verses.text: And they said to him, We neither received letters out of Judea concerning you, nor have any of the brothers who came declared or spoke anything evil of you.

verses.name: Acts 28:22
verses.text: But we think <hi>it</hi> right to hear from you what you think. For truly as concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:23
verses.text: And they having appointed him a day, many came to him in <hi>his</hi> lodging; to whom he expounded, testifying the kingdom of God, and persuading them the things concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses and out of the prophets, from morning until evening.

verses.name: Acts 28:24
verses.text: And some indeed believed the things that were said, others did not believe.

verses.name: Acts 28:25
verses.text: And disagreeing with one another, they were let go, Paul saying one word: Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

verses.name: Acts 28:26
verses.text: saying, "Go to this people and say: Hearing you shall hear and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see and not perceive.

verses.name: Acts 28:27
verses.text: For the heart of this people was fattened, and they have heard with their ears dully; and they closed their eyes; lest at any time they should see with <hi>their</hi> eyes, and hear with <hi>their</hi> ears, and understand with <hi>their</hi> heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them."

verses.name: Acts 28:28
verses.text: Therefore be it known to you that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will hear.

verses.name: Acts 28:29
verses.text: And he having said these words, the Jews departed, having much discussion amongst themselves.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:30
verses.text: And Paul remained two years in his own hired house. And he welcomed all who came in to him,

verses.name: Acts 28:31
verses.text: proclaiming the kingdom of God, and teaching those things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom, <hi>and</hi> without hindrance.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:1
verses.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, separated to the gospel of God

verses.name: Romans 1:2
verses.text: (which He had promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures),

verses.name: Romans 1:3
verses.text: about His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh,

verses.name: Romans 1:4
verses.text: who was marked out the Son of God in power, according to <hi>the</hi> Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from <hi>the</hi> dead;

verses.name: Romans 1:5
verses.text: by whom we have received grace and apostleship, to obedience to the faith among all nations, for His name;

verses.name: Romans 1:6
verses.text: among whom you also are the called-out ones of Jesus Christ:

verses.name: Romans 1:7
verses.text: to all those who are in Rome, beloved of God, called-out saints. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and <hi>the</hi> Lord Jesus Christ.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:8
verses.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Romans 1:9
verses.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of His Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you

verses.name: Romans 1:10
verses.text: always in my prayers, making request if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come to you.

verses.name: Romans 1:11
verses.text: For I long to see you, so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to you for the establishing of you.

verses.name: Romans 1:12
verses.text: And this is to be comforted together with you by our mutual faith, both yours and mine.

verses.name: Romans 1:13
verses.text: But I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that oftentimes I purposed to come to you, and was kept back until the present; that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other nations.

verses.name: Romans 1:14
verses.text: I am debtor both to the Greeks and to the foreigners, both to the wise and to the unwise.

verses.name: Romans 1:15
verses.text: So, as much as is in me <hi>lies</hi>, I am ready to preach the gospel to you who are at Rome also.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:16
verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is <hi>the</hi> power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

verses.name: Romans 1:17
verses.text: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written, "The just shall live by faith."

verses.name: Romans 1:18
verses.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from Heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness,  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:19
verses.text: because the thing which may be known of God is clearly revealed within them, for God revealed <hi>it</hi> to them.

verses.name: Romans 1:20
verses.text: For the unseen things of Him from <hi>the</hi> creation of <hi>the</hi> world <hi>are</hi> clearly seen, being realized by the things that are made, <hi>even</hi> His eternal power and Godhead, for them to be without excuse.

verses.name: Romans 1:21
verses.text: Because, knowing God, they did not glorify Him as God, neither were thankful. But <hi>they</hi> became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.name: Romans 1:22
verses.text: Professing to be wise, they became fools

verses.name: Romans 1:23
verses.text: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man, and birds, and four-footed animals, and creeping things.

verses.name: Romans 1:24
verses.text: Therefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of <hi>their</hi> hearts, to dishonor their own bodies between themselves.

verses.name: Romans 1:25
verses.text: For they changed the truth of God into a lie, and they worshiped and served the created thing more than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

verses.name: Romans 1:26
verses.text: For this cause, God gave them up to dishonorable affections. For even their women changed the natural use into that which is against nature.

verses.name: Romans 1:27
verses.text: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another; males with males working out shamefulness, and receiving in themselves the recompense which was fitting for their error.

verses.name: Romans 1:28
verses.text: And even as they did not think fit to have God in <hi>their</hi> knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do the things not right,

verses.name: Romans 1:29
verses.text: being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; <hi>being</hi> full of envy, murder, quarrels, deceit, evil habits, <hi>becoming</hi> whisperers,

verses.name: Romans 1:30
verses.text: backbiters, haters of God, insolent, proud, braggarts, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

verses.name: Romans 1:31
verses.text: without discernment, covenant-breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful;

verses.name: Romans 1:32
verses.text: who, knowing the righteous order of God, that those practicing such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but have pleasure in those practicing <hi>them</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:1
verses.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who judges; for in that in which you judge another, you condemn yourself, for you who judge do the same things.

verses.name: Romans 2:2
verses.text: But know that the judgment of God is according to truth on those who practice such things.

verses.name: Romans 2:3
verses.text: And, O man, the <hi>one</hi> judging those who do such things, and practice them, do you think this, that you shall escape the judgment of God?

verses.name: Romans 2:4
verses.text: Or do you despise the riches of His kindness, and the forbearance and long-suffering, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?

verses.name: Romans 2:5
verses.text: But according to your hardness and your impenitent heart, do you treasure up wrath for yourself in a day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,

verses.name: Romans 2:6
verses.text: who will render to each according to his works;

verses.name: Romans 2:7
verses.text: indeed to those who with patience <hi>in</hi> good work <hi>are</hi> seeking for glory, and honor, and incorruptibility, everlasting life.

verses.name: Romans 2:8
verses.text: But to those who even disobey the truth out of self-interest, but obey unrighteousness, <hi>it will be</hi> anger and wrath,

verses.name: Romans 2:9
verses.text: tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man who has worked out evil; of the Jew first, and also of the Greek.

verses.name: Romans 2:10
verses.text: But He <hi>will give</hi> glory, honor and peace to every man who works good, to <hi>the</hi> Jew first and also to <hi>the</hi> Greek.

verses.name: Romans 2:11
verses.text: For there is no respect of persons with God.

verses.name: Romans 2:12
verses.text: For as many as sinned without Law will also perish without Law. And as many as have sinned within Law shall be judged through Law.

verses.name: Romans 2:13
verses.text: For it is not the hearers of the Law who <hi>are</hi> just before God, but the doers of the Law will be justified.

verses.name: Romans 2:14
verses.text: For when the nations, who do not have the Law, do by nature the things of the Law, these, not having the Law, are a law unto themselves;

verses.name: Romans 2:15
verses.text: who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and the thoughts between one another accusing or even excusing one another,

verses.name: Romans 2:16
verses.text: in a day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:17
verses.text: Behold, you are called a Jew, and rest in the Law, and boast in God;

verses.name: Romans 2:18
verses.text: and know <hi>His</hi> will and approve the things excelling, being instructed out of the Law;

verses.name: Romans 2:19
verses.text: and persuading yourselves to be a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness;

verses.name: Romans 2:20
verses.text: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, who have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the Law.

verses.name: Romans 2:21
verses.text: Therefore the <hi>one</hi> teaching another, do you not teach yourself? The <hi>one</hi> preaching not to steal, do you steal?

verses.name: Romans 2:22
verses.text: The <hi>one</hi> saying not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? The <hi>one</hi> detesting idols, do you rob temples?

verses.name: Romans 2:23
verses.text: <hi> You</hi> who boast in Law, do you dishonor God through breaking the Law?

verses.name: Romans 2:24
verses.text: For the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you, as it is written.

verses.name: Romans 2:25
verses.text: For circumcision truly profits if you keep <hi>the</hi> Law, but if you are a transgressor of the Law, circumcision becomes uncircumcision.

verses.name: Romans 2:26
verses.text: If then the uncircumcision keeps the ordinances of the Law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

verses.name: Romans 2:27
verses.text: And the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfills the Law, shall it not judge you, who through letter and circumcision <hi>become</hi> transgressors of the Law?

verses.name: Romans 2:28
verses.text: For he is not a Jew who <hi>is one</hi> outwardly, nor <hi>is</hi> circumcision that outwardly in flesh;

verses.name: Romans 2:29
verses.text: but he <hi>is</hi> a Jew who <hi>is one</hi> inwardly, and circumcision <hi>is</hi> of the heart; in spirit and not in letter; whose praise <hi>is</hi> not from men, but from God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:1
verses.text: Then what <hi>is</hi> the superiority of the Jew? Or what <hi>is</hi> the profit of circumcision?

verses.name: Romans 3:2
verses.text: Much, by every way! Chiefly, indeed, because they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

verses.name: Romans 3:3
verses.text: For what? If some did not believe, will not their unbelief nullify the faith of God?

verses.name: Romans 3:4
verses.text: Let it not be! But let God be true, and every man a liar; as it is written, "That You might be justified in Your sayings, and will overcome when You are judged."

verses.name: Romans 3:5
verses.text: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? <hi>Is</hi> God unrighteous who lays on wrath? (I speak as a man.)

verses.name: Romans 3:6
verses.text: Let it not be! For then how shall God judge the world?

verses.name: Romans 3:7
verses.text: For if in my lie the truth has more abounded to His glory why am I still judged as a sinner?

verses.name: Romans 3:8
verses.text: And not <hi>rather</hi>, (as we are wrongly accused, and as some affirm that we say), Let us do bad things that good may come? <hi>Their</hi> condemnation is just.

verses.name: Romans 3:9
verses.text: What then? Do we excel? No, in no way; for we have before charged both Jews and Greeks all <hi>with</hi> being under sin,

verses.name: Romans 3:10
verses.text: as it is written: "There is none righteous, no not one;

verses.name: Romans 3:11
verses.text: there is none that understands, there is none that seeks after God."

verses.name: Romans 3:12
verses.text: "They are all gone out of the way, <hi>they</hi> have together become unprofitable, there is none that does good, no, not one."

verses.name: Romans 3:13
verses.text: "Their throat <hi>is</hi> an open grave, with their tongues they have used deceit, <hi>the</hi> poison of asps <hi>is</hi> under their lips;

verses.name: Romans 3:14
verses.text: whose mouth <hi>is</hi> full of cursing and bitterness;"

verses.name: Romans 3:15
verses.text: "their feet <hi>are</hi> swift to shed blood;

verses.name: Romans 3:16
verses.text: destruction and misery <hi>are</hi> in their way,

verses.name: Romans 3:17
verses.text: and the way of peace they did not know."

verses.name: Romans 3:18
verses.text: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 3:19
verses.text: But we know that whatever things the Law says, it says to those who are under the Law; so that every mouth may be stopped and all the world may be under judgment before God,

verses.name: Romans 3:20
verses.text: because by the works of the Law none of all flesh will be justified in His sight; for through the Law <hi>is</hi> the knowledge of sin.

verses.name: Romans 3:21
verses.text: But now a righteousness of God has been revealed apart from Law, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets;

verses.name: Romans 3:22
verses.text: even the righteousness of God through the faith of Jesus Christ, toward all and upon all those who believe. For there is no difference,

verses.name: Romans 3:23
verses.text: for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God,

verses.name: Romans 3:24
verses.text: being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus;

verses.name: Romans 3:25
verses.text: whom God has set forth <hi>to be</hi> a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness through the passing by of the sins that had taken place before, in the forbearance of God;

verses.name: Romans 3:26
verses.text: for the display of His righteousness at this time, for Him to be just and, forgiving the <hi>one</hi> being of the faith of Jesus.

verses.name: Romans 3:27
verses.text: Then where <hi>is</hi> the boasting? It is excluded. Through what law? Of works? No, but through the law of faith.

verses.name: Romans 3:28
verses.text: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law.

verses.name: Romans 3:29
verses.text: Or <hi>is He</hi> the God of the Jews only, and not also of the nations? Yes, of the nations also,

verses.name: Romans 3:30
verses.text: since <hi>it is</hi> one God who will justify circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

verses.name: Romans 3:31
verses.text: Do we then make the Law void through faith? Let it not be! But we establish the Law.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:1
verses.text: What then shall we say that our father Abraham has found, according to flesh?

verses.name: Romans 4:2
verses.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a boast; but not before God.

verses.name: Romans 4:3
verses.text: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness."

verses.name: Romans 4:4
verses.text: But to him working, the reward is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt.

verses.name: Romans 4:5
verses.text: But to him not working, but believing on Him justifying the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 4:6
verses.text: Even as David also says of the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works,

verses.name: Romans 4:7
verses.text: <hi> saying</hi>, "Blessed are those whose lawlessnesses are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;

verses.name: Romans 4:8
verses.text: blessed <hi>is</hi> the man to whom <hi>the</hi> Lord will in no way impute sin."  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:9
verses.text: <hi> Is</hi> this blessedness then on the circumcision only, or on the uncircumcision also? For we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 4:10
verses.text: How then was it reckoned? Being in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

verses.name: Romans 4:11
verses.text: And he received a sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith <hi>while still</hi> uncircumcised; so that he might be <hi>the</hi> father of all those believing through uncircumcision, for righteousness to be imputed to them also;

verses.name: Romans 4:12
verses.text: and a father of circumcision to those not of the circumcision only, but also to those walking by the steps of the faith of our father Abraham during uncircumcision.

verses.name: Romans 4:13
verses.text: For the promise that he should be the heir of the world <hi>was</hi> not to Abraham or to his seed through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.

verses.name: Romans 4:14
verses.text: For if they of the Law <hi>are</hi> heirs, faith is made void and the promise is made of no effect;

verses.name: Romans 4:15
verses.text: because the Law works out wrath, for where no law is, <hi>there is</hi> no transgression.

verses.name: Romans 4:16
verses.text: Therefore <hi>it is</hi> of faith so that <hi>it might be</hi> according to grace; for the promise to be made sure to all the seed, not only to that which is of the Law, but to that also which is of <hi>the</hi> faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:17
verses.text: (as it has been written, "I have made you a father of many nations") --before God, whom he believed, who makes the dead live, and calls the things <hi>which</hi> do not exist as <hi>though they</hi> do exist.

verses.name: Romans 4:18
verses.text: <hi> For he</hi> who beyond hope believed on hope for him to become the father of many nations (according to that which was spoken, "So your seed shall be").

verses.name: Romans 4:19
verses.text: And not being weak in faith, he did not consider his own body already dead (being about a hundred years old) or the deadening of Sarah's womb.

verses.name: Romans 4:20
verses.text: He did not stagger at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strong in faith, giving glory to God,

verses.name: Romans 4:21
verses.text: and being fully persuaded that what God had promised, He was also able to perform.

verses.name: Romans 4:22
verses.text: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 4:23
verses.text: Now it was not written for him alone that it was imputed to him,

verses.name: Romans 4:24
verses.text: but for us also to whom it is to be imputed, to the ones believing on Him who has raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;

verses.name: Romans 4:25
verses.text: who was delivered because of our offenses and was raised for our justification.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 5:1
verses.text: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Romans 5:2
verses.text: Through Him we also have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice on the hope of the glory of God.

verses.name: Romans 5:3
verses.text: And not only <hi>this</hi>, but we glory in afflictions also, knowing that afflictions work out patience,

verses.name: Romans 5:4
verses.text: and patience <hi>works out</hi> experience, and experience <hi>works out</hi> hope.

verses.name: Romans 5:5
verses.text: And hope does not make <hi>us</hi> ashamed, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through <hi>the</hi> Holy Spirit given to us.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 5:6
verses.text: For we yet being without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.

verses.name: Romans 5:7
verses.text: For one will with difficulty die for a righteous one, yet perhaps one would even dare to die for a good one.

verses.name: Romans 5:8
verses.text: But God commends His love toward us in that while we were yet sinners Christ died for us.

verses.name: Romans 5:9
verses.text: Much more then, being now justified by His blood, we shall be saved from wrath through Him.

verses.name: Romans 5:10
verses.text: For if <hi>when</hi> we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.

verses.name: Romans 5:11
verses.text: And not only <hi>so</hi>, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the reconciliation.

verses.name: Romans 5:12
verses.text: Therefore, even as through one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed on all men inasmuch as all sinned:

verses.name: Romans 5:13
verses.text: for until the Law sin was in <hi>the</hi> world, but sin is not imputed <hi>when</hi> there is no law.

verses.name: Romans 5:14
verses.text: But death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is the type of Him who was to come;

verses.name: Romans 5:15
verses.text: but the free gift <hi>shall</hi> not <hi>be</hi> also like the offense. For if by the offense of the one many died, much more the grace of God, and the gift in grace; which <hi>is</hi> of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abounded to many.

verses.name: Romans 5:16
verses.text: And the free gift <hi>shall</hi> not <hi>be</hi> as by one having sinned; (for indeed the judgment <hi>was</hi> of one to condemnation, but the free gift <hi>is</hi> of many offenses to justification.

verses.name: Romans 5:17
verses.text: For if by one man's offense death reigned by one, much more they who receive abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by One, Jesus Christ.)

verses.name: Romans 5:18
verses.text: Therefore as by one offense <hi>sentence came</hi> on all men to condemnation, even so by the righteousness of One the free gift <hi>came</hi> to all men to justification of life.

verses.name: Romans 5:19
verses.text: For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of One shall many be made righteous.

verses.name: Romans 5:20
verses.text: But the Law entered so that the offense might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound,

verses.name: Romans 5:21
verses.text: so that as sin has reigned to death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 6:1
verses.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may abound?

verses.name: Romans 6:2
verses.text: Let it not be! How shall we who died to sin live any longer in it?

verses.name: Romans 6:3
verses.text: Do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into His death?

verses.name: Romans 6:4
verses.text: Therefore we were buried with Him by baptism into death, so that as Christ was raised up from <hi>the</hi> dead by the glory of the Father; even so we also should walk in newness of life.

verses.name: Romans 6:5
verses.text: For if we have been joined together in the likeness of His death, we shall also be <hi>in the likeness</hi> of His resurrection;

verses.name: Romans 6:6
verses.text: knowing this, that our old man is crucified with <hi>Him</hi> in order that the body of sin might be destroyed, that from now on we should not serve sin.

verses.name: Romans 6:7
verses.text: For he who died has been justified from sin.

verses.name: Romans 6:8
verses.text: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him,

verses.name: Romans 6:9
verses.text: knowing that when Christ was raised from <hi>the</hi> dead, He dies no more; death no longer has dominion over Him.

verses.name: Romans 6:10
verses.text: For in that He died, He died to sin once; but in that He lives, He lives to God.

verses.name: Romans 6:11
verses.text: Likewise count yourselves also to be truly dead to sin, but alive to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.name: Romans 6:12
verses.text: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.

verses.name: Romans 6:13
verses.text: Do not yield your members <hi>as</hi> instruments of unrighteousness to sin, but yield yourselves to God, as <hi>one</hi> alive from <hi>the</hi> dead, and your members <hi>as</hi> instruments of righteousness to God.

verses.name: Romans 6:14
verses.text: For sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under Law, but under grace.

verses.name: Romans 6:15
verses.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under Law, but under grace? Let it not be!

verses.name: Romans 6:16
verses.text: Do you not know that to whom you yield yourselves <hi>as</hi> slaves for obedience, you are slaves to him whom you obey; whether it is of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 6:17
verses.text: But thanks <hi>be</hi> to our God that you were the slaves of sin, but you have obeyed from <hi>the</hi> heart that form of doctrine to which you were delivered.

verses.name: Romans 6:18
verses.text: Then being made free from sin, you became the slaves of righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 6:19
verses.text: I speak in the manner of men because of the weakness of your flesh; for as you have yielded your members <hi>as</hi> slaves to uncleanness, and to lawless act unto lawless act, even so now yield your members as slaves to righteousness unto holiness.

verses.name: Romans 6:20
verses.text: For when you were the slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.

verses.name: Romans 6:21
verses.text: What fruit did you have then <hi>in those things</hi> of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things <hi>is</hi> death.

verses.name: Romans 6:22
verses.text: But now, being made free from sin, and having become slaves to God, you have your fruit to holiness, and the end everlasting life.

verses.name: Romans 6:23
verses.text: For the wages of sin <hi>is</hi> death, but the gift of God <hi>is</hi> eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:1
verses.text: Or are you ignorant, brothers; for I speak to those who know the Law; that the law has dominion over a man as long as he lives?

verses.name: Romans 7:2
verses.text: For the married woman was bound by law to the living husband. But if the husband is dead, she is set free from the law of <hi>her</hi> husband.

verses.name: Romans 7:3
verses.text: So then <hi>if</hi>, while <hi>her</hi> husband lives, she is married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, <hi>so that</hi> she is no adulteress by becoming another man's wife.

verses.name: Romans 7:4
verses.text: So, my brothers, you also have become dead to the law by the body of Christ so that you should be married to Another, <hi>even</hi> to Him raised from <hi>the</hi> dead, that we should bring forth fruit to God.

verses.name: Romans 7:5
verses.text: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sin worked in our members through the law to bring forth fruit to death.

verses.name: Romans 7:6
verses.text: But now we having been set free from the Law, having died <hi>to that</hi> in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of spirit and not <hi>in</hi> oldness of the letter.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: Romans 7:7
verses.text: What shall we say then? <hi>Is</hi> the law sin? Let it not be said! But I did not know sin except through the law. For also I did not know lust except the law said, You shall not lust.

verses.name: Romans 7:8
verses.text: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, worked in me all kinds of lust. For apart from law sin <hi>was</hi> dead.

verses.name: Romans 7:9
verses.text: For I was alive without the law once. But when the commandment came, sin revived and I died.
