verses.text: So then I run, not as if I were uncertain. And so I fight, not as <hi>one who</hi> beats the air.

verses.name: I Corinthians 9:27
verses.text: But I buffet my body, and lead <hi>it</hi> captive, lest proclaiming to others I myself might be rejected.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:1
verses.text: And, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:2
verses.text: And all were baptized to Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:3
verses.text: and all ate the same spiritual food,

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:4
verses.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank of the spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:5
verses.text: But with many of them God was not well pleased, for they were scattered in the wilderness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:6
verses.text: And these things were our examples, that we should not be lusters after evil, as they also lusted.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:7
verses.text: Nor should we be idolaters, even as some of them, as it is written: "The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play."

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:8
verses.text: Nor let us commit fornication, as some of them fornicated, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:9
verses.text: Nor let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted Him and were destroyed by serpents.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:10
verses.text: Nor murmur as some of them also murmured and were destroyed by the destroyer.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:11
verses.text: And all these things happened to them <hi>as</hi> examples; and <hi>it</hi> is written for our warning on whom the ends of the world have come.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:12
verses.text: So let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:13
verses.text: No temptation has taken you but <hi>what is</hi> common to man; but God <hi>is</hi> faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but with the temptation also will make a way to escape, so that you may be able to bear <hi>it</hi>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:14
verses.text: Therefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:15
verses.text: I speak as to wise men, you judge what I say.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:16
verses.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:17
verses.text: For we, the many, are one bread <hi>and</hi> one body; for we are all partakers of that one bread.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:18
verses.text: Behold Israel after the flesh. Are not those who eat of the sacrifices also partakers of the altar?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:19
verses.text: What then do I say? That the idol is anything, or that an idolatrous sacrifice is anything?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:20
verses.text: But <hi>I say</hi> that the things which the nations sacrifice, <hi>they</hi> sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not desire that you should have fellowship with demons.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:21
verses.text: You cannot drink <hi>the</hi> cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot be partakers of <hi>the</hi> Lord's table and of a table of demons.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:22
verses.text: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:23
verses.text: All things are lawful to me, but not all things profit. All things are lawful to me, but not all things build up.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:24
verses.text: Let no one seek his own, but each one another's.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:25
verses.text: Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, asking no question for conscience' sake;

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:26
verses.text: "for the earth <hi>is</hi> the Lord's, and the fullness of it."

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:27
verses.text: If any of those who do not believe invite you <hi>to a feast</hi>, and if you are disposed to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for conscience' sake.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:28
verses.text: But if anyone says to you, This is slain in sacrifice to idols, do not eat for the sake of him who showed <hi>it</hi>, and for conscience' sake; "for the earth <hi>is</hi> the Lord's, and the fullness of it";

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:29
verses.text: conscience, I say, not your own, but the other's. For why is my liberty judged by another's conscience?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:30
verses.text: For if I by grace am a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that <hi>for</hi> which I give thanks?

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:31
verses.text: Therefore whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:32
verses.text: Give no offense, either to the Jews, or to the Greeks or to the church of God;

verses.name: I Corinthians 10:33
verses.text: even as I please all <hi>men</hi> in all <hi>things</hi>, not seeking my own profit, but the <hi>profit</hi> of many, so that they may be saved.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:1
verses.text: Be imitators of me, even as I also <hi>am</hi> of Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:2
verses.text: But I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and you keep the doctrines as I delivered <hi>them</hi> to you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:3
verses.text: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman <hi>is</hi> the man; and the head of Christ <hi>is</hi> God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:4
verses.text: Every man praying or prophesying with <hi>his</hi> head covered dishonors his Head.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:5
verses.text: But every woman who prays or prophesies with <hi>her</hi> head unveiled dishonors her head; for that is even the same as if she were shaved.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:6
verses.text: For if the woman is not veiled, let her also be shorn. But <hi>if it</hi> is a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be veiled.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:7
verses.text: For a man indeed ought not to have <hi>his</hi> head covered, because he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is <hi>the</hi> glory of <hi>the</hi> man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:8
verses.text: For the man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:9
verses.text: Nor was the man created for the woman, but the woman for the man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:10
verses.text: For this reason the woman ought to have authority on <hi>her</hi> head because of the angels.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:11
verses.text: But neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:12
verses.text: For as the woman <hi>is</hi> of the man, even so the man <hi>is</hi> also by the woman; but all things of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:13
verses.text: Judge among yourselves: is it right that a woman pray to God unveiled?

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:14
verses.text: Does not even nature itself teach you that if man has long hair, it is a shame to him?

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:15
verses.text: But if a woman should have long hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her in place of a veil.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:16
verses.text: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor the churches of God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:17
verses.text: But in enjoining this, I do not praise <hi>you</hi>, because you come together not for the better, but for the worse.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:18
verses.text: For first of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:19
verses.text: For there must also be heresies among you, that the approved ones may be revealed among you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:20
verses.text: Therefore when you come together into one place, <hi>this</hi> is not to eat <hi>the</hi> Lord's supper.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:21
verses.text: For in eating each one takes his own supper first; and one is hungry, and another drunken.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:22
verses.text: For do you not have houses <hi>in which</hi> to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God, and shame those who do not have? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? I do not praise <hi>you</hi>!  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:23
verses.text: For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus in the night in which he was betrayed took bread;

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:24
verses.text: And giving thanks, He broke <hi>it</hi> and said, "Take, eat; this is My body, which is broken for you; this do in remembrance of Me."

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:25
verses.text: In the same way <hi>He took</hi> the cup also, after supping, saying, "This cup is the New Covenant in My blood; as often as you drink it, do this in remembrance of Me."

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:26
verses.text: For "as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you show" the Lord's death until He shall come.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:27
verses.text: So that whoever shall eat this bread and drink <hi>this</hi> cup of the Lord unworthily, he will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:28
verses.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of <hi>that</hi> bread and drink of that cup.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:29
verses.text: For he who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks condemnation to himself, not discerning the Lord's body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:30
verses.text: For this cause many among you <hi>are</hi> weak and sickly, and many sleep.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:31
verses.text: For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:32
verses.text: But when we are judged, we are chastened by <hi>the</hi> Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:33
verses.text: So that, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

verses.name: I Corinthians 11:34
verses.text: But if anyone hungers, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together to condemnation. And the rest I will set in order when I come.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:1
verses.text: Now concerning spiritual <hi>gifts</hi>, brothers, I would not have you ignorant.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:2
verses.text: You know that being led away, you nations were led to dumb idols.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:3
verses.text: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by <hi>the</hi> Spirit of God says Jesus <hi>is</hi> a curse, and <hi>that</hi> no one can say that Jesus <hi>is</hi> Lord, but by the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:4
verses.text: But there are differences of gifts, but the same Spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:5
verses.text: And there are differences of ministries, but the same Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:6
verses.text: And there are differences of workings, but it is the same God working all things in all.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:7
verses.text: But to each one is given the showing forth of the Spirit to <hi>our</hi> profit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:8
verses.text: For through the Spirit is given to one a word of wisdom; and to another a word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:9
verses.text: and to another faith by the same Spirit; and to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit;

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:10
verses.text: and to another workings of powers, to another prophecy; and to another discerning of spirits; and to another kinds of tongues; and to another the interpretation of tongues.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:11
verses.text: But the one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing separately to each one as He desires.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:12
verses.text: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, <hi>are</hi> one body; so also <hi>is</hi> Christ.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:13
verses.text: For also by one Spirit we are all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free, even all were made to drink into one Spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:14
verses.text: For the body is not one member, but many.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:15
verses.text: If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:16
verses.text: And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:17
verses.text: If all the body <hi>were</hi> an eye, where <hi>would be</hi> the hearing? If all hearing, where <hi>would be</hi> the smelling?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:18
verses.text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body as it has pleased Him.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:19
verses.text: And if they were all one member, where <hi>would be</hi> the body?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:20
verses.text: But now indeed many <hi>are</hi> the members, yet only one body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:21
verses.text: And the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you; nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:22
verses.text: But much rather the members of the body seeming to be weaker are necessary.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:23
verses.text: And those <hi>members</hi> of the body which we think to be less honorable, on these we put more abundant honor around <hi>them</hi>. And our unpresentable <hi>members</hi> have more abundant propriety.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:24
verses.text: For our presentable <hi>members</hi> have no need, but God tempered the body together, giving more abundant honor to the <hi>member</hi> having need;

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:25
verses.text: that there not be division in the body, but <hi>that</hi> the members should have the same care for one another.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:26
verses.text: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with <hi>it</hi>; if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice with <hi>it</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:27
verses.text: And you are the body of Christ, and members in part.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:28
verses.text: And God set some in the church, firstly, apostles; secondly, prophets; thirdly, teachers, then works of power, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, kinds of languages.

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:29
verses.text: <hi> Are</hi> all apostles? <hi>Are</hi> all prophets? <hi>Are</hi> all teachers? <hi>Are</hi> all workers of power?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:30
verses.text: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak languages? Do all interpret?

verses.name: I Corinthians 12:31
verses.text: But zealously strive after the better gifts. And yet I show to you a more excellent way.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:1
verses.text: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I have become <hi>as</hi> sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:2
verses.text: And though I have prophecies, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so as to move mountains, and do not have charity, I am nothing.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:3
verses.text: And though I give out all my goods <hi>to feed the poor</hi>, and though I deliver my body to be burned, and have not charity, I am profited nothing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:4
verses.text: Charity has patience, is kind; charity is not envious, is not vain, is not puffed up;

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:5
verses.text: does not behave indecently, does not seek her own, is not easily provoked, thinks no evil.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:6
verses.text: Charity does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices in the truth,

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:7
verses.text: quietly covers all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:8
verses.text: Charity never fails. But if <hi>there are</hi> prophecies, they will be abolished; if tongues, they shall cease; if knowledge, it will be abolished.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:9
verses.text: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:10
verses.text: But when the perfect thing comes, then that which is in part will be caused to cease.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:11
verses.text: When I was an infant, I spoke as an infant, I thought as an infant, I reasoned as an infant. But when I became a man, I did away with the things of an infant.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:12
verses.text: For now we see in a mirror dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall fully know even as I also am fully known.

verses.name: I Corinthians 13:13
verses.text: And now faith, hope, charity, these three remain; but the greatest of these <hi>is</hi> charity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:1
verses.text: Follow after love and desire spiritual <hi>things</hi>, but rather that you may prophesy.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:2
verses.text: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men but to God. For no one hears, but in spirit he speaks mysteries.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:3
verses.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men <hi>for</hi> building up, and exhortation, and comfort.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:4
verses.text: The one speaking in a tongue builds himself up, but he prophesying builds up a church.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:5
verses.text: I wish all of you to speak in languages, but rather that you may prophesy; for greater <hi>is</hi> he prophesying than he speaking in tongues, unless he interpret so that the church may receive building up.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:6
verses.text: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you, except I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in teaching?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:7
verses.text: Yet lifeless things giving a sound, whether flute or harp, if they do not give a distinction in the sound, how will it be known what is being piped or harped?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:8
verses.text: For also if a trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself for the battle?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:9
verses.text: So also you, if you do not give a clear word through the language, how will it be known what <hi>is</hi> being said? For you will be speaking into the air.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:10
verses.text: So it may be many kinds of sounds are in <hi>the</hi> world, and not one <hi>is</hi> without a distinct sound.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:11
verses.text: Therefore if I do not know the power of the sound, I will be a foreigner to him speaking, and he speaking <hi>will be</hi> a foreigner to me.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:12
verses.text: Even so you, since you are zealots of spiritual <hi>things</hi>, seek to build up the church, in order that you may abound

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:13
verses.text: So then he speaking in a language, let him pray that he may interpret.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:14
verses.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:15
verses.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with the mind.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:16
verses.text: Else, if you bless in the spirit, he occupying the place of the unlearned, how will he say the amen at your giving of thanks, since he does not know what you say?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:17
verses.text: For you truly give thanks well, but the other is not built up.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:18
verses.text: I thank my God <hi>that</hi> I speak more languages than all of you;

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:19
verses.text: yet in a church I desire to speak five words with my mind, so that I might also teach others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:20
verses.text: Brothers, do not be children in your minds, but in malice be like infants, and in your minds be mature.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:21
verses.text: In the law it is written, "By other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people, and even so they will not hear Me, says the Lord."

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:22
verses.text: So that tongues are not a sign to those who believe, but to those who do not believe. But prophesying <hi>is</hi> not to those who do not believe, but to those who believe.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:23
verses.text: Therefore if the whole church has come together, and all speak in languages, and if uninstructed ones or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you rave?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:24
verses.text: But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or one not instructed comes, he is convicted by all, he is judged by all.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:25
verses.text: And so the secrets of his heart become revealed. And so, falling down on <hi>his</hi> face, he will worship God and report that God is truly among you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:26
verses.text: Then how is it, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be for building up.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:27
verses.text: If one speaks in a language, <hi>let it be</hi> by two, or <hi>at</hi> the most three, and in succession. And let one interpret.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:28
verses.text: But if there is no interpreter, let him be silent in a church; and let him speak to himself and to God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:29
verses.text: And <hi>if there are</hi> two or three prophets, let them speak, and let the others judge.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:30
verses.text: If <hi>a revelation</hi> is revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:31
verses.text: For you may all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be comforted.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:32
verses.text: And the spirits of the prophets <hi>are</hi> subject to the prophets.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:33
verses.text: For God is not <hi>the author</hi> of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:34
verses.text: Let your women be silent in the churches; for it is not permitted to them to speak, but to be in subjection, as the Law also says.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:35
verses.text: And if they desire to learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home; for it is a shame for a woman to speak in a church.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:36
verses.text: Or did the Word of God go out from you? Or did it reach only to you?

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:37
verses.text: If anyone thinks to be a prophet, or a spiritual one, let him recognize the things I write to you, that they are a commandment of the Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:38
verses.text: But if any is ignorant, let him be ignorant.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:39
verses.text: So then, brothers, seek to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak in languages.

verses.name: I Corinthians 14:40
verses.text: Let all things be done decently and in order.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:1
verses.text: And, brothers, I declare to you the gospel which I preached to you, which also you have received, and in which you stand;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:2
verses.text: by which you also are being kept safe, if you hold fast the word which I preached to you, unless you believed in vain.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:3
verses.text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received, that Christ died for our sins, according to the Scriptures,

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:4
verses.text: and that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:5
verses.text: and that He was seen by Cephas, then by the Twelve.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:6
verses.text: Afterward He was seen by over five hundred brothers at once, of whom the greater part remain until this present day, but also some fell asleep.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:7
verses.text: Afterward He was seen by James, then by all the apostles.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:8
verses.text: And last of all He was seen by me also, as one born out of time.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:9
verses.text: For I am the least of the apostles and am not sufficient to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:10
verses.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace which <hi>was</hi> toward me has not been without fruit, but I labored more abundantly than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God with me.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:11
verses.text: Therefore whether <hi>it was</hi> I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:12
verses.text: But if Christ is proclaimed, that He was raised from <hi>the</hi> dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:13
verses.text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:14
verses.text: And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation <hi>is</hi> worthless, and your faith <hi>is</hi> also worthless.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:15
verses.text: And we are also found <hi>to be</hi> false witnesses of God, because we testified of God that He raised Christ; whom He did not raise if the dead are not raised.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:16
verses.text: For if <hi>the</hi> dead are not raised, then Christ is not raised.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:17
verses.text: And if Christ is not raised, your faith <hi>is</hi> foolish; you are yet in your sins.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:18
verses.text: Then also those that fell asleep in Christ were lost.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:19
verses.text: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:20
verses.text: But now Christ has risen from <hi>the</hi> dead, <hi>and</hi> has become the firstfruit of those who slept.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:21
verses.text: For since death <hi>is</hi> through man, the resurrection of <hi>the</hi> dead also <hi>is</hi> through a Man.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:22
verses.text: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ all will be made alive.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:23
verses.text: But each in <hi>his</hi> own order: Christ the first-fruit, and afterward they who are Christ's at His coming;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:24
verses.text: then <hi>is</hi> the end, when He delivers the kingdom to God, even the Father; when He makes to cease all rule and all authority and power.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:25
verses.text: for it is right for Him to reign until He has put all the enemies under His feet.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:26
verses.text: The last enemy made to cease <hi>is</hi> death.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:27
verses.text: For He put all things under His feet. But when He says that all things have been put under <hi>His feet</hi>, it is plain that <hi>it</hi> excepts Him who has put all things under Him.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:28
verses.text: But when all things are subjected to Him, then the Son Himself also will be subject to Him who has subjected things to Him, so that God may be all things in all.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:29
verses.text: Otherwise, what will they do, those being baptized on behalf of <hi>the</hi> dead? If the dead are not at all raised, why indeed are they baptized on behalf of <hi>the</hi> dead?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:30
verses.text: And why are we also in danger every hour?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:31
verses.text: Day by day I die, by your rejoicing, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:32
verses.text: If according to man I fought with beasts in Ephesus, what advantage is to me if <hi>the</hi> dead are not raised? "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:33
verses.text: Do not be deceived, evil companionships corrupt good habits.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:34
verses.text: Be righteously awake, and sin not; for some have ignorance of God. I speak <hi>this</hi> to your shame.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:35
verses.text: But someone will say, How are the dead raised up, and with what body do they come?

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:36
verses.text: Foolish one! What you sow is not made alive unless it dies.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:37
verses.text: And what you sow, you do not sow the body that <hi>is</hi> going to be, but a bare grain (perhaps of wheat or of some of the rest).

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:38
verses.text: And God gives it a body as it has pleased Him, and to each of the seeds its own body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:39
verses.text: All flesh <hi>is</hi> not the same flesh; but one <hi>kind of</hi> flesh of men, and another flesh of beasts, and another of fish, and another of birds.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:40
verses.text: <hi> There are</hi> also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the glory of the heavenly <hi>is</hi> truly different, and that of the earthly different;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:41
verses.text: one glory of <hi>the</hi> sun, and another glory of <hi>the</hi> moon, and another glory of <hi>the</hi> stars; for <hi>one</hi> star differs from <hi>another</hi> star in glory.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:42
verses.text: So also the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:43
verses.text: it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:44
verses.text: it is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:45
verses.text: And so it is written, "The first man, Adam, <hi>was made</hi> a living soul," the last Adam was a life-giving Spirit.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:46
verses.text: But not the spiritual first, but the natural; afterward the spiritual.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:47
verses.text: The first man <hi>was</hi> out of earth, earthy; the second Man <hi>was</hi> the Lord from Heaven.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:48
verses.text: Such the earthy <hi>man</hi>, such also the earthy ones. And such the heavenly <hi>Man</hi>, such also the heavenly ones.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:49
verses.text: And according as we bore the image of the earthy <hi>man</hi>, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly <hi>Man</hi>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:50
verses.text: And I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit <hi>the</hi> kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:51
verses.text: Behold, I speak a mystery to you; we shall not all fall asleep, but we shall all be changed;

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:52
verses.text: in a moment, in a glance of an eye, at the last trumpet. For a trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall all be changed.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:53
verses.text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal <hi>must</hi> put on immortality.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:54
verses.text: But when this corruptible shall put on incorruption, and when this mortal shall put on immortality, then will take place the word that is written, "Death is swallowed up in victory.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:55
verses.text: O death, where <hi>is</hi> your sting? O grave, where <hi>is</hi> your victory?"

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:56
verses.text: The sting of death <hi>is</hi> sin, and the strength of sin <hi>is</hi> the law.

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:57
verses.text: But thanks <hi>be</hi> to God who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 15:58
verses.text: So that, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not without fruit in the Lord.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:1
verses.text: And concerning the collection for the saints, as I charged the churches of Galatia, so also you do.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:2
verses.text: On the first <hi>day</hi> of the week let each of you put by himself, storing up what ever he is prospered, so that there may be no collections when I come.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:3
verses.text: And when I come, whomever you shall approve by <hi>your</hi> letters, I will send them to bring your gift to Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:4
verses.text: And if it is suitable for me to go also, they shall go with me.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:5
verses.text: But I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia; for I am going through Macedonia.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:6
verses.text: And it may be that I will stay with you, and even spend the winter with you, so that you may set me forward wherever I go.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:7
verses.text: For I do not desire to see you now in passage, but I am hoping to stay some time with you, if the Lord permits.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:8
verses.text: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:9
verses.text: For a great and effective door opened to me, and many <hi>are</hi> opposing.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:10
verses.text: But if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he works the work of the Lord, even as I <hi>do</hi>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:11
verses.text: Therefore let not any despise him, but set him forward in peace, so that he may come to me; for I am waiting for him with the brothers.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:12
verses.text: As regards <hi>our</hi> brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not altogether <hi>his</hi> will that he come now. But he will come when he has opportunity.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:13
verses.text: Watch! Stand fast in the faith! Be men! Be strong!

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:14
verses.text: Let all your things be done in charity.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:15
verses.text: But I exhort you, brothers. You know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruit of Achaia, and they appointed themselves to ministry to the saints.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:16
verses.text: See that you also submit to such ones, and to everyone working and laboring with <hi>me</hi>.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:17
verses.text: I am glad at the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus; for these supplied your lack.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:18
verses.text: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours; then acknowledge such ones.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:19
verses.text: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in <hi>the</hi> Lord, with the church that is in their house.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:20
verses.text: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:21
verses.text: The salutation of Paul with my own hand.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:22
verses.text: If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. The Lord comes!

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:23
verses.text: May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ <hi>be</hi> with you.

verses.name: I Corinthians 16:24
verses.text: Let my love <hi>be</hi> with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:1
verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy <hi>our</hi> brother, to the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in all Achaia.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:2
verses.text: Grace <hi>be</hi> unto you, and peace from God our Father and <hi>from the</hi> Lord Jesus Christ.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:3
verses.text: Blessed <hi>be</hi> God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:4
verses.text: He comforting us in all our trouble, so that we may be able to comfort those who are in every trouble, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:5
verses.text: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also abounds by Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:6
verses.text: And if we are troubled, <hi>it is</hi> for your consolation and salvation, being worked out in <hi>the</hi> endurance of the same sufferings which we also suffer; if we are comforted, <hi>it is</hi> for your consolation and salvation.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:7
verses.text: And our hope of you <hi>is</hi> certain, knowing that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so also of the consolation.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:8
verses.text: For, brothers, we would not have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength; so much so that we despaired even of life.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:9
verses.text: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, so that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead;

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:10
verses.text: who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver; in whom we trust that He will yet deliver <hi>us</hi>,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:11
verses.text: with you also helping together by prayer for us, so that the gracious gift by many persons be <hi>the cause of</hi> thanksgiving through many for us.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:12
verses.text: For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity; not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God; we have had our conduct in the world, and more abundantly toward you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:13
verses.text: For we write no other things to you than what you read or recognize, and I trust you shall recognize them even to the end,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:14
verses.text: even as you have recognized us <hi>in</hi> part, that we are your rejoicing, even as you also <hi>are</hi> ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:15
verses.text: And in this confidence I intended to come to you before, so that you might have a second benefit,

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:16
verses.text: and to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia to you, and to be brought on my way toward Judea by you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:17
verses.text: Then purposing this, did I indeed use lightness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose them according to the flesh, so that with me there should be yes, yes, and no, no?

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:18
verses.text: But <hi>as</hi> God <hi>is</hi> true, our word toward you was not yes and no.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:19
verses.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us; by me and Silas and Timothy; was not yes and no, but in Him was, yes!

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:20
verses.text: For all the promises of God in Him <hi>are</hi> yes, and in Him Amen, to the glory of God by us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:21
verses.text: But He confirming us and anointing us with you in Christ <hi>is</hi> God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:22
verses.text: And He has sealed us and having given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:23
verses.text: And I call God <hi>as</hi> witness to my soul that in order to spare you I have not yet come to Corinth.

verses.name: II Corinthians 1:24
verses.text: Not that we have dominion over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy; for by faith you stand.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:1
verses.text: But I determined this within myself, that I would not come to you again in grief.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:2
verses.text: For if I make you sorry, who then is he who makes me glad, but the same who has been made sorry by me?

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:3
verses.text: And I wrote this to you, lest when I came I should have sorrow from the <hi>ones</hi> of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is <hi>the joy</hi> of you all.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:4
verses.text: For out of much trouble and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be grieved, but that you might know the love which I have more abundantly to you.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:5
verses.text: But if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me, except in part; so that I not overbear all of you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:6
verses.text: This punishment by the majority <hi>is</hi> enough for such a one;

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:7
verses.text: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive and comfort <hi>him</hi>, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overwhelming sorrow.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:8
verses.text: So I beseech you to confirm <hi>your</hi> love toward him.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:9
verses.text: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:10
verses.text: But to whom you forgive anything, I also <hi>forgive</hi>. For if I forgave anything, for your sakes I forgave <hi>it</hi> to him in the person of Christ;

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:11
verses.text: so that we should not be overreached by Satan, for we are not ignorant of his devices.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:12
verses.text: And, when I came to Troas to <hi>preach</hi> Christ's gospel, and a door was opened to me by <hi>the</hi> Lord,

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:13
verses.text: I had no rest in my spirit because I did not find Titus my brother. But taking my leave of them, I went from there into Macedonia.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:14
verses.text: Now thanks <hi>be</hi> to God, who always causes us to triumph in Christ, and He revealing through us the odor of the knowledge of Him in every place.

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:15
verses.text: For we are to God a sweet savor of Christ, in those being saved, and in those being lost;

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:16
verses.text: to the one <hi>we are</hi> the savor of death to death, and to the other we are the savor of life to life. And who is sufficient for these things?

verses.name: II Corinthians 2:17
verses.text: For we are not as many, hawking the Word of God; but as of sincerity, but as of God. We speak in Christ in the sight of God.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:1
verses.text: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, like some, epistles of commendation to you, or <hi>letters</hi> of commendation from you?

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:2
verses.text: You are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read by all men,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:3
verses.text: <hi> it</hi> having been made plain that you are the epistle of Christ, ministered by us, not having been written with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not on tablets of stone, but in fleshly tablets of <hi>the</hi> heart.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:4
verses.text: And we have such trust through Christ toward God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:5
verses.text: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our sufficiency <hi>is</hi> of God;  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:6
verses.text: who also has made us able ministers of the new covenant; not of the letter, but of the spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:7
verses.text: But if the ministry of death, having been engraved in letters in stone was with glory (so that the sons of Israel could not steadfastly behold the face of Moses because of the glory of his face), which ministry was to be done away;

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:8
verses.text: shall not the ministry of the Spirit be with more glory?

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:9
verses.text: For if the ministry of condemnation <hi>is</hi> glorious, much more does the ministry of righteousness exceed in glory.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:10
verses.text: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, because of the glory that excels.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:11
verses.text: For if that which has been done away <hi>was</hi> glorious, much more that which remains <hi>is</hi> glorious.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:12
verses.text: Then since we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:13
verses.text: And we are not like Moses, <hi>who</hi> put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel could not steadfastly look to the end of the thing being done away.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:14
verses.text: (But their thoughts were blinded; for until the present the same veil remains on the reading of the old covenant, not taken away.) But this veil has been done away in Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:15
verses.text: But until this day, when Moses is read, the veil is on their heart.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:16
verses.text: But whenever it turns to <hi>the</hi> Lord, the veil shall be taken away.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:17
verses.text: And the Lord <hi>is</hi> that Spirit; and where the Spirit of <hi>the</hi> Lord <hi>is</hi>, there <hi>is</hi> liberty.

verses.name: II Corinthians 3:18
verses.text: But we all, with <hi>our</hi> face having been unveiled, having beheld the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Lord Spirit.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:1
verses.text: Therefore since we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we do not faint.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:2
verses.text: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the Word of God, but <hi>by</hi> the revelation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:3
verses.text: But also if our gospel is hidden, it is hidden to those being lost,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:4
verses.text: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving ones, so that the light of the glorious gospel of Christ (who is the image of God) should not dawn on them.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:5
verses.text: For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:6
verses.text: For <hi>it is</hi> God who said, "Out of darkness Light shall shine;" who shone in our hearts to <hi>give</hi> the brightness of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:7
verses.text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excellence of the power may be of God and not of us;  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:8
verses.text: in every <hi>way</hi> having been troubled, but not having been hemmed in; having been perplexed, but not utterly at a loss;

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:9
verses.text: having been persecuted, but not having been forsaken; having been thrown down, but not having been destroyed;

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:10
verses.text: always bearing about the dying of the Lord Jesus in the body, so that the life of Jesus also might be revealed in our body.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:11
verses.text: For we who live are always being delivered to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus might also be revealed in our body.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:12
verses.text: So then death works in us, but life in you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:13
verses.text: For we, having the same spirit of faith (according as it is written, "I believed, and therefore I have spoken"); we also believed and therefore speak,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:14
verses.text: knowing that He who raised up the Lord Jesus shall also raise us up by Jesus, and shall present <hi>us</hi> with you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:15
verses.text: For all things <hi>are</hi> for your sake, so that the superabounding grace might be made to abound through the thanksgiving of the greater number, to the glory of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:16
verses.text: For this cause we do not faint; but though our outward man perishes, yet the inward <hi>man</hi> is being renewed day by day.

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:17
verses.text: For the lightness of our present affliction works out for us a far more excellent eternal weight of glory,

verses.name: II Corinthians 4:18
verses.text: we not considering the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen; for the things which <hi>are</hi> seen <hi>are</hi> not lasting, but the things which <hi>are</hi> not seen <hi>are</hi> everlasting.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:1
verses.text: For we know that if our earthly house of <hi>this</hi> tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:2
verses.text: For indeed in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed with our dwelling-place out of Heaven;

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:3
verses.text: if indeed <hi>in</hi> being clothed, we shall not be found naked.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:4
verses.text: For we who are in <hi>this</hi> tabernacle groan, being burdened; inasmuch as we do not wish to be unclothed, but to be clothed, so that the mortal might be swallowed up by the life.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:5
verses.text: And He who has worked in us for this same thing <hi>is</hi> God, who also <hi>is</hi> giving to us the earnest of the Spirit.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:6
verses.text: Then being always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are away from home from the Lord;

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:7
verses.text: for we walk by faith, not by sight;

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:8
verses.text: then we are confident and we are pleased rather to go away from home out of the body, and to come home to the Lord.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:9
verses.text: Therefore we are also laboring to be well-pleasing to Him, whether at home or away from home.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:10
verses.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive the things <hi>done</hi> in his body, according to that which he has done, whether good or bad.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:11
verses.text: Therefore, knowing the terror of the Lord, we persuade men. But we are revealed to God, and I trust also that we are revealed in your consciences.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:12
verses.text: For we do not commend ourselves again to you, but are giving you occasion to glory on our behalf, so that you may have <hi>it</hi> to <hi>answer those</hi> boasting in appearance, and not in heart.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:13
verses.text: For if we are out of our mind, <hi>it is</hi> to God; or <hi>if</hi> we are in our senses, <hi>it is</hi> for you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:14
verses.text: For the love of Christ constrains us, judging this, that if one died for all, then all died;

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:15
verses.text: and He died for all, that the living ones may live no more to themselves, but to Him who died for them having been raised.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:16
verses.text: So as we now know no one according to flesh, but even if we have known Christ according to flesh, yet now we no longer know <hi>Him</hi> so.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:17
verses.text: So that if any one <hi>is</hi> in Christ, <hi>that one is</hi> a new creature; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:18
verses.text: And all things <hi>are</hi> of God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and has given to us the ministry of reconciliation;

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:19
verses.text: whereas God was in Christ reconciling <hi>the</hi> world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses to them, and putting the word of reconciliation in us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:20
verses.text: Then we are ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as God exhorting through us, we beseech <hi>you</hi> on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 5:21
verses.text: For He has made Him who knew no sin, <hi>to be</hi> sin for us, that we might become <hi>the</hi> righteousness of God in Him.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:1
verses.text: But working together, we also call on you not to receive the grace of God in vain.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:2
verses.text: (For He says, "In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation, I helped you;" Behold, now <hi>is</hi> the accepted time. Behold, now <hi>is</hi> the day of salvation.)

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:3
verses.text: <hi> We are</hi> in nothing giving cause of stumbling, in no way, so that the ministry may not be blamed,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:4
verses.text: but in everything commending ourselves as God's servants, in much patience, in troubles, in emergencies, in distresses,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:5
verses.text: in stripes, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:6
verses.text: in pureness, in knowledge, in long-suffering, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love unfeigned,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:7
verses.text: in <hi>the</hi> word of truth, in <hi>the</hi> power of God, through the weapons of righteousness on the right <hi>hand</hi> and on the left,

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:8
verses.text: through glory and dishonor, through evil report and good report; as deceivers and <hi>yet</hi> true;

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:9
verses.text: as unknown and <hi>yet</hi> well known; as dying and, behold, we live; as chastened and not killed;

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:10
verses.text: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, <hi>yet</hi> possessing all things.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:11
verses.text: O Corinthians, our mouth is opened to you, our heart has been enlarged.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:12
verses.text: You are not restrained in us, but you are restrained in your own affections.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:13
verses.text: But for the same reward, (I speak as to children), you also be enlarged.

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:14
verses.text: Do not be unequally yoked together <hi>with</hi> unbelievers; for what fellowship does righteousness <hi>have</hi> with lawlessness? And what partnership does light <hi>have</hi> with darkness?

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:15
verses.text: And what agreement does Christ <hi>have</hi> with Belial? Or what part does a believer <hi>have</hi> with an unbeliever?

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:16
verses.text: And what agreement does a temple of God <hi>have</hi> with idols? For you are the temple of <hi>the</hi> living God, as God has said, "I will dwell in them and walk among <hi>them</hi>; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people."

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:17
verses.text: Therefore come out from among them and be separated, says the Lord, and do not touch the unclean <hi>thing</hi>. And I will receive you

verses.name: II Corinthians 6:18
verses.text: and I will be a Father to you, and you shall be My sons and daughters, says <hi>the</hi> Lord Almighty.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:1
verses.text: Then having these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilements of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:2
verses.text: Make room for us. We wronged no one, we corrupted no one, we overreached no one.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:3
verses.text: I do not speak <hi>this</hi> to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts for <hi>us</hi> to die together, and to live together.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:4
verses.text: My boldness of speech <hi>is</hi> great toward you; my glorying on your behalf <hi>is</hi> much. I have been filled with comfort, I am overflowing with joy on all our trouble.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:5
verses.text: For, indeed, coming into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but being troubled in every way, <hi>with</hi> fightings <hi>on the</hi> outside, and fears <hi>on the</hi> inside.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:6
verses.text: But He who comforts the lowly comforted us by the coming of Titus.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:7
verses.text: And not only by his coming, but by the comfort with which he was comforted over you, telling us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced the more.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:8
verses.text: For even if I grieved you in the letter, I do not regret; if indeed I did regret; for I see that that letter grieved you for an hour.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:9
verses.text: Now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you grieved to repentance. For you were grieved according to God, so that you might suffer loss by nothing in us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:10
verses.text: For the grief according to God works repentance to salvation, not to be regretted, but the grief of the world works out death.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:11
verses.text: For behold this same thing (you being grieved according to God); how much it worked out earnestness in you; but <hi>also</hi> defense; but <hi>also</hi> indignation; but <hi>also</hi> fear; but <hi>also</hi> desire; but <hi>also</hi> zeal; but <hi>also</hi> vengeance! In everything you approved yourselves to be clear in the matter.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:12
verses.text: Then, though I wrote to you, <hi>it was</hi> not on account of the one who did wrong, nor on account of the one who suffered wrong, but for the sake of revealing our earnestness on your behalf, for you before God.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:13
verses.text: Therefore we have been comforted in your comfort, and we rather rejoiced more abundantly over the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:14
verses.text: For if I have boasted anything about you to him, I was not ashamed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, even so our boasting as to Titus became truth.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:15
verses.text: And his tender feelings are more abundant toward you, remembering the obedience of you all, as you received him with fear and trembling.

verses.name: II Corinthians 7:16
verses.text: Therefore I rejoice that I have confidence in you in everything.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:1
verses.text: And, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given among the churches of Macedonia;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:2
verses.text: that in much testing of trouble, the overflowing of their joy, and the depth of their poverty, abounded to the riches of their generosity.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:3
verses.text: For I testify <hi>that</hi> according to <hi>their</hi> ability, and beyond their ability; <hi>they</hi> gave willingly;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:4
verses.text: with much beseeching, begging us <hi>that they might</hi> receive of us the grace and the fellowship of the ministry to the saints.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:5
verses.text: And not as we hoped, but first <hi>they</hi> gave themselves to the Lord, and to us through <hi>the</hi> will of God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:6
verses.text: for us to call on Titus, that even as he began before, so he would also complete this grace to you also.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:7
verses.text: But even as you abound in everything, in faith, and in word, and in knowledge, and in all earnestness, and in your love to us; you should abound in this grace also.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:8
verses.text: I do not speak according to command, but through the eagerness of others, and testing the trueness of your love.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:9
verses.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though He was rich, for your sakes He became poor, in order that you might be made rich through His poverty.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:10
verses.text: And in this I give <hi>my</hi> judgment; for this is profitable for you, who began before, not only to do, but also to be willing a year ago.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:11
verses.text: But now also finish the doing <hi>of it</hi>, so that, as <hi>there was</hi> a readiness to will, so also the finishing, <hi>giving</hi> out of <hi>what</hi> you have.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:12
verses.text: For if the eagerness is present, <hi>it is</hi> acceptable according to <hi>what</hi> one has, <hi>and</hi> not according to <hi>what</hi> one does not have.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:13
verses.text: For <hi>it is</hi> not that others may <hi>have</hi> ease, but you trouble;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:14
verses.text: but by equality in the present time; your abundance for their need, that their abundance also may be for your need; so that there may be equality;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:15
verses.text: as it is written, "He <hi>gathering</hi> much, he had nothing left over; and he <hi>gathering</hi> little did not have less."  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:16
verses.text: But thanks <hi>be</hi> to God, who put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:17
verses.text: For indeed he accepted the entreaty. But being more earnest, of his own accord he went to you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:18
verses.text: And we have sent with him the brothers whose praise <hi>is</hi> in the gospel throughout all the churches;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:19
verses.text: and not only <hi>so</hi>, but also he having been chosen by the churches to travel with us with this gift, which is administered by us to the glory of the Lord Himself, and <hi>as a witness of</hi> your eager mind;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:20
verses.text: avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us;

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:21
verses.text: providing for honest things, not only before <hi>the</hi> Lord, but also before men.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:22
verses.text: And we have sent with them our brother whom we have often proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest by the great confidence which <hi>I have</hi> in you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:23
verses.text: If anyone inquires of Titus, <hi>he is</hi> my partner and fellow-worker for you, or <hi>of</hi> our brothers, <hi>they are</hi> the messengers of the churches, <hi>the</hi> glory of Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 8:24
verses.text: Therefore show them a proof of your love and of our boasting toward you in the presence of the churches.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:1
verses.text: For indeed regarding the ministry to the saints, it is not necessary for me to write to you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:2
verses.text: For I know your eagerness, of which I boast to Macedonia on your behalf, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal has aroused the greater number.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:3
verses.text: Yet I sent the brothers, lest our boasting (which <hi>is</hi> on your behalf) should not be in vain, that, as I said, you may be ready.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:4
verses.text: <hi> I say this</hi> lest perhaps Macedonians should come with me and find you unprepared. We (not to say you) would then be put to shame in this confident boasting.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:5
verses.text: Therefore I thought <hi>it</hi> necessary to exhort the brothers that they would go forward to you, and make up beforehand your blessing, it having been promised that this would be ready, thus as <hi>a matter of</hi> blessing, and not as of covetousness.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:6
verses.text: But <hi>I say</hi> this, He who sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully shall also reap bountifully.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:7
verses.text: Each one, as he purposes in his heart, <hi>let him give</hi>; not of grief, or of necessity, for God loves a cheerful giver.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:8
verses.text: And God <hi>is</hi> able to make all grace abound toward you, that in everything, always having all self-sufficiency, you may abound to every good work;

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:9
verses.text: As it is written, "He scattered; he has given to the poor; his righteousness remains forever."

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:10
verses.text: Now He who supplies seed to the sower, and bread for eating, may He supply and multiply your seed, and increase the fruits of your righteousness

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:11
verses.text: you being enriched in everything to all generosity, which works out thanksgiving to God through us.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:12
verses.text: For the ministry of this service not only supplies the things lacking of the saints, but also multiplying through many thanksgivings to God,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:13
verses.text: through the proof of this ministry <hi>they</hi> glorify God for your freely expressed submission to the gospel of Christ, and the generosity of the fellowship toward them and toward all,

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:14
verses.text: and <hi>in</hi> their prayer for you, who long after you, because of the exceeding grace of God on you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 9:15
verses.text: Thanks <hi>be</hi> to God for His unspeakable free gift.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:1
verses.text: And I myself, Paul, beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ; I, who indeed to look upon <hi>am</hi> lowly among you, but being absent am bold toward you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:2
verses.text: But I ask, not being present, that I may be bold with the confidence which I think to be daring against some, who thought <hi>of</hi> us as walking according to flesh.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:3
verses.text: For though walking about in flesh, we do not war according to flesh.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:4
verses.text: For the weapons of our warfare <hi>are</hi> not fleshly, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds,

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:5
verses.text: pulling down imaginations and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought into the obedience of Christ;

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:6
verses.text: and having readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:7
verses.text: Do you look at things according to appearance? If anyone has persuaded himself that he <hi>is</hi> Christ's, let him think this again as to himself, that as he <hi>is</hi> Christ's, even so we <hi>are</hi> Christ's.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:8
verses.text: For even if I also should boast somewhat more fully of our authority (which the Lord has given us for building up, and not for pulling you down) I will not be put to shame;

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:9
verses.text: so that I might not seem to terrify you by letters.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:10
verses.text: For indeed they say, the letters <hi>are</hi> weighty and powerful, but the bodily presence <hi>is</hi> weak, and his speech is contemptible.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:11
verses.text: Let such a one think this, that, such as we <hi>are</hi> in word by letters, being absent, such <hi>we will be</hi> also in deed when we are present.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:12
verses.text: For we do not dare to rank or compare ourselves with some of the ones commending themselves. But they, measuring themselves among themselves, and comparing themselves to themselves, are not perceptive.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:13
verses.text: But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule which the God of measure distributed to us, to reach even to you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:14
verses.text: For we do not overstretch ourselves as <hi>though</hi> not reaching to you. For we also came to you in the gospel of Christ;

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:15
verses.text: not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, but having hope that the growing faith among you will be increased according to our rule, to overflowing;

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:16
verses.text: to preach the gospel in that beyond you, and not to boast in another's rule in things made ready.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:17
verses.text: But he who glories, let him glory in <hi>the</hi> Lord.

verses.name: II Corinthians 10:18
verses.text: For not he who commends himself is approved, but he whom the Lord commends.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:1
verses.text: I would that you were bearing with me a little in foolishness; but indeed bear with me.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:2
verses.text: For I am jealous <hi>over</hi> you with godly jealousy. For I have espoused you to one Man, to present <hi>you as</hi> a pure virgin to Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:3
verses.text: But I fear lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve in his craftiness, so your thoughts should be corrupted from the simplicity due to Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:4
verses.text: For if, indeed, the <hi>one</hi> coming proclaims another Jesus, whom we have not proclaimed, or <hi>if</hi> you receive another spirit, which you did not receive, or another gospel, which you never accepted, you might well endure <hi> these</hi>.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:5
verses.text: For I judge <hi>myself</hi> to have come behind the highest apostles <hi>in</hi> nothing.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:6
verses.text: But even if <hi>I am</hi> unskilled in speech, yet not in knowledge; but in every way <hi>I</hi> have been clearly revealed to you in all things.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:7
verses.text: Or did I commit sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you without charge?

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:8
verses.text: I stripped other churches, taking wages for the serving of you.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:9
verses.text: And being present with you, and in need, I was not a burden to anyone. For the brothers from Macedonia made up completely my need. And in every way I have kept myself from being burdensome <hi>to you</hi>, and I will keep myself.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:10
verses.text: The truth of Christ is in me that this boasting shall not be silenced in me in the regions of Achaia.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:11
verses.text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:12
verses.text: But what I do, that I will do, so that I may cut off occasion from those who desire occasion; so that in the thing in which they boast, they may be found even as we.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:13
verses.text: For such ones <hi>are</hi> false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:14
verses.text: Did not even Satan marvelously transform himself into an angel of light?

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:15
verses.text: Therefore <hi>it is</hi> no great thing if his ministers also transform themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:16
verses.text: Again I say, Let no one think me foolish. If otherwise, yet receive me as foolish, so that I may also boast a little.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:17
verses.text: What I speak, I do not speak according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this boldness of boasting.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:18
verses.text: Since many glory according to the flesh, I also will boast.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:19
verses.text: For you gladly bear with fools, being wise.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:20
verses.text: For you endure if anyone enslaves you, if anyone devours, if anyone takes <hi>from you</hi>, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you in the face.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:21
verses.text: I speak according to dishonor, as though we have been weak. But in whatever anyone dares (I speak foolishly), I also dare.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/> <lb type="x-begin-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:22
verses.text: Are they Hebrews? I also! Are they Israelites? I also! Are they the seed of Abraham? I also!

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:23
verses.text: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as beside myself,) I <hi>am</hi> more! <hi>I have been</hi> in labors more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in prisons more, in deaths many times.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:24
verses.text: Five times from the Jews I received forty <hi>stripes</hi> minus one.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:25
verses.text: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I have spent a night and a day in the deep.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:26
verses.text: I have been in travels often; in dangers from waters; in dangers from robbers; in dangers from <hi>my</hi> race; in dangers from <hi>the</hi> heathen; in dangers in <hi>the</hi> city; in dangers in <hi>the</hi> wilderness; in dangers on <hi>the</hi> sea; in dangers among false brothers.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:27
verses.text: <hi> I have been</hi> in hardship and toil; often in watchings; in hunger and thirst; often in fastings; in cold and nakedness;

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:28
verses.text: besides the things outside conspiring against me daily, the care of all the churches.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:29
verses.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I do not burn?

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:30
verses.text: If it is right to boast, I will boast, I will boast <hi>of</hi> the things of my weakness.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:31
verses.text: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I do not lie.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:32
verses.text: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king guarded the city of <hi>the</hi> Damascenes, desiring to lay hold of me.

verses.name: II Corinthians 11:33
verses.text: And I was let down in a basket through a window through the wall, and escaped their hands.  <lb type="x-end-paragraph"/>

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:1
verses.text: Indeed, it is not profitable for me to boast. For I will come to visions and revelations of <hi>the</hi> Lord.

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:2
verses.text: I know a man in Christ fourteen years before (whether in <hi>the</hi> body, I do not know; or outside of <hi>the</hi> body, I do not know; God knows) such a one <hi>was</hi> caught up to <hi>the</hi> third Heaven.

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:3
verses.text: And I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I do not know; God knows),

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:4
verses.text: that he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not allowed for a man to utter.

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:5
verses.text: I will glory of such a one, yet I will not boast on my behalf, except in my weaknesses.

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:6
verses.text: For if I desire to boast, I shall not be foolish. For I will speak the truth. But I spare, lest anyone should think of me as <hi>being</hi> beyond what he sees me, or hears of me;

verses.name: II Corinthians 12:7
